IT & Technology – Yerevan is a growing tech hub, nicknamed the 'Silicon Mountain'.
Agriculture – Apricots (the best in the world), grapes, pomegranates, and walnuts.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Armenian is the official language, with its own unique alphabet created in 405 AD by Mesrop Mashtots.
The Armenian diaspora (10 million worldwide) is larger than the population of Armenia itself (3 million).
Armenians are renowned for their apricots – the Latin name for apricot (Prunus armeniaca) means 'Armenian plum'.
Armenian culture is rich in music (duduk – a mournful woodwind), tapestry, and epic poetry.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Armenia covers 29,743 sq km in the South Caucasus.
A landlocked country bordered by Georgia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkey.
Mountainous terrain with Lake Sevan at its centre and the Aragats peak at 4,090m.
The Armenian Highland is one of the ancient world's cradles of civilisation.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Armenia was the world's first Christian country, adopting the religion in 301 AD!
The Armenian alphabet, created in 405 AD, is still used virtually unchanged today.
Kim Kardashian is of Armenian descent – she has brought global attention to the Armenian Genocide of 1915.
Armenia's apricots inspired the Latin scientific name Prunus armeniaca – 'Armenian plum'.

Azerbaijan.tagline: Land of Fire – Eternal Flames, Caspian Shores, and Caucasus Crossroads 🇦🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Baku is Azerbaijan's capital on the Caspian Sea, a city mixing medieval Old Town with modern flame-shaped skyscrapers.
Baku hosted the first ever Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix in 2016.
Azerbaijan literally means 'Land of Fire' – eternal natural gas flames have burned here for millennia.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Flame Towers – Three skyscrapers shaped like flames dominate Baku's skyline and are lit up at night.
Old City of Baku (İçərişəhər) – A UNESCO World Heritage walled medieval city with a Maiden Tower.
Yanar Dag (Burning Mountain) – A natural hillside that has been on fire for decades from underground gas.
Gobustan Rock Art – UNESCO-listed prehistoric rock carvings and mud volcanoes dating back 40,000 years.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – The Baku oil fields have been producing since the 1840s; the first commercial oil well was drilled here.
Carpets – Azerbaijani carpet weaving is UNESCO heritage; each region has distinct patterns.
Agriculture – Pomegranates, hazelnuts, saffron, and grapes are important.
Tourism – Baku's mix of ancient and ultra-modern architecture is drawing growing tourism.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Azerbaijani (Azeri) is the official language, a Turkic language.
Azerbaijan is a secular Muslim-majority country with strong Turkic and Persian cultural influences.
Mugham – a classical Azerbaijani vocal and instrumental tradition – is UNESCO heritage.
Pomegranate is the symbol of Azerbaijan; the Goychay Pomegranate Festival is a major celebration.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Azerbaijan covers 86,600 sq km in the South Caucasus.
Bordered by Russia, Georgia, Armenia, Iran, and the Caspian Sea (the world's largest enclosed water body).
Varied geography from the Greater Caucasus mountains in the north to the Caspian lowlands.
The Kura and Aras rivers drain through the country.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The world's first commercial oil well was drilled in Baku in 1848 – 11 years before the famous Drake well in Pennsylvania!
Azerbaijan has more mud volcanoes than anywhere else in the world – about 400 of the world's 700.
Yanar Dag mountain has been burning for centuries and is believed to be the origin of Zoroastrian fire worship.
Azerbaijan won Eurovision 2011 and immediately built a massive arena in Baku for the next contest.

Bahrain.tagline: Pearl of the Gulf – Ancient Dilmun, Formula 1, and Island Kingdom 🇧🇭

Capital City 🏛️.text: Manama is Bahrain's capital and a modern financial centre on the Arabian Gulf.
Bahrain is an archipelago of 33 small islands, connected to Saudi Arabia by the King Fahd Causeway.
Bahrain was the first Gulf state to discover oil (1932) and first to nearly run out.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Bahrain Fort (Qal'at al-Bahrain) – UNESCO-listed ancient capital of the Dilmun civilisation.
Tree of Life – A 400-year-old mesquite tree in the desert with no known water source, a mysterious natural wonder.
Bahrain International Circuit – Hosts the Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix.
Al-Fateh Grand Mosque – One of the world's largest mosques, holding 7,000 worshippers.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Finance & Banking – Bahrain is a leading Gulf financial centre.
Aluminium – The ALBA smelter is one of the world's largest aluminium smelters.
Oil Refining – Despite declining reserves, oil remains important.
Tourism & Hospitality – F1, shopping, and culture draw visitors from the Gulf region.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language; English is widely used in business.
Bahrain has a mix of Sunni and Shia Muslims; the royal family is Sunni.
Bahraini culture is known for its pearl diving heritage – Bahraini pearls were world-famous before synthetic pearls.
Dilmun, the ancient civilisation on Bahrain, features in the Sumerian Epic of Gilgamesh as a paradise land.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Bahrain covers just 778 sq km – one of the world's smallest countries.
An archipelago in the Arabian Gulf between Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
Connected to Saudi Arabia by the 25km King Fahd Causeway.
Mostly flat and arid with a central limestone plateau.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Tree of Life in Bahrain is a 400-year-old tree in the middle of the desert with no known water source!
Bahrain was the ancient land of Dilmun – the Sumerian paradise, mentioned in the Epic of Gilgamesh.
Bahrain was the first Gulf state to give women the right to vote (2002).
Bahrain's pearl industry was so important that before oil, it was the world's top source of natural pearls.

Cyprus.tagline: Island of Aphrodite – Myth, Mosaics, and Mediterranean Sunshine 🇨🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Nicosia is Cyprus's capital, the world's last divided capital city – split between the Republic of Cyprus and Turkish-administered North Cyprus since 1974.
Limassol is the island's main port and commercial city.
Cyprus is the birthplace of Aphrodite, the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Petra tou Romiou – The legendary birthplace of Aphrodite, a sea rock with a romantic myth.
Paphos Mosaics – Stunning UNESCO-listed Roman floor mosaics depicting Greek myths.
Troodos Mountains – Pine-forested mountains with painted Byzantine churches (UNESCO World Heritage).
Famagusta (Gazimağusa) – A medieval walled city in the north with Gothic cathedrals.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Cyprus is one of the Mediterranean's top beach and cultural destinations.
Finance & Business Services – A major European and international business hub.
Shipping – Cyprus has one of the world's largest shipping registries.
Agriculture – Halloumi cheese, citrus fruits, carobs, and olives are famous exports.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Greek and Turkish are both official languages.
Cyprus has a Greek Cypriot majority (south) and Turkish Cypriot minority (north), divided since 1974.
Halloumi – the squeaky grilling cheese – originates from Cyprus and is now protected as EU origin.
Cypriot folk dancing, lace-making (lefkaritika), and silver craft are UNESCO-recognised traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Cyprus covers 9,251 sq km, the third-largest island in the Mediterranean Sea.
Located south of Turkey and west of Syria in the eastern Mediterranean.
The Troodos mountain range dominates the interior; the Mesaoria plain is in the centre.
Cyprus has one of the Mediterranean's sunniest climates with 340+ days of sunshine per year.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Nicosia is the world's last divided capital – you can walk across the border of two states inside the city!
Cyprus is the legendary birthplace of Aphrodite, goddess of love, at Petra tou Romiou.
Halloumi cheese from Cyprus is protected by EU law as a product of Cypriot origin.
Cyprus has been inhabited for over 10,000 years; the world's oldest known well is on Cyprus!

Georgia.tagline: Where the Caucasus Meets the Vine – Ancient Wine, Golden Fleece, and Mountain Towers 🇬🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tbilisi is Georgia's capital, a city of sulphur bath houses, carved wooden balconies, and cliff-side churches.
Kutaisi, the ancient Colchis capital, is associated with Jason and the Golden Fleece myth.
Georgia has been called the 'Cradle of Wine' – evidence of winemaking 8,000 years ago found here.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Vardzia Cave Monastery – A 12th-century cave city carved into a volcanic cliff, with over 600 rooms.
Gergeti Trinity Church – A medieval church perched at 2,170m below Mount Kazbek (5,047m).
Uplistsikhe – An ancient cave city hewn from rock, 3,000 years old.
Old Town Tbilisi – A UNESCO-candidate neighbourhood of carved wooden balconies, Orthodox domes, and Persian-influenced bathhouses.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Wine – Georgia produces wine in clay qvevri amphorae (UNESCO heritage); Saperavi and Rkatsiteli are famous varieties.
Tourism – Growing rapidly, especially to Tbilisi, Svaneti, and Kazbegi.
Agriculture – Mandarins, hazelnuts, tea, and grapes are key exports.
Hydropower – Georgia exports electricity from Caucasus mountain rivers.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Georgian (Kartuli) is the official language, with a unique alphabet unlike any other in the world.
Georgia has four scripts developed in antiquity; the current Mkhedruli script dates from the 10th century.
Georgian polyphonic singing (three independent vocal parts) is UNESCO world heritage.
Georgia is famous for its hospitality, feasting tradition (supra), and toasting culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Georgia covers 69,700 sq km in the South Caucasus.
Bordered by Russia, Turkey, Armenia, and Azerbaijan, with a Black Sea coast.
The Greater Caucasus range forms the northern border; the Lesser Caucasus is in the south.
One of the world's most geographically diverse small countries.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Georgia is the world's oldest winemaking country – 8,000-year-old winemaking equipment was found here!
The Georgian script is one of only 14 unique writing systems in the world still in active use.
The mythological land of Colchis (Georgia) is where Jason and the Argonauts sought the Golden Fleece.
Georgia has the world's longest cave system (Krubera Cave) at over 2,197 metres deep – the deepest known cave on Earth.

Iran.tagline: Persia – Ancient Empires, Blue Tilework, and Persian Poetry 🇮🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tehran is Iran's capital and largest city, a vast modern metropolis at the foot of the Alborz mountains.
Isfahan (Esfahan) is the historic city of breathtaking Islamic architecture, called 'half of the world'.
Shiraz is the city of poets, gardens, and wine (historically), birthplace of Hafez and Sa'di.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Persepolis – The magnificent ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Persian Empire, founded by Darius I in 518 BC (UNESCO World Heritage).
Imam Square (Naghsh-e Jahan), Isfahan – One of the world's largest squares with stunning 17th-century mosques.
Nasir al-Mulk Mosque (Pink Mosque), Shiraz – A mosque that floods with rainbow light through stained glass.
Golestan Palace, Tehran – A UNESCO-listed Qajar-era royal palace complex.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – Iran has the world's 4th largest oil reserves and 2nd largest natural gas reserves.
Carpets – Iranian hand-knotted carpets are the world's finest; carpet weaving is a national art form.
Pistachios & Saffron – Iran is the world's top producer of saffron and among top pistachio producers.
Petrochemicals & Steel – Major industrial sectors.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Persian (Farsi) is the official language, one of the world's great literary languages.
Iran is a multi-ethnic nation of Persians, Azerbaijanis, Kurds, Arabs, Baloch, and others.
Persian poetry – Rumi, Hafez, Omar Khayyam – is revered worldwide as a supreme literary tradition.
Iranian culture is 3,000 years old; Nowruz (Persian New Year) is celebrated by 300 million people worldwide.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Iran covers 1.65 million sq km – the 17th largest country in the world.
Bordered by Iraq, Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Caspian Sea, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan, and the Persian/Oman Gulf.
Dominated by the Iranian Plateau surrounded by Alborz and Zagros mountain ranges.
Contains salt deserts (Dasht-e Kavir), tropical forests (Gilan coast), and snow-capped peaks.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Iran (Persia) created one of history's greatest empires – the Achaemenid Empire stretched from Egypt to India in 500 BC.
Rumi, born in what is now Afghanistan but writing in Persian, is the world's best-selling poet today!
Iran produces 85% of the world's saffron – the world's most expensive spice by weight.
The world's oldest known legal system, the Code of Hammurabi, was created in the region of ancient Persia/Mesopotamia.

National Animal 🐾.text: Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica) – on the flag (historical)

Iraq.tagline: Cradle of Civilisation – Mesopotamia, Tigris, Euphrates, and Babylon 🇮🇶

Capital City 🏛️.text: Baghdad is Iraq's capital, once the most magnificent city in the medieval world as capital of the Abbasid Caliphate.
Basra in the south is Iraq's major port and gateway to the Persian Gulf.
Erbil (Hawler) in Iraqi Kurdistan is one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Babylon – Ruins of the ancient city including Nebuchadnezzar's Hanging Gardens (one of Seven Wonders of the World).
Ur – Ancient Sumerian city and birthplace of Abraham; site of the Great Ziggurat of Ur.
Ctesiphon – Ruins of the Sassanid Persian capital with the world's largest brick arch.
Marshes of Mesopotamia – UNESCO World Heritage wetlands, birthplace of civilisation and home of the Marsh Arabs.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Iraq has the world's 5th largest oil reserves; oil accounts for over 99% of export earnings.
Agriculture – The Tigris-Euphrates valley was the world's first great agricultural region.
Dates – Iraq was historically the world's largest date producer.
Natural Gas – Significant untapped gas reserves.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic and Kurdish are Iraq's official languages.
Iraq's population includes Arabs, Kurds, Turkmen, Assyrians, and other minorities.
The Marsh Arabs (Ma'dan) have lived in the southern marshes in reed houses since ancient Sumerian times.
Iraqi maqam music, traditional calligraphy, and poetry are living cultural arts.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Iraq covers 438,317 sq km in the Middle East.
Bordered by Iran, Turkey, Syria, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and the Persian Gulf.
The Tigris and Euphrates rivers, between which civilisation began, run through Iraq.
Landscape ranges from desert in the west, fertile river valley in the centre, to mountains in the north.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Iraq (ancient Mesopotamia) is where writing, agriculture, the wheel, and the first cities were invented!
The world's first written law code (Code of Hammurabi) was created in Mesopotamia (modern Iraq/Iran).
Baghdad in the 8th–13th centuries was the world's largest city and centre of global learning.
The Sumerian city of Uruk in Iraq is considered the world's first true city, founded over 5,000 years ago.

Jordan.tagline: Rose-Red City and Desert Kingdom – Petra, Dead Sea, and Bedouin Warmth 🇯🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Amman is Jordan's capital, a city built on seven hills with Roman ruins alongside modern cafes.
Aqaba on the Red Sea is Jordan's only port city and a famous diving destination.
Jordan hosts the highest proportion of refugees per capita of any country in the world.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Petra – The rose-red Nabataean city carved into rock cliffs, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Wadi Rum – A vast, otherworldly desert of red sandstone cliffs used as a film location for The Martian and Dune.
Dead Sea – The saltiest body of water on Earth; the lowest point on land at 430m below sea level.
Jerash – One of the world's best-preserved Roman cities, with colonnaded streets and temples.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Phosphate – Jordan is one of the world's top phosphate producers.
Potash – Major export from the Dead Sea mineral industry.
Tourism – Petra, Wadi Rum, and Dead Sea attract over 4 million visitors annually.
Services – Banking, IT, and trade services are growing sectors.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is Jordan's official language.
Jordan's population is mostly Arab with Palestinian, Bedouin, Circassian, and Iraqi communities.
Bedouin culture – nomadic desert hospitality, camel herding, and coffee ceremonies – is deeply honoured.
Mansaf (lamb cooked in dried yoghurt sauce served over rice) is Jordan's national dish.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Jordan covers 89,342 sq km in the Middle East.
Bordered by Israel/Palestine, Syria, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, and the Red Sea.
Mostly desert with the Jordan River valley (the world's lowest valley) in the west.
The Dead Sea on the western border is the saltiest natural lake on Earth.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Petra's Treasury (Al-Khazneh) was carved into a cliff face by the Nabataeans 2,000 years ago without machinery!
Wadi Rum was used to film The Martian and Lawrence of Arabia – its landscape really does look like Mars.
Jordan's Dead Sea is so salty you float without trying – 10 times saltier than the ocean!
Jordan has given refuge to more refugees per capita than any other country in the world.

Kuwait.tagline: Pearl of the Gulf – Oil Wealth, Desert Sands, and Gulf Heritage 🇰🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Kuwait City is the capital and commercial hub, featuring the iconic Kuwait Towers on the Gulf coast.
Kuwait is a constitutional emirate ruled by the Al-Sabah family.
Kuwait was liberated from Iraqi occupation in 1991 by a US-led coalition in the Gulf War.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Kuwait Towers – The iconic three-towers water complex, a symbol of Kuwait's modernity and prosperity.
Grand Mosque of Kuwait – Accommodates 10,000 worshippers with a spectacular dome.
Failaka Island – An ancient island with Greek ruins from Alexander the Great's expedition.
Kuwait National Museum – Showcasing Kuwait's rich heritage from dhow building to pearl diving.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Kuwait holds nearly 10% of the world's proven oil reserves.
Finance – Kuwait is a major Gulf financial centre and home of the Kuwait Investment Authority, one of the world's oldest sovereign wealth funds.
Petrochemicals – Major downstream oil processing industry.
Desalination – Kuwait is a world leader in sea water desalination technology.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is Kuwait's official language; English is widely used in business.
Kuwait has a majority expatriate population – only about 30% of residents are Kuwaiti citizens.
Kuwaiti culture blends Bedouin traditions with Gulf pearling and maritime heritage.
Machboos (spiced rice with meat or fish) and harees are beloved Kuwaiti dishes.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Kuwait covers 17,818 sq km at the head of the Persian Gulf.
Bordered by Iraq and Saudi Arabia; a tiny, mostly flat desert country.
Summer temperatures regularly exceed 50°C – among the hottest on Earth.
Kuwait Bay provides a natural harbour that made it a historic trading port.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Kuwait has almost no rainfall – some years get less than 25mm – yet it has one of the world's highest living standards.
Kuwait's sovereign wealth fund (Kuwait Investment Authority, founded 1953) is the world's first!
Kuwait was occupied by Iraq in 1990; the world's largest oil field fires followed its liberation.
Kuwait City is one of the world's wealthiest cities per capita.

Lebanon.tagline: Pearl of the Middle East – Cedars, Civilisations, and Culinary Legacy 🇱🇧

Capital City 🏛️.text: Beirut is Lebanon's capital, nicknamed the 'Paris of the Middle East' for its culture, fashion, and nightlife.
Beirut has been destroyed and rebuilt 7 times in its history; its people are renowned for resilience.
Lebanon gave the world the Phoenician alphabet – the ancestor of all modern Western alphabets.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Cedars of God (Arz el-Rab) – Ancient cedar trees in the mountains; the cedar is Lebanon's national symbol.
Baalbek – Spectacular Roman temple complex with the world's largest Roman stone blocks.
Byblos – One of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities, a UNESCO site and birthplace of the alphabet.
Jeita Grotto – A spectacular network of underground caverns with a subterranean lake.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Banking & Finance – Lebanon was historically the Middle East's banking capital.
Tourism – Skiing, beaches, ruins, and Beirut's nightlife attract visitors.
Agriculture – Grapes, olives, citrus, and apples from the fertile Bekaa Valley.
Diaspora Remittances – The 12 million Lebanese diaspora (vs 4 million at home) send significant income.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language; French and English are widely spoken.
Lebanon is one of the most diverse countries in the Arab world with 18 officially recognised religious sects.
Lebanese cuisine – hummus, tabbouleh, fattoush, kibbeh, baklava – is one of the world's most celebrated.
The Lebanese diaspora is enormous: Brazil alone has 7 million people of Lebanese descent!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Lebanon covers 10,452 sq km – one of the Middle East's smallest countries.
Bordered by Syria, Israel, and the Mediterranean Sea.
A mountain country – the Lebanon and Anti-Lebanon ranges run parallel to the coast.
The fertile Bekaa Valley between the two mountain ranges is Lebanon's breadbasket.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lebanon gave the world the Phoenician alphabet around 1050 BC – the origin of the Greek, Latin, Arabic, and Hebrew alphabets!
You can ski in the morning and swim in the Mediterranean in the afternoon on the same day in Lebanon.
Baalbek's Temple of Jupiter has six remaining columns larger than anything built by the Romans anywhere else.
Carlos Ghosn (of Nissan/Renault fame) and Shakira are both of Lebanese descent.

Oman.tagline: Arabia Felix – Incense Routes, Fjords, and Peaceful Desert Kingdom 🇴🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: Muscat is Oman's capital, a scenic city nestled between dramatic mountains and the Gulf of Oman.
Salalah in the south is famous for its monsoon season (khareef) when it turns lush green.
Oman is ruled by Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, following the long reign of the beloved Sultan Qaboos.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque – A stunning white marble mosque, the largest in Oman with a world-famous chandelier.
Wahiba Sands – A classic red-orange sand desert with Bedouin camps.
Wadi Shab – A dramatic gorge with emerald pools and waterfalls hidden behind boulders.
Musandam Fjords – Dramatic limestone fjords on the Strait of Hormuz, called 'the Norway of Arabia'.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – Oil is the main revenue source, though Oman has smaller reserves than Gulf neighbours.
Frankincense – Oman's Dhofar region produces the world's finest frankincense (luban), exported for millennia.
Tourism – Adventure tourism (wadis, deserts, diving) is a growing focus.
Fisheries – Rich fishing in the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language; English is widely spoken.
Oman is predominantly Ibadi Muslim – a rare and moderate branch of Islam found mainly in Oman.
Omani culture is deeply hospitable; coffee (qahwa) with dates is offered to every guest.
Frankincense trade made Oman one of Arabia's wealthiest regions for 3,000 years.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Oman covers 309,500 sq km in the southeastern Arabian Peninsula.
Bordered by UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Yemen, with coasts on the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea.
The Hajar Mountains run along the north coast; vast desert in the interior.
The Musandam Peninsula (an exclave) controls the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Oman controlled the world's frankincense trade for 3,000 years – it was more valuable than gold.
The Musandam fjords are some of the world's most dramatic coastal scenery – called the 'Norway of Arabia'.
Oman was one of the world's first seafaring nations; Omani sailors navigated to East Africa and India for centuries.
Sultan Qaboos transformed Oman from a medieval kingdom to a modern state in just 50 years.

Palestine.tagline: Holy Land – Olive Trees, Ancient History, and Enduring Spirit 🇵🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Ramallah serves as the administrative capital of the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank.
East Jerusalem is claimed by Palestinians as the capital of a future Palestinian state.
Palestine consists of two non-contiguous areas: the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Church of the Nativity, Bethlehem – UNESCO World Heritage site built over the traditional birthplace of Jesus.
Al-Aqsa Mosque, Jerusalem – The third-holiest site in Islam, on the Temple Mount.
Dome of the Rock, Jerusalem – The golden-domed Islamic shrine built in 691 AD.
Jericho – Considered the world's oldest continuously inhabited city, over 10,000 years old.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Olive oil, dates, and stone fruit from ancient olive groves.
Handicrafts – Palestinian embroidery (tatreez), ceramics, and olive wood carvings are world-renowned.
Construction – A major economic activity in the West Bank.
Remittances – Palestinian diaspora supports the economy from abroad.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language.
Palestinian culture has a rich tradition of embroidery (tatreez), each region with distinct patterns.
Palestinian cuisine – musakhan (sumac chicken), maqluba (upside-down rice), and knafeh dessert – is beloved.
The Palestinian keffiyeh (chequered headscarf) is one of the world's most recognised cultural symbols.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Palestine consists of the West Bank (5,655 sq km) and Gaza Strip (365 sq km).
The West Bank lies between Israel and Jordan; Gaza borders Israel and Egypt on the Mediterranean coast.
The Jordan River and Dead Sea border the West Bank to the east.
The land is the birthplace of three world religions: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Jericho in Palestine is considered the world's oldest continuously inhabited city – over 10,000 years old!
Palestine is the birthplace of Jesus Christ (Bethlehem) and a holy land for three world religions.
The Dead Sea Scrolls – the oldest biblical manuscripts – were discovered in caves in the West Bank in 1947.
Palestinian tatreez (embroidery) is on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

Qatar.tagline: Desert Jewel – World Cup, Natural Gas, and Pearl Heritage 🇶🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Doha is Qatar's capital and nearly its only city, a futuristic skyline rising from the Arabian Gulf.
Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup – the first in the Middle East and the first in a Muslim-majority country.
Qatar has the world's highest GDP per capita due to its massive natural gas wealth.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lusail Stadium – The magnificent golden stadium that hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup final.
Museum of Islamic Art – A stunning I.M. Pei-designed museum on Doha's corniche with 7,000 years of Islamic art.
Souq Waqif – A restored traditional bazaar in Doha selling spices, falcons, and Qatari crafts.
The Pearl – An artificial island development with luxury residences and a Venice-inspired marina.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Natural Gas – Qatar is the world's largest LNG (liquefied natural gas) exporter.
Oil – Significant oil production alongside gas.
Finance & Investment – Qatar Investment Authority manages $450 billion+ in global assets.
Sports & Media – Al Jazeera (news), beIN Sports, and Qatar Airways are global Qatari brands.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is Qatar's official language; English is widely spoken.
Only about 12% of Qatar's population are Qatari citizens; 88% are expatriate workers.
Falconry is Qatar's most cherished cultural tradition – UNESCO-recognised and deeply embedded in Gulf identity.
Qatari cuisine includes machboos (spiced rice), harees (wheat and meat porridge), and luqaimat (fried dumplings).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Qatar covers 11,571 sq km – a small peninsula jutting into the Arabian Gulf.
Bordered only by Saudi Arabia on land, with the Arabian Gulf on all other sides.
Mostly flat desert with no mountains; summer temperatures exceed 45°C.
Sits above the world's largest natural gas field (North Dome/South Pars, shared with Iran).

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Qatar has the world's highest GDP per capita – Qatari citizens are among the wealthiest people on Earth.
The 2022 World Cup was the first held in a Muslim-majority country and the first in the Middle East.
Qatar's North Dome gas field is the world's largest single gas reservoir.
Qatar built a fully air-conditioned outdoor stadium for the World Cup!

Syria.tagline: Cradle of Cities – Damascus, Aleppo, and the Ancient Silk Road 🇸🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Damascus is Syria's capital, often called the world's oldest continuously inhabited capital city.
Aleppo (Halab) is Syria's second city and one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities.
Syria has been central to human civilisation for over 10,000 years.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Old City of Damascus – A UNESCO World Heritage walled city with the Umayyad Mosque and covered souqs.
Palmyra (Tadmor) – Once a spectacular Roman-era desert oasis city, partially destroyed in recent conflict.
Krak des Chevaliers – A UNESCO Crusader castle considered the finest medieval fortress in the world.
Old City of Aleppo – UNESCO World Heritage ancient citadel and bazaars, being rebuilt after conflict.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Wheat, cotton, olives, and fruit from the fertile Euphrates valley.
Oil – Declining oil production was once significant.
Textiles – Damascus silk and Aleppo soap (made from laurel berry and olive oil) are ancient exports.
Reconstruction – Rebuilding after years of conflict is a massive ongoing effort.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is Syria's official language.
Syria has Arab, Kurdish, Alawite, Christian, and Druze communities with diverse traditions.
Damascus steel – the legendary blade metal – and Aleppo soap have been made in Syria for over a millennium.
Syrian cuisine – kibbeh, shawarma, fattoush, and baklava – has influenced food across the Middle East.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Syria covers 185,180 sq km in the Middle East.
Bordered by Turkey, Iraq, Jordan, Israel/Palestine, Lebanon, and the Mediterranean Sea.
The Euphrates River flows through eastern Syria; the Mediterranean coast is in the west.
The Syrian Desert covers much of the interior; the coast and northwest are fertile.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Damascus is believed to be the world's oldest continuously inhabited capital city – over 11,000 years old!
The Umayyad Mosque in Damascus was the world's largest mosque when built in 705 AD.
Aleppo soap – made from olive and laurel oil – has been produced in Syria for over 3,000 years.
The world's first alphabet was created by Phoenicians along the Syrian/Lebanese coast.

Yemen.tagline: Arabia Felix – Frankincense, Socotra Island, and Ancient Highland Kingdoms 🇾🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Sana'a is Yemen's capital, an ancient walled city with tower houses decorated in stained glass, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Aden in the south is a historic port city on the Gulf of Aden.
Yemen was historically called 'Arabia Felix' (Happy Arabia) by Romans for its fertile highlands.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Old City of Sana'a – A UNESCO World Heritage ancient city of mud-brick tower houses with white stained-glass windows.
Socotra Island – A UNESCO Biosphere with alien-looking Dragon Blood trees found nowhere else on Earth.
Shibam Hadramawt – A UNESCO-listed city of 500-year-old mud-brick skyscrapers, called the 'Manhattan of the Desert'.
Ma'rib – Site of the ancient Sabaean kingdom and the legendary dam of the Queen of Sheba.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Declining oil reserves have been the main revenue source.
Fishing – Rich fishing in the Arabian Sea and Gulf of Aden.
Agriculture – Coffee (Mocha coffee originates from Yemen), honey, and qat (a stimulant leaf) are traditional crops.
Remittances – Yemeni diaspora in Saudi Arabia and Gulf countries send vital funds home.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is Yemen's official language.
Yemenis are among the oldest Arab peoples with distinct Hadhrami, Tihami, and highland cultures.
Yemeni coffee (mocha) is the ancestor of global coffee culture – the word 'mocha' comes from the port of Al-Mukha.
Jambiya (curved dagger) is worn as a status symbol by Yemeni men; it is central to cultural identity.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Yemen covers 527,968 sq km in the southwestern Arabian Peninsula.
Bordered by Saudi Arabia and Oman, with coastlines on the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
The Arabian Sea island of Socotra is part of Yemen.
The western highlands receive monsoon rains making them fertile; the interior is desert.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The word 'mocha' coffee comes from Yemen's port of Al-Mukha – the world's original coffee export hub in the 15th century!
Socotra Island has 700 plant species found nowhere else on Earth, including the bizarre Dragon Blood tree.
Shibam's mud-brick skyscrapers, built 500 years ago and reaching 11 stories, are the world's oldest skyscrapers!
The Queen of Sheba's legendary kingdom was in ancient Yemen (Saba/Sheba).

Egypt.tagline: Gift of the Nile – Land of Pharaohs and Ancient Mysteries 🇪🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Cairo is the capital of Egypt and the largest city in Africa, home to over 20 million people.
Cairo sits right next to the ancient city of Giza, home to the Great Pyramids.
The city is called 'The City of a Thousand Minarets' for its many beautiful mosques.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Great Pyramid of Giza – The only remaining Wonder of the Ancient World, built over 4,500 years ago.
The Sphinx – A giant limestone statue with a lion's body and a human head, guarding the pyramids.
Luxor Temple – A spectacular ancient temple complex on the banks of the Nile.
Valley of the Kings – Where the tombs of pharaohs, including Tutankhamun, were discovered.
Abu Simbel – Giant rock temples built by Ramesses II, relocated to save them from flooding.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Egypt's ancient wonders attract millions of visitors every year.
Suez Canal – One of the world's most important trade routes, connecting the Mediterranean to the Red Sea.
Agriculture – Cotton and wheat grown along the fertile Nile Delta.
Oil & Natural Gas – Egypt is one of Africa's leading energy producers.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is Egypt's official language; the Egyptian dialect is the most widely understood in the Arab world.
Egyptians are descendants of one of the world's oldest civilisations, dating back 5,000+ years.
The Coptic Christian community is one of the oldest Christian communities in the world.
Traditional music, belly dancing, and ahwa (coffee house) culture are central to Egyptian life.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Egypt covers 1 million sq km; 90% is desert – the Sahara and Eastern Desert.
The Nile River, the world's longest river, runs through Egypt into the Mediterranean Sea.
Sinai Peninsula connects Africa to Asia, containing Mount Sinai and Red Sea coral reefs.
Bordered by Libya, Sudan, Israel, and the Red Sea.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Ancient Egyptians invented writing (hieroglyphics), paper (papyrus), and the 365-day calendar!
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the pyramids.
Egypt has more ancient monuments than any other country in the world.
The ancient Egyptians mummified cats and worshipped them as sacred animals.

Nigeria.tagline: Giant of Africa – Colours, Culture, and Unstoppable Energy 🇳🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Abuja is Nigeria's capital, a purpose-built modern city designed in the 1970s.
Lagos, the former capital, remains the commercial heart and most populous city in Africa.
Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory of Abuja.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Zuma Rock – A massive monolith near Abuja, often called the 'Gateway to Abuja'.
Olumo Rock – A historic natural fortress in Abeokuta used for refuge during wars.
Yankari National Park – Home to hippos, elephants, and Nigeria's most famous wildlife.
Lekki Conservation Centre – A canopy walkway above Lagos lagoon ecosystems.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – Nigeria is Africa's largest oil producer, providing 90% of the country's export income.
Nollywood – Nigeria's film industry is the world's 2nd largest by volume, producing thousands of movies a year.
Agriculture – Cassava, yam, cocoa, and groundnuts are major crops.
Music – Afrobeats artists like Burna Boy and WizKid have taken Nigerian music global.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Nigeria has over 500 languages; Hausa, Yoruba, and Igbo are the three major ones.
With 220 million people, Nigeria is Africa's most populous nation.
Over 250 ethnic groups with rich traditions in art, music, storytelling, and dance.
Nigerian cuisine – jollof rice, egusi soup, suya – is beloved across Africa and the diaspora.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Nigeria covers 923,768 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Benin, Niger, Chad, and Cameroon, with a southern coast on the Atlantic Ocean.
Geography ranges from Sahel savannah in the north to tropical rainforests and Niger Delta in the south.
The Niger and Benue rivers merge in Nigeria, forming one of Africa's largest river deltas.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Nigeria will likely become the world's 3rd most populous country by 2050.
Lagos is Africa's largest city and one of the fastest-growing cities in the world.
Nigeria has produced Nobel Prize winners and world-class writers like Chinua Achebe and Wole Soyinka.
The country has the highest rate of twins born naturally in the world – especially in Igbo-Ora town.

South Africa.tagline: Rainbow Nation – Wildlife, Wonder, and Human Triumph 🇿🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (executive), Cape Town (legislative), and Bloemfontein (judicial).
Cape Town is considered one of the world's most beautiful cities, framed by Table Mountain.
Johannesburg is the financial capital and largest city.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Table Mountain – A flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town and the Atlantic Ocean.
Kruger National Park – One of Africa's largest game reserves, home to the Big Five.
Robben Island – Where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned for 27 years; now a UNESCO site.
Drakensberg Mountains – Dramatic mountain range with San rock art galleries.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Mining – South Africa is the world's largest producer of platinum and chromium.
Wine Industry – South Africa's Cape Winelands produce world-class wines.
Tourism – Wildlife safaris, Cape Town, and Garden Route attract millions of visitors.
Financial Services – Johannesburg Stock Exchange is Africa's largest stock market.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: South Africa has 11 official languages including Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, and English.
Known as the 'Rainbow Nation' for its diverse mix of cultures, races, and traditions.
The Zulu, Xhosa, Sotho, Tswana, and San (Bushmen) are major indigenous groups.
Ubuntu philosophy – 'I am because we are' – defines South African community spirit.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: South Africa covers 1.22 million sq km at the southern tip of Africa.
Surrounded by the Atlantic and Indian Oceans, meeting at Cape Agulhas – Africa's southernmost point.
Climates range from desert (Kalahari) to Mediterranean (Cape) to subtropical (east coast).
The Orange and Limpopo rivers are major waterways.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: South Africa is the only country to have voluntarily given up its nuclear weapons programme.
The world's first heart transplant was performed in Cape Town in 1967 by Dr. Christiaan Barnard.
South Africa holds the world's largest known reserves of platinum group metals.
Nelson Mandela became president at age 75 after 27 years in prison – a symbol of forgiveness and freedom.

Kenya.tagline: Home of Safari – Wild Skies and Warrior Spirit 🇰🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Nairobi is Kenya's capital and the largest city in East Africa.
Nairobi National Park sits on the edge of the city – the only national park within a capital city!
Nairobi is a major hub for East African business, technology (Silicon Savannah), and diplomacy.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Maasai Mara National Reserve – Famous for the Great Wildebeest Migration, one of nature's greatest spectacles.
Mount Kenya – Africa's second-highest mountain and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Amboseli National Park – Iconic views of elephants with Mount Kilimanjaro as a backdrop.
Lake Nakuru – A pink flamingo paradise and rhino sanctuary.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tea & Coffee – Kenya is one of the world's top exporters of tea and specialty coffee.
Horticulture – Cut flowers, especially roses, grown in Kenya supply Europe daily.
Tourism – Wildlife safaris bring millions of visitors and major revenue to the country.
Mobile Banking – Kenya's M-Pesa was the world's first successful mobile money system.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Swahili and English are the official languages of Kenya.
Kenya has over 40 ethnic groups including the Kikuyu, Luo, Maasai, Luhya, and Kalenjin.
The Maasai are renowned for their distinctive red clothing, beadwork, and warrior traditions.
Kenya has produced many world champion marathon runners including Eliud Kipchoge.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Kenya covers 580,367 sq km in East Africa, straddling the equator.
Bordered by Ethiopia, Somalia, Tanzania, Uganda, and South Sudan.
Geography includes the Great Rift Valley, savannah grasslands, volcanic highlands, and Indian Ocean coastline.
Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, touches Kenya's western border.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Kenya is where the world's fastest runners come from – Kenyan athletes dominate long-distance running globally.
The wildebeest migration in Maasai Mara involves over 1.5 million animals crossing crocodile-filled rivers!
Kenya was a pioneer in mobile money – M-Pesa revolutionised banking for millions without bank accounts.
Nairobi means 'cool water' in the Maasai language.

Ethiopia.tagline: Land of Origins – Where Humanity and Coffee Were Born 🇪🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Addis Ababa is Ethiopia's capital and the diplomatic capital of Africa, hosting the African Union headquarters.
It sits at 2,355m above sea level, making it one of the world's highest capital cities.
Addis Ababa means 'New Flower' in Amharic.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lalibela Rock-Hewn Churches – 11 medieval churches carved directly into volcanic rock, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Simien Mountains – Dramatic highland landscape with unique wildlife like the Gelada baboon.
Aksum Obelisks – Ancient stone pillars of the Aksumite Empire.
Blue Nile Falls – One of Africa's most impressive waterfalls on the outflow of Lake Tana.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Coffee – Ethiopia is the birthplace of coffee; it remains the country's largest export.
Flowers – Ethiopia is one of the world's leading exporters of cut flowers.
Agriculture – Teff grain (used to make injera flatbread) and pulses are major crops.
Textiles – Growing garment manufacturing sector exporting to global brands.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Amharic is the official language; over 80 languages are spoken across the country.
Ethiopia has over 120 million people from diverse ethnic groups: Oromo, Amhara, Tigrinya, Somali, and more.
Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months and is about 7–8 years behind the Gregorian calendar!
The Ethiopian Orthodox Church is one of the world's oldest Christian churches.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Ethiopia covers 1.1 million sq km in the Horn of Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by Eritrea, Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan, and Sudan.
The Great Rift Valley runs through Ethiopia, creating dramatic landscapes and lakes.
The Danakil Depression is one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The oldest human ancestor fossil ('Lucy', 3.2 million years old) was found in Ethiopia.
Coffee was discovered in Ethiopia – legend says a goat herder noticed his goats energised by coffee berries!
Ethiopia was never colonised by Europeans, making it a symbol of African independence.
Ethiopian runners are among the world's greatest – Haile Gebrselassie and Abebe Bikila are legends.

Morocco.tagline: Kingdom of Light – Sahara Sands, Ancient Medinas, and Atlantic Shores 🇲🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Rabat is Morocco's capital and seat of the king and government.
Casablanca is the largest city and economic hub, known globally from the classic 1942 film.
Marrakech and Fez are two of the world's best-preserved ancient Islamic cities.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Medina of Fez – The world's largest car-free urban area and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Jemaa el-Fnaa Square, Marrakech – A vibrant square packed with storytellers, snake charmers, and food stalls.
Sahara Desert (Erg Chebbi) – Towering golden dunes where you can ride camels and sleep under the stars.
Hassan II Mosque, Casablanca – One of the world's largest mosques, built partly over the Atlantic Ocean.
Atlas Mountains – A dramatic range with Berber villages and Morocco's highest peak, Toubkal (4,167m).

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Phosphate – Morocco holds 70% of the world's known phosphate reserves, essential for fertilisers.
Tourism – One of Africa's top tourist destinations for culture, beaches, and the Sahara.
Agriculture – Argan oil (liquid gold), olives, oranges, and dates are major exports.
Renewable Energy – The Noor Solar Power Plant complex is one of the world's largest solar farms.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic and Tamazight (Berber) are official languages; French is widely used in business.
Berber (Amazigh) people are Morocco's indigenous inhabitants with their own language and traditions.
Moroccan culture blends Arab, Berber, African, and Andalusian influences.
Mint tea is the symbol of Moroccan hospitality – refusing a glass is considered rude!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Morocco covers 446,550 sq km in northwestern Africa.
The only African country with both Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea coastlines.
Bordered by Algeria and the disputed Western Sahara territory.
Separated from Spain by only 14 km at the Strait of Gibraltar.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859 AD, is the world's oldest continuously operating university!
Morocco is the only African country not in the African Union (it left over the Western Sahara issue).
Argan trees are climbed by goats to eat the fruit – a quirky sight unique to Morocco!
Morocco co-hosted the 2030 FIFA World Cup along with Spain and Portugal.

National Animal 🐾.text: Barbary Lion (Panthera leo leo) – now extinct in the wild

Ghana.tagline: Black Star of Africa – The Gateway to West Africa 🇬🇭

Capital City 🏛️.text: Accra is Ghana's capital and largest city, on the Gulf of Guinea coast.
Kumasi is Ghana's second city and cultural capital of the Ashanti Kingdom.
Ghana was the first sub-Saharan African country to gain independence (1957), led by Kwame Nkrumah.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Cape Coast Castle – A UNESCO-listed former slave fortress, a powerful reminder of the transatlantic slave trade.
Kakum National Park – A tropical forest with a canopy walkway 30 metres above the forest floor.
Mole National Park – Ghana's largest wildlife refuge, home to elephants, hippos, and baboons.
Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park – Honouring Ghana's founding father and pan-African hero.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Cocoa – Ghana is the world's 2nd largest cocoa producer; most of the world's chocolate starts here!
Gold – Ghana is Africa's largest gold producer, historically known as the 'Gold Coast'.
Oil – Offshore oil discovered in 2007 made Ghana an important energy producer.
Timber & Agriculture – Major exporter of timber, palm oil, and rubber.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is the official language; Twi, Ga, Ewe, and Dagbani are major local languages.
Ghana has over 100 ethnic groups; the Akan (Ashanti and Fante) are the largest.
Kente cloth – colourful woven fabric worn at celebrations – is Ghana's most iconic cultural symbol.
Ghanaian hospitality is legendary; the country consistently ranks as one of Africa's most welcoming.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Ghana covers 238,533 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, and Togo, with a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.
Lake Volta – created by the Akosombo Dam – is the world's largest man-made lake by area.
Climate is tropical with a distinct dry Harmattan season from the Sahara.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Ghana sits almost exactly at the intersection of the Prime Meridian (0° longitude) and the Equator (0° latitude)!
The Ashanti Kingdom had one of West Africa's most powerful empires, famous for its golden stool (Sika Dwa).
Ghana's Faroe Island-inspired 'fantasy coffins' are shaped like eagles, cars, or fish – colourful farewell art!
Ghana inspired many African Americans to reconnect with their roots through the 'Year of Return' in 2019.

Tanzania.tagline: Serengeti Soul – Kilimanjaro, Wildlife, and Zanzibar Spice 🇹🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Dodoma is Tanzania's official capital, though Dar es Salaam remains the largest city and commercial hub.
Zanzibar City (Stone Town) is a UNESCO World Heritage site on the spice islands.
Tanzania was formed in 1964 by the union of Tanganyika and the islands of Zanzibar.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mount Kilimanjaro – Africa's highest mountain (5,895m) and the world's highest free-standing mountain.
Serengeti National Park – Home to the world's largest mammal migration – 2 million wildebeest and zebras.
Ngorongoro Crater – The world's largest intact caldera, a natural animal enclosure with the Big Five.
Zanzibar Beaches – Indian Ocean paradise islands famous for white sand, turquoise water, and spices.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Safari tourism to Serengeti, Kilimanjaro, and Zanzibar is the backbone of the economy.
Agriculture – Coffee, tea, cotton, and cloves (Tanzania/Zanzibar produce 75% of world's cloves).
Mining – Gold, tanzanite (found ONLY in Tanzania), and diamonds are important exports.
Fishing – The coastline and Lake Victoria provide significant fishing industry.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Swahili (Kiswahili) and English are official languages; Swahili originated on the Tanzanian coast.
Tanzania has over 120 ethnic groups, including Chaga, Maasai, Sukuma, and Swahili peoples.
The Maasai maintain their warrior traditions, colourful beadwork, and cattle herding lifestyle.
Tanzanian food includes ugali (maize porridge), pilau rice, and Zanzibar seafood curry.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Tanzania covers 945,087 sq km in East Africa, including Zanzibar and other islands.
Bordered by Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, DRC, Zambia, Malawi, Mozambique, and the Indian Ocean.
Lake Victoria (world's largest tropical lake) and Lake Tanganyika (world's longest lake) touch Tanzania.
The Great Rift Valley cuts through Tanzania, creating dramatic escarpments and soda lakes.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Tanzanite, a blue-violet gemstone found ONLY near Mount Kilimanjaro, is 1,000 times rarer than diamonds!
The Serengeti wildebeest migration is called the 'Greatest Show on Earth' – 2 million animals moving together.
Mount Kilimanjaro can be climbed without any technical mountaineering skills – just determination!
Zanzibar's spice trade made it one of the world's most important commercial hubs in the 1800s.

Algeria.tagline: Pearl of the Maghreb – Sahara Vastness and Mediterranean Soul 🇩🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Algiers (El Djazaïr) is Algeria's capital and largest city on the Mediterranean coast.
Known as 'Algiers the White' (La Ville Blanche) for its whitewashed buildings cascading down hillsides.
Algeria gained independence from France in 1962 after an 8-year war.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Tassili n'Ajjer – A UNESCO World Heritage plateau in the Sahara with over 15,000 prehistoric rock paintings.
Timgad (Roman city) – A remarkably well-preserved Roman city in the Aurès mountains.
Hoggar Mountains (Ahaggar) – Dramatic volcanic spires rising from the Sahara Desert.
Casbah of Algiers – A UNESCO-listed ancient Islamic city with winding alleys and Ottoman architecture.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Natural Gas – Algeria is Africa's largest natural gas exporter and a top 10 global oil producer.
Agriculture – Dates, wheat, and olives are key crops in the northern coastal region.
Mining – Iron ore, phosphate, and uranium deposits.
Renewables – Investing in massive Sahara solar energy projects.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic and Tamazight (Berber) are official languages; French is widely used.
Algeria has the world's largest Berber (Amazigh) speaking population.
The Tuareg – the 'Blue People of the Sahara' – are nomadic Berber people of the deep desert.
Algerian cuisine is heavily influenced by Berber, Arab, Ottoman, and French traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Algeria is Africa's largest country, covering 2.38 million sq km.
Over 80% of the country is covered by the Sahara Desert.
Borders 7 countries: Morocco, Western Sahara, Mauritania, Mali, Niger, Libya, and Tunisia.
The Mediterranean coast is narrow but fertile, called the Tell region.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Algeria is the largest country in Africa and the 10th largest in the world.
The Sahara in Algeria is home to the world's oldest known rock art – over 10,000 years old!
Algeria supplies a quarter of Europe's natural gas through undersea pipelines.
The ancient Phoenicians and Romans had major civilisations in what is now Algeria.

Libya.tagline: Ancient Tripolitania – Sahara Dunes, Roman Ruins, and Mediterranean Shores 🇱🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tripoli is Libya's capital on the Mediterranean coast, a city of Roman arches and Ottoman bazaars.
Benghazi is the second city in the east.
Libya has Africa's largest proven oil reserves and a tiny population of just 7 million.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Leptis Magna – One of the best-preserved Roman cities in the world, a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Sabratha Roman Theatre – A spectacular 2nd-century Roman theatre on the Mediterranean coast.
Acacus Mountains – UNESCO-listed Saharan rock art dating back 12,000 years.
Ghadames Old Town – A UNESCO-listed ancient Saharan oasis city with covered walkways.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Libya has Africa's largest oil reserves; oil accounts for nearly all government revenue.
Natural Gas – Significant gas exports, mainly to Europe.
Agriculture – Limited; dates, olives, and wheat in coastal areas.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language; Berber (Amazigh) languages are also spoken.
Libya is predominantly Arab and Berber with Tuareg and Tebu communities in the south.
Libyan cuisine features couscous, bazin (barley dough), and lamb dishes.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Libya covers 1.76 million sq km – Africa's 4th largest country.
90% of Libya is desert; most people live in a narrow coastal strip.
Borders Egypt, Sudan, Chad, Niger, Algeria, and Tunisia.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Leptis Magna was the birthplace of Roman Emperor Septimius Severus and is one of the world's best-preserved Roman cities.
Libya has more ancient Roman ruins than Italy itself!
The Libyan Sahara contains some of the world's most dramatic sand seas (ergs) and rock formations.

Tunisia.tagline: Mediterranean Jewel – Carthage, Medinas, and Saharan Oases 🇹🇳

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tunis is Tunisia's capital, a city of whitewashed medinas and French colonial boulevards.
Carthage, now a suburb of Tunis, was the capital of one of the ancient world's greatest empires.
Tunisia sparked the Arab Spring in 2010, inspiring revolutions across the Arab world.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Carthage – UNESCO ruins of the ancient Phoenician/Carthaginian city destroyed by Rome in 146 BC.
Medina of Tunis – A UNESCO World Heritage labyrinthine old city with 700 monuments.
Dougga – The best-preserved Roman town in North Africa, a UNESCO site.
Sahara Oases (Douz, Tozeur) – Gateway towns to the Sahara Desert with date palm forests.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Tunisia is one of Africa's top tourist destinations for its beaches, ruins, and Sahara.
Phosphates – Tunisia is a major phosphate producer.
Olive Oil – Tunisia is the world's 4th largest olive oil producer.
Textiles – Major garment manufacturer for European brands.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language; French is widely used in business and education.
Tunisia is predominantly Arab-Berber; the Amazigh (Berber) culture survives in Matmata and island communities.
Tunisian cuisine features harissa (chilli paste), brik pastry, and couscous with fish.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Tunisia covers 163,610 sq km – the smallest North African country.
Bordered by Algeria and Libya, with coastlines on the Mediterranean and Gulf of Gabes.
Northern Tunisia is fertile Mediterranean; the south is Sahara Desert.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Tunisia was the birthplace of the Arab Spring – a fruit vendor's protest in 2010 changed the Arab world.
Carthage was Rome's greatest rival; the Carthaginian general Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome!
Tunisia's island of Djerba is home to one of the world's oldest Jewish communities (El Ghriba synagogue).

Sudan.tagline: Land of the Black Pharaohs – Nubian Pyramids and Nile Civilisations 🇸🇩

Capital City 🏛️.text: Khartoum is Sudan's capital, at the confluence of the Blue and White Nile rivers.
Omdurman across the Nile is Sudan's largest city and cultural heart.
Sudan separated from South Sudan in 2011 after a referendum.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Meroe Pyramids – Over 200 ancient Nubian pyramids in the desert, more than Egypt has!
Jebel Barkal – A sacred mountain with ancient Nubian temples at its base, a UNESCO site.
Nile River – The world's longest river flows through Sudan, sustaining ancient civilisations.
Dinder National Park – A vast savannah reserve with elephants, lions, and giraffes.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Cotton, sesame, sorghum, and groundnuts are major crops.
Oil – Sudan lost most oil fields to South Sudan after partition.
Gold Mining – Growing gold production in the eastern deserts.
Livestock – One of Africa's largest livestock populations.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is the official language; over 130 indigenous languages are spoken.
Sudan has over 570 tribes; the Nubian people of the north have one of Africa's oldest civilisations.
Sudanese culture blends Arab and African traditions in music, dance, and cuisine.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Sudan covers 1.86 million sq km – Africa's 3rd largest country.
Bordered by Egypt, Libya, Chad, Central African Republic, South Sudan, Ethiopia, and Eritrea.
The Sahara Desert covers northern Sudan; the Nile valley is the lifeline.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Sudan has more ancient pyramids than Egypt – over 200 Nubian pyramids!
The ancient Nubian (Kushite) pharaohs ruled all of Egypt in the 8th century BC.
The Blue and White Nile meet in Khartoum – you can see the two rivers running side by side before merging.

South Sudan.tagline: World's Newest Nation – Nile Wetlands, Wildlife, and Rebuilding Hope 🇸🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Juba is South Sudan's capital on the White Nile, a city rapidly developing since independence.
South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011 – the world's newest nation.
It is one of the least developed countries but rich in natural resources and wildlife.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sudd Wetlands – One of the world's largest freshwater ecosystems, a vast Nile swamp teeming with wildlife.
Nimule National Park – Home to hippos, elephants, and Cape buffalo on the Uganda border.
Boma National Park – Site of one of Africa's greatest wildlife migrations, rivalling the Serengeti.
Imatong Mountains – The highest range in South Sudan with lush montane forests.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – South Sudan controls 75% of former Sudan's oil fields; oil is almost the entire economy.
Agriculture – Sorghum, maize, and cassava are subsistence crops.
Cattle Herding – Cattle are a form of wealth and social status for the Dinka and Nuer peoples.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is the official language; over 60 indigenous languages are spoken.
South Sudan has over 60 ethnic groups; the Dinka and Nuer are the largest.
The Dinka are among the world's tallest people – men average over 180cm.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: South Sudan covers 644,329 sq km in East-Central Africa.
Landlocked, bordered by Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, DRC, and Central African Republic.
The White Nile flows through the centre; the Sudd swamp is one of the world's largest wetlands.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: South Sudan is the world's newest country, gaining independence on 9 July 2011.
The Sudd in South Sudan is one of the world's largest freshwater ecosystems.
South Sudan's Boma-Jonglei migration may be the largest land migration in the world – 1.2 million antelopes!

Somalia.tagline: Land of Punt – Ancient Incense Trade, Longest Coastline, and Resilience 🇸🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Mogadishu is Somalia's capital, an ancient Indian Ocean port city now rebuilding after decades of conflict.
Hargeisa in Somaliland (a self-declared republic) is the region's largest city.
Somalia has the longest coastline in mainland Africa – over 3,300 km.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Laas Geel – UNESCO-candidate cave paintings from 9,000–3,000 BC, some of Africa's finest.
Mogadishu Cathedral – A ruined Italian colonial cathedral, a haunting symbol of the civil war era.
Cape Guardafui – The 'Horn of Africa', the easternmost point of the African continent.
Liido Beach, Mogadishu – A beautiful beach on the Indian Ocean, slowly returning to life.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Livestock – Somalia is the world's largest exporter of live camels.
Fishing – Vast Indian Ocean fishing grounds along Africa's longest coastline.
Remittances – The Somali diaspora sends over $1 billion annually.
Frankincense & Myrrh – Somalia is a top producer of these ancient resins.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Somali is the official language – uniquely, Somalia is Africa's most ethnically homogeneous large country.
Almost all Somalis are ethnic Somali and Muslim; clan affiliation is socially central.
Somali poetry and oral literature is rich; the 'Somali Shakespeare' Raage Ugaas is celebrated.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Somalia covers 637,657 sq km in the Horn of Africa.
Bordered by Ethiopia, Kenya, and Djibouti, with coasts on the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden.
Mostly arid plateau; the north (Somaliland) is more mountainous.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Ancient Egypt traded with the 'Land of Punt' for frankincense and myrrh – many historians believe Punt was Somalia.
Somalia has Africa's longest coastline – 3,333 km – yet lacks a developed fishing industry.
Despite the collapse of formal government in 1991, Somali mobile money (Zaad) became Africa's first mobile payment system!

Eritrea.tagline: Red Sea Pearl – Ancient Aksum, Italian Architecture, and Hard-Won Freedom 🇪🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Asmara is Eritrea's capital, nicknamed the 'Little Rome' for its Art Deco Italian colonial architecture – UNESCO-listed.
Massawa is the historic Red Sea port, one of the hottest inhabited cities on Earth.
Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993 after a 30-year independence war.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Asmara – A UNESCO World Heritage city of extraordinary 1930s Italian Modernist architecture.
Dahlak Archipelago – A pristine Red Sea island chain with coral reefs and sea turtles.
Qohaito – Ancient ruins of an Aksumite city with an obelisk and dam over 2,000 years old.
Nakfa – The mountain town that never fell to Ethiopian forces, a symbol of Eritrean resistance.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Mining – Gold, silver, copper, and zinc deposits are being developed.
Agriculture – Sorghum, millet, and teff are staple crops.
Fisheries – The Red Sea provides rich fishing grounds.
Construction – Chinese investment in infrastructure is growing.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Tigrinya, Arabic, and English are the main working languages; Eritrea has 9 ethnic groups.
The Tigrinya, Tigre, Saho, and Afar are the main ethnic groups.
Eritrean coffee ceremony is a treasured cultural ritual of hospitality.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Eritrea covers 117,600 sq km in the Horn of Africa.
Bordered by Sudan, Ethiopia, and Djibouti, with a long Red Sea coastline.
The Dahlak Archipelago in the Red Sea contains over 200 islands.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Asmara's Art Deco architecture is so extraordinary it became a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Eritrea has one of the lowest internet usage rates in the world – the government tightly controls information.
The Eritrean independence war (1961–1991) lasted 30 years – one of Africa's longest liberation struggles.

Djibouti.tagline: Horn of Contrasts – Volcanic Lakes, Strategic Straits, and Desert Heat 🇩🇯

Capital City 🏛️.text: Djibouti City is both the capital and the country's main city, sitting at the mouth of the Red Sea.
Djibouti is one of the most strategically important ports in the world – at the entrance to the Suez Canal route.
Djibouti has more foreign military bases than any other country – USA, France, China, Japan, and Italy all have bases here.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lake Assal – A crater lake that is Africa's lowest point (155m below sea level) and one of Earth's saltiest.
Lake Abbe – A surreal landscape of limestone chimneys and flamingos on the Ethiopian border.
Ardoukoba Volcano – A young volcano that last erupted in 1978.
Gulf of Tadjoura – A stunning inlet of crystal blue water popular for whale shark diving.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Port & Logistics – Djibouti's port handles 95% of land-locked Ethiopia's trade.
Military Bases – Hosting foreign military bases provides significant rental income.
Salt – Lake Assal's salt is extracted and exported.
Services – Banking and transport services for the Horn of Africa region.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French and Arabic are official languages; Somali and Afar are widely spoken.
Djibouti has two main ethnic groups: the Somali (Issa) and the Afar.
Despite its tiny size (just 900,000 people), Djibouti is a model of regional stability.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Djibouti covers just 23,200 sq km – one of Africa's smallest countries.
Bordered by Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Somalia, with coasts on the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
Mostly volcanic desert; Lake Assal at -155m is Africa's lowest point.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lake Assal is the world's largest salt reserve after the Dead Sea – and the lowest point in Africa!
Djibouti has the highest concentration of foreign military bases of any country in the world.
Whale sharks gather year-round off Djibouti's coast – one of the best places in the world to swim with them.

Uganda.tagline: Pearl of Africa – Mountain Gorillas, Source of the Nile, and Churchill's Jewel 🇺🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Kampala is Uganda's capital, a hilly city of seven hills on the shores of Lake Victoria.
Winston Churchill called Uganda 'the Pearl of Africa' for its extraordinary natural beauty.
Uganda is home to roughly half the world's remaining mountain gorilla population.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Bwindi Impenetrable Forest – Home to over 400 mountain gorillas; gorilla trekking is a bucket-list experience.
Murchison Falls – The world's most powerful waterfall, where the Nile squeezes through a 7m gap.
Source of the Nile (Jinja) – The point where the Nile leaves Lake Victoria and begins its 6,650 km journey to the Mediterranean.
Queen Elizabeth National Park – Stunning park with tree-climbing lions, hippos, and over 600 bird species.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Coffee is Uganda's top export; also tea, fish, and cut flowers.
Oil – Offshore Lake Albert oil discoveries are being developed.
Tourism – Mountain gorilla trekking is the world's most exclusive wildlife experience.
Fishing – Lake Victoria provides a huge tilapia and Nile perch fishing industry.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English and Swahili are official languages; Luganda is the most spoken local language.
Uganda has over 40 ethnic groups; the Baganda, Banyakole, Basoga, and Acholi are the largest.
Ugandan culture celebrates music, traditional dances, and the Baganda Kingdom's royal culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Uganda covers 241,551 sq km in East Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by South Sudan, DRC, Rwanda, Tanzania, and Kenya.
Lies on the equator; Lake Victoria – the world's largest tropical lake – covers the southeast.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Uganda has the world's youngest population – the median age is just 15.7 years!
The mountain gorilla population is actually growing – from ~600 in 2007 to over 1,000 today, thanks to conservation.
Uganda produces 50% of Africa's vanilla – the world's second most expensive spice after saffron.

Rwanda.tagline: Land of a Thousand Hills – Remarkable Recovery, Gorillas, and Green Vision 🇷🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Kigali is Rwanda's capital, consistently ranked the cleanest and most ordered city in Africa.
Rwanda is called 'the Land of a Thousand Hills' for its rolling green terrain.
Rwanda has rebuilt from the 1994 genocide to become one of Africa's fastest-growing economies.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Volcanoes National Park – Home to mountain gorillas in the Virunga volcanoes, made famous by Dian Fossey.
Kigali Genocide Memorial – A sobering but important site honouring the 800,000 killed in 100 days in 1994.
Nyungwe Forest – One of Africa's oldest rainforests with chimpanzees and 300 bird species.
Lake Kivu – A stunning mountain lake on the DRC border with island resorts.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Gorilla trekking permits ($1,500 each) generate vital conservation revenue.
Tea & Coffee – Rwandan specialty coffee wins international awards.
Mining – Coltan, cassiterite, and wolfram (minerals essential for electronics).
Technology – Kigali is building itself as Africa's tech startup hub.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Kinyarwanda, French, and English are official languages.
Unlike most African countries, Rwanda has just one main ethnic language and culture despite Hutu/Tutsi divisions.
Rwanda has more women in parliament than any other country in the world (over 60%).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Rwanda covers 26,338 sq km – one of Africa's smallest and most densely populated countries.
A landlocked country bordered by Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi, and DRC.
Entirely hilly – Rwanda truly has a thousand hills – with elevations between 1,000m and 4,507m.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Rwanda has banned plastic bags since 2008 – one of the world's first countries to do so!
Rwanda has more women in parliament than any country in the world.
Kigali is Africa's cleanest city – citizens participate in monthly community cleaning days (Umuganda).
Rwanda's economy grew at 8% annually for 20 years after the 1994 genocide – one of history's greatest recoveries.

Burundi.tagline: Heart of Africa – Drum Nation, Lake Tanganyika, and Highland Kingdom 🇧🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: Gitega is Burundi's official capital; Bujumbura remains the largest city and economic hub on Lake Tanganyika.
Burundi is one of the world's smallest and most densely populated countries.
The Batwa (Pygmy) people are among the original inhabitants of Burundi's forests.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lake Tanganyika – The world's longest lake and second deepest (1,470m), with crystal-clear water and unique fish.
Kibira National Park – The largest rainforest in Burundi, home to chimpanzees.
Rusizi National Park – Hippos and crocodiles in the Rusizi River delta.
Gishora Drum Sanctuary – Centre of Burundi's royal drum tradition, a UNESCO masterpiece.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Coffee & Tea – Burundi's highland coffee is considered some of Africa's finest specialty coffee.
Agriculture – The vast majority of Burundians are subsistence farmers.
Fishing – Lake Tanganyika provides important protein from freshwater sardines.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Kirundi and French are official languages.
Burundi has three main groups: Hutu (majority), Tutsi, and Twa (Batwa).
The royal drums of Burundi (Karyenda) are sacred; drumming is a living cultural art form.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Burundi covers 27,834 sq km in Central/East Africa.
Landlocked, bordered by Rwanda, Tanzania, and DRC.
A mountainous country sitting on the Great Rift Valley rim above Lake Tanganyika.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Burundi's royal drumming tradition (Ingoma) is UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.
Lake Tanganyika is the world's longest freshwater lake and holds 16% of the world's surface fresh water.
Burundi consistently ranks as one of the world's poorest countries despite having extraordinary natural beauty.

Democratic Republic of Congo.tagline: Heart of Darkness and Light – Congo Basin, Gorillas, and Extraordinary Wealth 🇨🇩

Capital City 🏛️.text: Kinshasa is DRC's capital, the world's largest French-speaking city with over 15 million people.
Lubumbashi is the mining capital in the copper-rich south.
The Congo River – the world's deepest river – flows through the country.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Congo Rainforest – The world's second-largest rainforest, covering 2 million sq km; a vital climate regulator.
Virunga National Park – Africa's oldest national park, home to gorillas, okapis, and active volcanoes.
Congo River – The world's deepest river (220m) and second largest by water flow after the Amazon.
Nyiragongo Volcano – One of the world's most active volcanoes with a permanent lava lake.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Coltan & Cobalt – DRC produces 70% of the world's cobalt, essential for every phone and EV battery.
Copper & Diamonds – Major global producer of both.
Timber – Vast Congo rainforest timber resources.
Hydropower – Inga Falls could generate 40,000 MW – the world's largest hydroelectric potential.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Lingala, Swahili, Kikongo, and Tshiluba are national languages.
DRC has over 250 ethnic groups and 600+ languages – the world's most linguistically diverse country.
The Pygmy (Mbuti, Aka) peoples are the Congo rainforest's original inhabitants.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: DRC covers 2.34 million sq km – Africa's 2nd largest and world's 11th largest country.
Borders 9 countries: Congo-Brazzaville, CAR, South Sudan, Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania, Zambia, Angola.
The Congo Basin is covered by the world's second-largest tropical rainforest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: DRC produces 70% of the world's cobalt – every smartphone and EV battery likely contains Congolese cobalt.
The bonobo – humanity's closest relative (sharing 98.7% of our DNA) – lives ONLY in the DRC.
Inga Falls on the Congo River has more hydroelectric potential than any other site on Earth.
The Congo River is the world's deepest river at over 220m – deeper than most people's houses are tall.

Republic of Congo.tagline: Congo-Brazzaville – Jungle Capital, Jazz, and Congo River Crossings 🇨🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Brazzaville is the capital, sitting directly across the Congo River from Kinshasa – the world's two closest capitals.
Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the world's two closest foreign capital cities – separated only by the river.
Republic of Congo is different from DRC (Congo-Kinshasa); it was once known as Congo-Brazzaville.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Odzala-Kokoua National Park – One of Africa's oldest parks, with forest elephants, gorillas, and bongo antelope.
Congo River – The border with DRC; crossing the river by ferry is a unique adventure.
Brazzaville Cathedral – A striking French colonial cathedral in the capital.
Nouabalé-Ndoki National Park – Pristine Congo Basin forest with minimal human impact.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Oil accounts for over 80% of government revenue.
Timber – Significant tropical timber exports.
Agriculture – Cassava, plantains, and maize are staple crops.
Mining – Potash and iron ore deposits being developed.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is the official language; Lingala and Kikongo are widely spoken.
The Kongo, Teke, and Mboshi are the main ethnic groups.
The Sapeurs of Brazzaville are famous worldwide – working-class men who dress in extravagant designer suits.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Republic of Congo covers 342,000 sq km in Central Africa.
Bordered by Gabon, Cameroon, CAR, DRC, Angola, and the Atlantic Ocean.
Mostly rainforest with the Congo River forming the eastern border.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Sapeurs of Brazzaville – working men who dedicate their lives to elegant dress – are a global cultural phenomenon!
Brazzaville and Kinshasa are the world's two closest capital cities of different countries – just 4 km apart!
The forests of Congo-Brazzaville hold some of the world's last untouched tropical wilderness.

Cameroon.tagline: Africa in Miniature – Rainforests, Savannah, Mountains, and Beaches 🇨🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: Yaoundé is Cameroon's capital, a hill city in the centre of the country.
Douala is the largest city and economic capital, on the Gulf of Guinea.
Cameroon is called 'Africa in Miniature' because it contains every landscape found across the continent.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mount Cameroon – An active volcano and West/Central Africa's highest peak (4,095m).
Waza National Park – Savannah wildlife reserve with elephants, lions, and giraffes.
Dja Faunal Reserve – UNESCO World Heritage rainforest, one of Africa's best-conserved.
Bamileke Highlands – A region of volcanic lakes, crater lakes, and traditional chieftainships.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Declining but still significant oil production.
Agriculture – Cameroon is the world's 5th largest cocoa producer; also produces coffee, cotton, and rubber.
Timber – Significant forest industry.
Hydropower – Major hydroelectric potential on the Sanaga River.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French and English are both official languages – Cameroon is bilingual.
Cameroon has over 250 ethnic groups and 280+ languages – one of the world's most ethnically diverse.
Cameroonian music styles like Bikutsi and Makossa are beloved across Africa.
