Area & Geography 🌍.text: Cameroon covers 475,442 sq km in West-Central Africa.
Borders Nigeria, Chad, Central African Republic, Congo, Gabon, and Equatorial Guinea.
Geography ranges from Atlantic coast mangroves to Sahel savannah to rainforest to alpine peaks.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lake Nyos in Cameroon suddenly released a cloud of CO₂ in 1986 that suffocated 1,700 people and 3,500 livestock overnight.
Cameroon's Roger Milla became the oldest player (42) to score in a World Cup!
Cameroon is bilingual in French and English – a legacy of being divided between French and British rule.

Central African Republic.tagline: Heart of the Continent – Rainforests, Lowland Gorillas, and Undiscovered Wilderness 🇨🇫

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bangui is the CAR's capital on the Ubangi River.
CAR sits at the geographic heart of Africa.
Despite enormous natural resources, CAR consistently ranks among the world's least developed countries.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Dzanga-Sangha Special Reserve – One of the world's best places to see forest elephants and lowland gorillas.
Sangha Trinational Park – A UNESCO World Heritage transboundary forest park.
Boali Falls – A spectacular waterfall on the Mbali River near Bangui.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Diamonds – CAR is a significant diamond producer; illegal mining remains a challenge.
Timber – Tropical hardwood logging is a major industry.
Gold & Uranium – Significant mineral resources, largely untapped.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Sango and French are official languages.
Over 80 ethnic groups including Gbaya, Banda, Mandjia, and Sara.
The Bayaka (Pygmy) people of the southwest are forest dwellers with extraordinary polyphonic music.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: CAR covers 622,984 sq km in the centre of Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by Chad, Sudan, South Sudan, DRC, Congo, and Cameroon.
Ranges from tropical rainforest in the south to Sahel savannah in the north.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Bayaka Pygmy music of CAR is UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage – one of the world's oldest musical traditions.
CAR is one of the darkest countries at night viewed from space – minimal electrification outside Bangui.
Dzanga Bai in CAR is the best place in the world to see forest elephants gathering at mineral licks.

Gabon.tagline: Last Eden – 80% Rainforest, Oil Wealth, and Africa's Green Heart 🇬🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Libreville is Gabon's capital on the Atlantic coast, meaning 'Free Town' – named by freed slaves in 1849.
Gabon is one of Africa's wealthiest countries per capita, thanks to oil and gas.
Gabon has maintained 80%+ forest cover while neighbours have deforested – a remarkable achievement.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lopé National Park – UNESCO World Heritage site where rainforest meets savannah; gorillas, elephants, and forest buffalo.
Ivindo National Park – Home to the spectacular Kongou and Mingouli waterfalls in pristine rainforest.
Pongara National Park – Beaches where leatherback sea turtles nest in large numbers.
Crystal Mountains – A sandstone and quartzite range with extraordinary biodiversity.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Oil has made Gabon one of sub-Saharan Africa's wealthiest countries per capita.
Manganese – Gabon is the world's 2nd largest manganese producer.
Timber – High-quality tropical hardwoods, though increasingly managed sustainably.
Agriculture – Palm oil, cocoa, and rubber.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is the official language; over 40 Bantu languages are spoken.
Gabon has about 40 ethnic groups; the Fang are the largest.
Bwiti spiritual ceremonies using the visionary plant iboga are an important Gabonese cultural tradition.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Gabon covers 267,668 sq km on the equator in Central-West Africa.
Bordered by Equatorial Guinea, Cameroon, Congo, and the Atlantic Ocean.
80% covered by dense tropical rainforest – one of the world's most forested countries.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Gabon protects 11% of its land in national parks – more than most developed countries.
Gabon has more forest elephants than any other country – over 60,000!
The iboga plant from Gabon is being studied as a potential treatment for addiction disorders.

Equatorial Guinea.tagline: Oil-Rich Island Nation – Bioko Gorillas and Mainland Rainforest 🇬🇶

Capital City 🏛️.text: Malabo on Bioko Island is the capital; a new capital (Oyala/Ciudad de la Paz) is being built on the mainland.
Equatorial Guinea is the only Spanish-speaking country in Africa.
It became Africa's 4th largest oil producer after offshore oil discovery in 1995, transforming its economy.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Pico Basile – The highest peak in Equatorial Guinea (3,011m) on Bioko Island, surrounded by cloud forest.
Monte Alén National Park – Mainland rainforest with gorillas, chimpanzees, and forest elephants.
Bioko Island Beaches – Critically important leatherback sea turtle nesting sites.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – Offshore oil has made Equatorial Guinea one of Africa's richest per capita.
Cocoa – Bioko Island was once the world's largest cocoa producer.
Timber – Tropical hardwood extraction.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish, French, and Portuguese are official languages – uniquely trilingual.
The Fang are the main mainland ethnic group; the Bubi are the main Bioko island group.
Equatorial Guinea is the only African nation with Spanish as an official language.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Equatorial Guinea covers 28,051 sq km, comprising Bioko Island, Annobón Island, and mainland Río Muni.
Bordered by Cameroon and Gabon on the mainland; Bioko Island sits in the Gulf of Guinea.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Equatorial Guinea is the only Spanish-speaking country in Sub-Saharan Africa!
Bioko Island has one of the world's highest primate diversity – 10 species of primates including drill monkeys.
Equatorial Guinea went from one of Africa's poorest to richest (per capita) countries in just 20 years after oil.

Chad.tagline: Dead Heart of Africa – Sahara, Sahel, Lake Chad, and Ancient Kingdoms 🇹🇩

Capital City 🏛️.text: N'Djamena is Chad's capital on the Chari River at the border with Cameroon.
Chad is one of the world's most landlocked countries – 1,700 km from the sea.
The country spans from the Sahara Desert in the north to tropical savannah in the south.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lake Chad – A once-massive lake that has shrunk by 90% since 1960 due to climate change and irrigation.
Ennedi Massif – UNESCO-listed desert plateau with extraordinary rock arches, gorges, and prehistoric rock art.
Zakouma National Park – A recovering wildlife haven with elephants, lions, and giraffes.
Tibesti Mountains – Remote volcanic mountains in the Sahara with the highest peak in the Sahara (3,415m).

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Oil discovered in 2003 has become the main export.
Agriculture – Cotton, sorghum, and millet in the south.
Livestock – Nomadic herding is a major livelihood for northern and central Chad.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French and Arabic are official languages; over 120 local languages are spoken.
Chad has over 200 ethnic groups; Sara, Arab, Toubou, and Fulani are the largest.
The ancient Kanem-Bornu Empire centred on Lake Chad was one of Africa's longest-lasting states.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Chad covers 1.28 million sq km in north-central Africa.
Bordered by Libya, Sudan, South Sudan, CAR, Nigeria, Cameroon, and Niger.
Lake Chad in the southwest was once Africa's largest freshwater lake.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lake Chad has shrunk by 90% since 1960 – one of the world's most dramatic examples of climate change impact.
The Ennedi Plateau has natural rock arches more spectacular than those in Utah, USA, yet rarely visited.
Chad is the world's second most landlocked country after Kazakhstan (furthest point from the sea).

Niger.tagline: Land of the Tuareg – Saharan Splendour and the World's Largest Uranium Deposits 🇳🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Niamey is Niger's capital on the Niger River.
Niger is the world's largest country by area in West Africa.
Over 80% of Niger is covered by the Sahara Desert.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Aïr Mountains and Ténéré Desert – UNESCO World Heritage; dramatic highlands and the Sahara's most scenic sand sea.
W National Park – A transboundary park with elephants, lions, and hippopotamuses.
Agadez – A historic Tuareg city and caravan hub with a magnificent mud-brick mosque.
Ténéré Desert – One of the world's largest sand deserts, part of the Sahara.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Uranium – Niger is the world's 5th largest uranium producer; French nuclear power partially depends on Nigerien uranium.
Gold – Growing gold production.
Agriculture – Millet, sorghum, and cowpeas; most Niger is too arid for farming.
Livestock – Large herds of cattle, goats, sheep, and camels.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Hausa and Zarma-Songhai are the most spoken local languages.
Niger has over 20 ethnic groups; Hausa, Zarma, Tuareg, Fulani are the largest.
The Tuareg are the iconic 'Blue Men of the Sahara' – nomadic Berber people famous for indigo-dyed robes.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Niger covers 1.27 million sq km – West Africa's largest country.
A landlocked country bordered by Algeria, Libya, Chad, Nigeria, Benin, Burkina Faso, and Mali.
Over 80% is Sahara or Sahel; only the far south gets enough rain for agriculture.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Tree of Ténéré was once the world's most isolated tree – a lone acacia in the Sahara, 400 km from the nearest tree, until a drunk driver knocked it down in 1973!
Niger is the world's 5th largest uranium producer – powering French nuclear reactors.
Niger has the highest fertility rate in the world (7.1 children per woman average).

Mali.tagline: Empire of Gold – Timbuktu, Niger River, and Ancient Djinguereber 🇲🇱

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bamako is Mali's capital on the Niger River, a fast-growing West African city.
Timbuktu (Tombouctou) was the legendary medieval city of learning and gold trade.
The Mali Empire (1230–1600) was the world's wealthiest empire during its peak.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Timbuktu – A UNESCO World Heritage city; once the world's greatest Islamic learning centre with 25,000 students.
Djinguereber Mosque, Timbuktu – A 14th-century mud-brick mosque, one of the oldest in sub-Saharan Africa.
Bandiagara Escarpment (Dogon Country) – A 150km sandstone cliff with extraordinary Dogon villages and culture.
Djenné – A UNESCO-listed city with the world's largest mud-brick building (Great Mosque of Djenné).

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Gold – Mali is Africa's 3rd largest gold producer.
Agriculture – Cotton, millet, sorghum; the Niger River delta (Inland Delta) is highly productive.
Livestock – Large cattle, sheep, and goat herds.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Bambara is the most widely spoken local language.
Mali has over 40 ethnic groups: Bambara, Fula, Tuareg, Songhai, and Dogon.
The Dogon people have a unique cosmology with knowledge of the Sirius star system that puzzled 20th-century astronomers.
Malian music – from Ali Farka Touré's blues to Salif Keita's Afropop – has influenced world music profoundly.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Mali covers 1.24 million sq km – one of Africa's largest countries.
A landlocked country bordered by Algeria, Niger, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Guinea, Senegal, and Mauritania.
The Niger River makes a great bend through Mali's heart, creating a vast inland delta.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Mansa Musa of the Mali Empire (1280–1337) is considered the wealthiest person in history – worth an estimated $400 billion!
His 1324 pilgrimage to Mecca with 60,000 men and gold so abundant he crashed the Egyptian economy!
The Great Mosque of Djenné is the world's largest mud-brick building, rebuilt every year by the community.
Timbuktu's ancient libraries hold 700,000 medieval manuscripts on astronomy, medicine, and law.

Burkina Faso.tagline: Land of Upright People – Sahel Spirit, Colourful Culture, and Ancient Kingdoms 🇧🇫

Capital City 🏛️.text: Ouagadougou (pronounced Waga-doo-goo) is Burkina Faso's capital and largest city.
Burkina Faso means 'Land of Upright/Honest People' in Mossi and Dioula languages.
The country was renamed from Upper Volta to Burkina Faso in 1984 by revolutionary leader Thomas Sankara.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: W-Arly-Pendjari Complex – UNESCO transboundary park with lions, elephants, and hippos.
FESPACO Film Festival – The largest pan-African cinema festival, held in Ouagadougou every two years.
Ruins of Loropéni – UNESCO-listed ruins of a 1,000-year-old stone enclosure in the southwest.
Laongo Sculpture Symposium – An outdoor gallery of granite sculptures by African artists.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Gold – Burkina Faso is now Africa's 4th largest gold producer.
Cotton – A major cash crop and export.
Agriculture – Subsistence farming of sorghum, millet, and maize.
Livestock – Significant cattle herding economy.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Mooré (Mossi language) and Dioula are the most widely spoken.
Over 60 ethnic groups; the Mossi are the largest group with a long history of kingdom governance.
Thomas Sankara (1983–1987) was a revolutionary leader who promoted African pride and women's rights.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Burkina Faso covers 274,200 sq km in West Africa.
A landlocked country surrounded by Mali, Niger, Benin, Togo, Ghana, and Ivory Coast.
Mostly flat Sahel plateau with the Mouhoun (Black Volta), Nakambé (White Volta), and Nazinon rivers.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Burkina Faso's revolutionary president Thomas Sankara was once called 'Africa's Che Guevara' – he banned luxury cars and first-class air travel for ministers!
FESPACO in Ouagadougou is the world's largest African film festival.
Burkina Faso consistently ranks near the bottom on the Human Development Index despite its culturally rich people.

Senegal.tagline: Teranga Nation – Jazz, Wrestling, Pink Lake, and West Africa's Cultural Hub 🇸🇳

Capital City 🏛️.text: Dakar is Senegal's capital, the westernmost city of mainland Africa, on the Cape Verde Peninsula.
Dakar is West Africa's cultural and economic capital.
Senegal is one of Africa's most stable democracies, having peacefully transferred power multiple times.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Goree Island – A UNESCO World Heritage site, the main departure point for enslaved Africans to the Americas.
Lake Retba (Lac Rose) – A pink lake coloured by salt-loving algae, where salt is harvested by hand.
Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary – One of the world's most important bird sanctuaries, UNESCO-listed.
African Renaissance Monument – A 52m bronze statue in Dakar, taller than the Statue of Liberty!

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Fishing – Senegal has one of West Africa's most important fishing industries.
Phosphate & Gold – Growing mining sector.
Oil & Gas – Major offshore discoveries are being developed.
Tourism – Beaches, music culture, and history attract visitors.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Wolof is the lingua franca spoken by 80% of Senegalese.
'Teranga' (hospitality in Wolof) is Senegal's national value – guests are treated with extraordinary warmth.
Senegal is the birthplace of Afrobeat pioneers; Youssou N'Dour is a global music superstar.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Senegal covers 196,722 sq km in West Africa.
Almost entirely surrounds The Gambia; borders Mauritania, Mali, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea.
Has a 531 km Atlantic coast; the landscape transitions from Sahel to tropical forest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Senegal's Lac Rose (Pink Lake) is so salty that harvesters can walk on top of salt deposits to collect it.
The African Renaissance Monument in Dakar is taller than the Statue of Liberty!
Senegal has never had a military coup – remarkable stability in a region prone to instability.
Sadio Mané, one of football's biggest stars, grew up in rural Senegal and now funds schools and hospitals there.

Guinea.tagline: Water Tower of West Africa – Mountains, Rivers, and Mineral Wealth 🇬🇳

Capital City 🏛️.text: Conakry is Guinea's capital, on a peninsula in the Atlantic.
Guinea is called the 'Water Tower of West Africa' because major rivers (Niger, Senegal, Gambia) originate here.
Guinea has more than half of the world's bauxite reserves.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Fouta Djalon Highlands – A plateau of waterfalls, rivers, and traditional Fula villages.
Bossou Chimpanzees – A community of chimpanzees that uses stone tools, studied for decades.
Conakry Grand Mosque – One of West Africa's largest mosques.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Bauxite – Guinea has 25%+ of the world's bauxite reserves; key for aluminium production globally.
Gold & Diamonds – Significant mining sector.
Agriculture – Coffee, pineapples, and palm oil.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Pular (Fula), Mandinka, and Susu are major local languages.
The Fula (Peul) are the dominant group in the highlands; Mandinka and Susu in the coastal areas.
Guinea's music tradition – the djembe drum and kora lute – has influenced world music deeply.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Guinea covers 245,857 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Guinea-Bissau, Senegal, Mali, Ivory Coast, Liberia, and Sierra Leone.
The Fouta Djalon highlands are the source of three great West African rivers.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Guinea has more than half of the world's known bauxite reserves – every aluminium can may contain Guinean minerals.
The chimpanzees of Bossou use stone tools – one of the only communities of wild apes observed doing so.
Guinea's Fouta Djalon is called the 'Water Tower of West Africa' – source of the Niger, Senegal, and Gambia rivers.

Sierra Leone.tagline: Lion Mountain – Blood Diamonds Redeemed, Beaches, and Freetown Heritage 🇸🇱

Capital City 🏛️.text: Freetown is Sierra Leone's capital, founded in 1792 as a settlement for freed slaves.
Sierra Leone means 'Lion Mountain' in Portuguese.
Freetown's Cotton Tree is a 500-year-old kapok tree around which freed slaves gathered – a national symbol.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Tacugama Chimpanzee Sanctuary – A major rescue centre for orphaned chimps near Freetown.
Outamba-Kilimi National Park – Rainforest park with hippos, elephants, and chimpanzees.
Banana Islands – Beautiful secluded islands with colonial Portuguese ruins.
Tiwai Island – A unique river island wildlife sanctuary with 11 primate species.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Diamonds – Sierra Leone is a major diamond producer; conflict diamonds funded a devastating civil war.
Rutile & Bauxite – Major mineral exports.
Fisheries – Rich Atlantic waters provide significant catches.
Agriculture – Rice, coffee, cocoa, and palm oil.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; Krio (a creole language) is the most widely spoken lingua franca.
The Mende and Temne are the largest ethnic groups; over 16 ethnic groups total.
Krio culture – descendants of freed slaves from Britain, the Caribbean, and America – is a unique heritage.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Sierra Leone covers 71,740 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Guinea and Liberia, with an Atlantic coast.
The Western Area Peninsula has mountains, forests, and beaches in close proximity.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Sierra Leone has one of the world's highest concentrations of diamonds per square kilometre.
Freetown was founded in 1792 specifically as a home for freed slaves – the 'Province of Freedom'.
The world's largest natural diamond (Sergio, 3,106 carats) was found in neighbouring countries but Sierra Leone is famous for gem diamonds.
Sierra Leone's beaches are among Africa's finest but remain almost untouched by tourism.

Ivory Coast.tagline: Côte d'Ivoire – Cocoa Kingdom, Economic Powerhouse, and Cultural Pride 🇨🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: Yamoussoukro is the official capital; Abidjan is the economic capital and largest city.
Abidjan is West Africa's largest French-speaking city and economic powerhouse.
Ivory Coast produces over 40% of the world's cocoa – the chocolate in your candy bar starts here!

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, Yamoussoukro – The world's largest church by area, inspired by St Peter's in Rome.
Taï National Park – UNESCO World Heritage rainforest, one of the last primary West African rainforests.
Comoé National Park – UNESCO World Heritage savannah park with elephants, hippos, and lions.
Grand-Bassam – A UNESCO-listed colonial-era coastal town, Ivory Coast's first capital.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Cocoa – Ivory Coast produces 40-45% of the world's cocoa; the world's largest cocoa producer.
Coffee – A major coffee producer and exporter.
Palm Oil & Rubber – Significant plantation crops.
Gold & Manganese – Growing mining sector.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Dioula is the main lingua franca.
Over 60 ethnic groups including Akan, Gur, Mande, and Kru peoples.
Ivorian music – particularly Zouglou, Coupé-Décalé, and their DJ culture – is influential across Africa.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Ivory Coast covers 322,463 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Liberia, Guinea, Mali, Burkina Faso, and Ghana.
Southern coastline on the Gulf of Guinea; northern savannah, southern rainforest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Ivory Coast produces almost half the world's cocoa – every chocolate bar owes something to this country.
Yamoussoukro's Basilica is the world's largest Christian church by area (covering more than St Peter's in Rome).
Didier Drogba – one of football's greatest strikers – is a national hero and helped negotiate a ceasefire in Ivory Coast's civil war!

Togo.tagline: Little Country, Big Heart – Voodoo Culture, Lomé Markets, and Atlantic Beaches 🇹🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Lomé is Togo's capital, one of the few African capitals directly on the Atlantic Ocean coastline.
Togo is a long, narrow country stretching from the coast to the Sahel.
Lomé's Grand Marché is one of West Africa's largest markets, famous for its female traders (Nana Benz).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Koutammakou – UNESCO World Heritage landscape of the Batammariba's unique two-storey mud tower houses (Takienta).
Fazao-Malfakassa National Park – Rainforest reserve with elephants and buffalo.
Lomé Cathedral and Central Market – Heart of the capital's colonial-era centre.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Phosphate – Togo is a top phosphate producer in Africa.
Agriculture – Cotton, coffee, cocoa, and cassava.
Port of Lomé – A major deep-water port serving landlocked West African countries.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Ewe and Kabiye are national languages.
Togo has 37 ethnic groups; the Ewe in the south and Kabiye in the north are the main groups.
Togo has a strong Vodun (Voodoo) tradition; Lomé has an extraordinary Akodessewa Fetish Market with animal parts for traditional medicine.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Togo covers 56,785 sq km – one of Africa's narrowest countries.
Bordered by Ghana, Benin, and Burkina Faso, with a short Atlantic coast.
A strip of territory running north-south from the Atlantic to the Sahel.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Togo's Akodessewa Fetish Market in Lomé is the world's largest voodoo market, selling animal skulls, skins, and talismans.
The Koutammakou mud tower houses are UNESCO-listed – each tower represents a family's history.
Togo's Nana Benz businesswomen controlled the Dutch wax fabric trade across West Africa for decades.

Benin.tagline: Birthplace of Voodoo – Dahomey Kingdom, Slave Trade History, and Sacred Forests 🇧🇯

Capital City 🏛️.text: Porto-Novo is Benin's official capital; Cotonou is the largest city and economic hub.
Benin (formerly Dahomey) was the heart of the West African slave trade to the Americas.
Benin is the birthplace of Voodoo (Vodun) religion, which spread to Haiti and the Americas.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Royal Palaces of Abomey – UNESCO World Heritage site; former palaces of the Dahomey Kingdom decorated with bas-reliefs.
Ganvié – A 'Venice of Africa' lake village on stilts on Lake Nokoué, home to 30,000 people.
Route of Slaves, Ouidah – A 4km route from the slave market to the 'Gate of No Return' on the ocean.
Pendjari National Park – One of West Africa's best wildlife parks with lions, elephants, and hippos.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Cotton – Benin's most important cash crop.
Re-export Trade – Benin is a major trade hub, re-exporting goods to Nigeria and landlocked neighbours.
Agriculture – Yams, cassava, maize, and palm oil.
Fisheries – Lake and ocean fishing.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is official; Fon and Yoruba are widely spoken.
Benin has over 42 ethnic groups; Fon, Adja, Yoruba, and Bariba are the largest.
Vodun (Voodoo) is officially recognised as a religion in Benin – January 10 is National Voodoo Day!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Benin covers 112,622 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Togo, Burkina Faso, Niger, and Nigeria, with a short Atlantic coast.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Benin is the birthplace of Voodoo (Vodun) – January 10 is a national holiday celebrating Voodoo!
Ganvié, the 'Venice of Africa', is the largest lake village in Africa – built on stilts to avoid slave raiders who could not cross water.
The Dahomey Amazons – an all-female military regiment – were one of the world's most feared fighting forces in the 19th century.

Gambia.tagline: The Smiling Coast – Africa's Smallest Country Wrapped Around a River 🇬🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: Banjul is The Gambia's capital, one of Africa's smallest capitals.
The Gambia is Africa's smallest mainland country, a narrow strip of land along the Gambia River surrounded by Senegal.
The Gambia River is the country's lifeline – the entire country is essentially a river basin.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Kunta Kinteh Island (James Island) – UNESCO World Heritage former slave fort where the protagonist of 'Roots' was held.
Abuko Nature Reserve – A tiny but diverse forest reserve near Banjul with monkeys and crocodiles.
Bijilo Forest Park – A small urban park with green vervet monkeys that come right up to visitors.
River Gambia National Park – Home to chimpanzees on river islands.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – 'The Smiling Coast' beaches attract European winter sun seekers.
Fishing – Both river and ocean fishing are important.
Groundnuts (Peanuts) – The traditional main export crop.
Re-export Trade – Gambia is a trading hub for the region.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; Mandinka, Wolof, and Fula are the most spoken local languages.
The Gambians are famous for their warmth – 'The Smiling Coast of Africa' is not just tourism marketing!
Alex Haley's 'Roots' traced his ancestry to The Gambia – inspiring African Americans worldwide.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: The Gambia covers just 11,295 sq km – Africa's smallest mainland country.
Entirely surrounded by Senegal except for its Atlantic coastline.
The country is essentially just the Gambia River valley, 50 km wide at most.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Gambia is so narrow you can drive from one border to the other in under an hour!
Alex Haley traced his ancestry 'Roots' to Juffure village in The Gambia, inspiring a global TV phenomenon.
The Gambia has a 'crocodile pool' where sacred crocodiles live with humans in peace – you can sit on them!

Guinea-Bissau.tagline: Bijagos Archipelago – Hippo Islands, Cashew Capital, and Resilient Spirit 🇬🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bissau is Guinea-Bissau's capital, a small coastal city.
Guinea-Bissau is one of West Africa's smallest and least developed countries.
The Bijagos Archipelago – 88 islands off the coast – is one of West Africa's last great wildernesses.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Bijagos Archipelago – UNESCO Biosphere Reserve with hippos living in the sea, sea turtles, and manatees.
Orango Island – Famous for hippopotamuses that swim in saltwater – the only population in the world!
Cacheu River Natural Park – Mangrove forests and coastal wildlife.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Cashew Nuts – Guinea-Bissau is the world's 6th largest cashew producer.
Fishing – Rich Atlantic fishing grounds.
Agriculture – Subsistence farming; rice is the staple.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is official; Kriol (Guinea-Bissau Creole) and Balanta, Fula, and Mandinka languages are spoken.
Guinea-Bissau has 27 ethnic groups; Balanta, Fula, and Mandinka are the largest.
Gumbe music – a percussive folk tradition – is the national musical style.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Guinea-Bissau covers 36,125 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Senegal and Guinea, with an Atlantic coast and the 88-island Bijagos Archipelago.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Bijagos Islands have the world's only marine hippopotamuses – hippos that swim in the sea!
Guinea-Bissau is one of only 5 countries in the world to have Portuguese as an official language in Africa.
The country has had more coups than peaceful transitions of power since independence in 1974.

Liberia.tagline: Land of the Free – Africa's Oldest Republic, Rainforest, and Rubber Legacy 🇱🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Monrovia is Liberia's capital, named after US President James Monroe.
Liberia was founded in 1822 by freed American slaves and became Africa's first republic in 1847.
Liberia's flag closely resembles the US flag – a testament to its founding history.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sapo National Park – One of West Africa's largest remaining rainforests with pygmy hippos and chimpanzees.
Lake Piso – A coastal lagoon with manatees and birds.
Providence Island – Where the first freed American slaves landed in 1822.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Rubber – Liberia's Firestone plantation was once the world's largest rubber plantation.
Iron Ore – Major iron ore deposits.
Timber – Tropical hardwood logging.
Gold & Diamonds – Artisanal mining is widespread.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; 16 indigenous Liberian languages are spoken.
16 indigenous ethnic groups alongside the Americo-Liberian descendants of freed American slaves.
Liberian English has a distinctive West African rhythm and vocabulary.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Liberia covers 111,369 sq km in West Africa.
Bordered by Sierra Leone, Guinea, and Ivory Coast, with an Atlantic coast.
One of West Africa's most forested countries.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Liberia is Africa's oldest republic, founded in 1847 by freed American slaves.
The pygmy hippopotamus – a shy, forest-dwelling miniature hippo – is found mainly in Liberia.
Liberia's flag has 11 stripes and a lone star – directly modelled on the US flag by its American-born founders.

Cape Verde.tagline: Atlantic Crossroads – Volcanic Islands, Morna Music, and Creole Soul 🇨🇻

Capital City 🏛️.text: Praia on Santiago Island is Cape Verde's capital.
Cape Verde is an Atlantic archipelago of 10 islands discovered and settled by the Portuguese in 1456.
Cape Verde was a key stop on the transatlantic slave trade routes.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Pico do Fogo – An active volcano and Cape Verde's highest peak (2,829m) with a village inside the crater!
Cidade Velha – The first European colonial settlement in the tropics, UNESCO World Heritage.
Sal Island Beaches – Stunning Atlantic beaches with kite surfing and whale watching.
Santo Antão – A dramatic island of deep gorges, valleys, and lush hiking trails.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Cape Verde is a major Atlantic tourism destination, especially for Europeans.
Fishing – Tuna fishing in the Atlantic.
Remittances – Cape Verdean diaspora (larger than the home population) sends vital funds.
Renewable Energy – Cape Verde aims to be 100% renewable by 2025.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is official; Cape Verdean Creole (Kriolu) is the native tongue of all Cape Verdeans.
Cape Verdean Creole is a mix of Portuguese and West African languages, one of the world's oldest creoles.
Morna music – melancholic Atlantic blues – is UNESCO heritage; Cesária Évora was its global ambassador.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Cape Verde covers 4,033 sq km across 10 volcanic islands in the Atlantic, 570 km west of Senegal.
Semi-arid; some islands are lush and green, others are barren and volcanic.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: A village actually sits inside the active crater of Pico do Fogo volcano – and was buried by lava in 2014, then rebuilt!
Cape Verde's singer Cesária Évora performed barefoot on all stages worldwide as a statement for the poor.
Cape Verde has more citizens living abroad (diaspora) than living on the islands.

Mauritania.tagline: Land of the Moors – Ancient Caravans, Saharan Dunes, and Iron Railways 🇲🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Nouakchott is Mauritania's capital, one of Africa's youngest capitals, founded in 1958.
Mauritania stretches from the Sahara to the Atlantic, but over 90% is desert.
The Mauritania Iron Ore Railway is the world's longest train – up to 3 km long and 200+ wagons!

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Ancient Ksour (Chinguetti, Ouadane, Tichitt, Oualata) – UNESCO World Heritage desert trade cities with ancient Islamic libraries.
Banc d'Arguin National Park – UNESCO World Heritage; millions of migratory birds and monk seals on the Atlantic coast.
Chinguetti – One of Islam's seven holy cities, a Saharan oasis of ancient mosques and libraries.
Richat Structure (Eye of the Sahara) – A mysterious 50km circular geological formation visible from space.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Iron Ore – Major iron ore mining and export from Zouerate.
Fishing – Rich Atlantic fishing grounds.
Oil – Offshore oil production since 2006.
Gold – Growing gold sector.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Arabic is official; Hassaniya Arabic is the main spoken dialect.
Mauritania is an Arab-Berber (Moor) and sub-Saharan African country; Wolof, Soninke, and Pulaar are spoken in the south.
Mauritania only officially abolished slavery in 1981 – and criminalised it in 2007.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Mauritania covers 1.03 million sq km in northwest Africa.
Bordered by Morocco, Algeria, Mali, Senegal, and the Atlantic Ocean.
Over 90% desert; the Sahara covers most of the country.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Richat Structure (Eye of Africa) – a 50km wide circular rock formation in the Sahara – is so symmetrical some believe it's the mythical Atlantis!
Mauritania's iron ore train is one of the world's longest – passengers can ride for free in open iron ore wagons!
Chinguetti's ancient libraries hold thousands of medieval Islamic manuscripts on astronomy and medicine.

Mozambique.tagline: Indian Ocean Pearl – Coral Archipelagos, Prawns, and Maputaland Magic 🇲🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Maputo is Mozambique's capital, a vibrant port city with Portuguese colonial architecture.
Mozambique has the world's longest coastline on the Indian Ocean in southern Africa.
Mozambique was devastated by 15 years of civil war (1977–1992) and has been rebuilding since.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Quirimbas Archipelago – A chain of pristine coral islands in northern Mozambique.
Bazaruto Archipelago – Spectacular sand islands with dugongs, whale sharks, and coral reefs.
Gorongosa National Park – A park dramatically recovering its elephant and lion populations.
Ilha de Moçambique – UNESCO World Heritage island that was Portugal's East Africa capital for 400 years.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Natural Gas – Massive offshore gas discoveries are being developed in northern Mozambique.
Aluminium – The Mozal smelter is one of southern Africa's largest.
Cashew & Prawns – Premium Mozambican prawns and cashews are gourmet exports.
Coal – Tete province has massive coal reserves.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is official; Emakhuwa, Xichangana, Cisena, and 40+ other Bantu languages are spoken.
Mozambique has over 40 ethnic groups.
Marrabenta music and Mozambican prawn dishes are cultural icons.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Mozambique covers 801,590 sq km in Southeast Africa.
Bordered by Tanzania, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, and Eswatini.
Has a 2,470 km Indian Ocean coastline – one of Africa's longest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Mozambique's Bazaruto Archipelago has the last viable dugong (sea cow) population in the Indian Ocean.
The Mozambique Channel between Mozambique and Madagascar is a whale highway – humpback whales migrate here annually.
Mozambique discovered one of the world's largest natural gas fields in 2011, potentially transforming its economy.

Zimbabwe.tagline: Great Zimbabwe – Ancient Stone Kingdoms, Mighty Victoria Falls, and Resilient People 🇿🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Harare is Zimbabwe's capital, formerly known as Salisbury under British colonial rule.
Bulawayo in the south is Zimbabwe's second city and cultural capital.
Zimbabwe takes its name from Great Zimbabwe – a massive medieval stone city built without mortar.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Victoria Falls (Mosi-oa-Tunya) – One of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World; the world's largest waterfall by area.
Great Zimbabwe – A UNESCO World Heritage ancient stone city, once capital of a medieval African empire.
Hwange National Park – Zimbabwe's largest park with the largest elephant population on Earth.
Matobo Hills – UNESCO World Heritage landscape with ancient San rock art and Cecil Rhodes' grave.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Mining – Zimbabwe has the world's 2nd largest platinum reserves and significant gold, diamonds, and chromite.
Tobacco – Zimbabwe was once the world's largest tobacco exporter.
Tourism – Victoria Falls and safaris attract international visitors.
Agriculture – Maize, cotton, and sugarcane.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Zimbabwe has 16 official languages – the most of any African country – including Shona, Ndebele, and English.
The Shona and Ndebele are the main ethnic groups.
Zimbabwe stone sculpture (Shona sculpture) is internationally celebrated in galleries worldwide.
Chimurenga music, popularised by Thomas Mapfumo, is Zimbabwe's political musical tradition.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Zimbabwe covers 390,757 sq km in southern Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by Zambia, Mozambique, South Africa, Botswana, and Namibia.
The Zambezi River forms the northern border; the Limpopo River the southern border.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Zimbabwe had 100 trillion dollar notes – the highest denomination banknote ever printed, during its 2008 hyperinflation!
Victoria Falls is so powerful it creates its own permanent 'rain' in the rainforest below.
Great Zimbabwe's dry stone walls stand 11m high – built without mortar – by an African civilisation in the 11th century.
Zimbabwe has the world's second-largest platinum deposits after South Africa.

Zambia.tagline: Real Africa – Victoria Falls, Copper, and Untamed Wilderness 🇿🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: Lusaka is Zambia's capital and largest city, in the centre of the country.
Livingstone in the south is the gateway to Victoria Falls and named after explorer David Livingstone.
Zambia is one of Africa's most politically stable countries, with peaceful transfers of power.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Victoria Falls – Zambia shares the falls with Zimbabwe; the Zambian side offers a unique spray-soaked view.
South Luangwa National Park – One of Africa's finest safari parks, pioneering walking safaris.
Lower Zambezi National Park – Canoe safaris on the Zambezi River past elephants and hippos.
Kafue National Park – One of the world's largest national parks with incredible biodiversity.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Copper – Zambia is the world's 7th largest copper producer; the Copperbelt is a major mining region.
Cobalt – Significant cobalt production alongside copper.
Agriculture – Maize, tobacco, and cotton.
Tourism – Safaris and Victoria Falls.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, and 70+ other languages are spoken.
Zambia has over 70 ethnic groups; Bemba and Nyanja peoples are the largest.
Zambia pioneered the 'walking safari' – the most authentic way to experience African bush.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Zambia covers 752,618 sq km in southern Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by 8 countries: DRC, Tanzania, Malawi, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Namibia, and Angola.
The Zambezi River (1,700 miles long) begins in Zambia and flows to the Indian Ocean.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Zambia invented the walking safari – Kenneth Kaunda decreed that tourists would walk with guides in the bush, not just drive.
Victoria Falls produces such force that mist and spray rise 400m into the air, visible from 50 km away.
Zambia has 3 UNESCO World Heritage sites and is home to David Livingstone's grave and artifacts.
The Zambezi River starts in Zambia and is home to the famous Victoria Falls, one of the world's greatest natural wonders.

Malawi.tagline: Warm Heart of Africa – Lake Malawi, Smiling People, and Tea Highlands 🇲🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Lilongwe is Malawi's capital; Blantyre in the south is the commercial hub.
Malawi is called the 'Warm Heart of Africa' for its famously friendly people.
Lake Malawi is the jewel of the country – 580 km long and home to more fish species than any other lake.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lake Malawi (Lake Nyasa) – UNESCO World Heritage; 580 km long, 3rd largest African lake with 1,000+ fish species.
Mulanje Massif – A dramatic granite inselberg rising to 3,002m, shrouded in mist and cedar forests.
Nyika National Park – Africa's largest miombo woodland plateau with rolling hills and roan antelope.
Livingstonia – A historic Scottish mission town perched dramatically on the lakeshore escarpment.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tobacco – Malawi's main export, though dependence is declining.
Tea – Malawi produces some of Africa's finest teas in the Thyolo and Mulanje highlands.
Fishing – Lake Malawi's chambo and usipa fish are dietary staples.
Agriculture – Maize, sugar, and coffee.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Chichewa and English are official languages.
The Chewa are Malawi's dominant ethnic group; Yao, Lomwe, and Tumbuka are also significant.
Malawi is famous for the warmth and friendliness of its people – consistently noted by travellers as exceptional.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Malawi covers 118,484 sq km in southeast Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by Tanzania, Mozambique, and Zambia.
Lake Malawi occupies about one-fifth of the country's area.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lake Malawi contains more species of fish than any other lake in the world – many found nowhere else!
Lake Malawi is so clear and warm it's called 'the Lake of Stars' for how it reflects the night sky.
Malawi has a law called the 'Flatulence Act' – it's illegal to foul the air in public! (though rarely enforced)

Madagascar.tagline: Eighth Continent – Lemurs, Baobabs, and Evolution's Isolated Laboratory 🇲🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Antananarivo (Tana) is Madagascar's capital, a highland city with French colonial and Merina Kingdom architecture.
Madagascar is the world's 4th largest island, separated from Africa 88 million years ago.
90% of Madagascar's wildlife is found NOWHERE else on Earth.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Avenue of the Baobabs – A dirt road lined with ancient bottle-shaped baobab trees, a photography icon.
Tsingy de Bemaraha – UNESCO World Heritage; razor-sharp limestone forest called the 'Stone Forest'.
Ranomafana National Park – Cloud forest with golden bamboo lemurs and dozens of endemic species.
Nosy Be – A tropical island paradise off the northwest coast.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Vanilla – Madagascar produces 80% of the world's natural vanilla.
Cloves & Spices – Madagascar is a top clove producer.
Mining – Sapphires, chromite, and nickel are major exports.
Tourism – Ecotourism for lemurs and unique biodiversity.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Malagasy and French are official languages.
Malagasy people are a remarkable blend of Austronesian (from Borneo) and East African origin.
Famadihana ('turning of the bones') – a burial ritual where ancestors' bones are rewrapped in fresh cloth – is a unique Malagasy tradition.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Madagascar covers 587,041 sq km – the world's 4th largest island.
Located 400 km east of Mozambique in the Indian Ocean.
Separated from Africa 88 million years ago; evolution on the island has produced extraordinary endemic species.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Madagascar is sometimes called the '8th continent' because 90% of its wildlife is found nowhere else!
Lemurs – gentle primates with big eyes – evolved only on Madagascar after the island split from Africa.
Madagascar produces 80% of the world's natural vanilla!
The fossa – Madagascar's top predator – looks like a cross between a cat and a mongoose and eats lemurs.

Mauritius.tagline: Jewel of the Indian Ocean – Paradise Island, Dodo Legacy, and Multicultural Harmony 🇲🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Port Louis is Mauritius's capital, a busy multicultural port city.
Mauritius was uninhabited until the 16th century; Dutch, French, and British colonisers all occupied it.
The dodo bird – now a global symbol of extinction – lived only in Mauritius.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Black River Gorges National Park – Lush forests with rare Mauritian pink pigeon and echo parakeet.
Ganga Talao (Grand Bassin) – A sacred Hindu crater lake, the holiest site in Mauritius.
Blue Bay Marine Park – UNESCO Biosphere; pristine coral reef in a turquoise lagoon.
Le Morne Brabant – UNESCO World Heritage mountain used by escaped slaves as a refuge.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – One of the Indian Ocean's premier luxury beach destinations.
Financial Services – A major offshore financial centre for African investment.
Sugar – Once the entire economy; sugar is still produced in scenic estates.
Textiles – A significant textile manufacturing sector.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Mauritius has no indigenous people; it's a diverse nation of Indian, African, European, and Chinese descent.
English is official; Mauritian Creole is spoken by nearly everyone; French, Hindi, and Tamil are common.
Mauritius is celebrated as a model of multicultural harmony with no ethnic conflict.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Mauritius covers 2,040 sq km in the Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar.
A volcanic island with a coral reef surrounding most of the coastline.
Other islands including Rodrigues and the Agaléga Islands are part of Mauritius.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The dodo lived only in Mauritius – it was driven to extinction by 1681 after Dutch sailors arrived.
Mauritius has an 'underwater waterfall' optical illusion caused by sand cascading off a shelf into the deep ocean.
Mauritius built one of Africa's strongest economies through tourism and finance with almost no natural resources.
Mark Twain wrote: 'Mauritius was made first, and then heaven; and heaven was copied after Mauritius.'

Seychelles.tagline: Last Eden – Granite Islands, Coco de Mer, and Clearest Waters on Earth 🇸🇨

Capital City 🏛️.text: Victoria on Mahé Island is the Seychelles' capital and the world's smallest capital by population.
Seychelles is an archipelago of 115 islands in the Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar.
It was uninhabited until 1742 and has no indigenous population.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Aldabra Atoll – UNESCO World Heritage; the world's second-largest coral atoll with 152,000 Aldabra giant tortoises.
Vallée de Mai – UNESCO World Heritage; a primeval palm forest with the coco de mer – the world's largest seed.
Anse Source d'Argent, La Digue – Ranked one of the world's most beautiful beaches with signature granite boulders.
Cousin Island – A conservation success story where rare birds like the Seychelles warbler have recovered from near-extinction.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Seychelles' tourism per capita is among the world's highest; it drives 60% of GDP.
Tuna Fishing – Seychelles' Exclusive Economic Zone is one of the world's richest tuna fishing grounds.
Finance – An offshore financial services sector.
Coco de Mer – The rare giant nut from Vallée de Mai is exported as a luxury souvenir.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Seychellois Creole, English, and French are all official languages.
Seychellois people are of African, French, Indian, and Chinese descent.
Seychelles was the first country in Africa to protect over 30% of its ocean territory.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Seychelles covers 455 sq km of land across 115 islands – one of the world's smallest countries.
Located in the Indian Ocean, northeast of Madagascar.
The main granitic islands are among Earth's only oceanic granite islands – fragments of ancient Gondwana.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The coco de mer palm produces the world's largest seed – up to 25kg and shaped distinctively!
Seychelles' Aldabra Atoll has more giant tortoises than the Galápagos Islands.
Seychelles is the only country in the world where the coco de mer palm grows in the wild.
The Seychelles granitic islands are fragments of ancient Gondwana – they are 750 million years old!

Lesotho.tagline: Kingdom in the Sky – Highest Lowest Point, Pony Trekking, and Basotho Blankets 🇱🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Maseru is Lesotho's capital on the border with South Africa.
Lesotho is the only country in the world entirely surrounded by another single country (South Africa).
Lesotho is the highest country in the world – even its lowest point (1,400m) is above most countries' highest points!

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sani Pass – A dramatic mountain pass (2,874m) connecting Lesotho to South Africa by a rough gravel road.
Tsehlanyane National Park – Highland wilderness with a rare Drakensberg plateau ecosystem.
Maletsunyane Falls – One of Africa's highest single-drop waterfalls (192m).
Katse Dam – A massive arch dam in the Maluti Mountains, engineering marvel of southern Africa.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Water Export – The Lesotho Highlands Water Project exports water to South Africa.
Diamonds – Letšeng Mine produces some of the world's largest gem diamonds per tonne.
Textiles – Garment manufacturing for US and EU markets.
Livestock – Wool and mohair from sheep and Angora goats.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Sesotho and English are official languages.
The Basotho people are the only ethnic group; it is one of Africa's most homogeneous nations.
The Basotho blanket – worn draped around the body – is a national symbol and worn by the king on official occasions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Lesotho covers 30,355 sq km – entirely surrounded by South Africa.
An entirely mountainous country; even its lowest point (1,400m above sea level) is higher than most countries' capitals.
Part of the Drakensberg/Maluti mountain system.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lesotho is the highest country in the world – its lowest point (1,400m) is higher than any point in many European countries!
Letšeng Diamond Mine in Lesotho produces the highest percentage of large, top-quality diamonds of any mine in the world.
Lesotho is one of only three countries entirely surrounded by another country (along with Vatican and San Marino).

Eswatini.tagline: Kingdom of the Swazis – Royal Ceremonies, Crafts, and Hlane Wilderness 🇸🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Mbabane is Eswatini's administrative capital; Lobamba is the royal and legislative capital.
Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) is one of the world's last absolute monarchies, ruled by King Mswati III.
Eswatini renamed itself from Swaziland in 2018 to shed its colonial name.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mlilwane Wildlife Sanctuary – A peaceful reserve with hippos, zebras, and warthogs.
Hlane Royal National Park – Eswatini's largest park with elephants, lions, and rhinos.
Sibebe Rock – The world's second-largest exposed granite monolith after Uluru in Australia.
Mantenga Cultural Village – A living museum of traditional Swazi village life.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Sugar & Timber – Sugarcane plantations and pine forests are major industries.
Textiles – Garment manufacturing for export.
Handicrafts – Swazi candles, woven baskets, and glassware are exported worldwide.
Tourism – Royal ceremonies and wildlife.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Siswati and English are official languages.
The Swazi are a Bantu people with strong royal traditions.
Incwala (sacred kingship ceremony) and Umhlanga (Reed Dance) are the two most important national ceremonies.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Eswatini covers 17,364 sq km – one of Africa's smallest countries.
Landlocked, surrounded by South Africa on three sides and Mozambique to the east.
Ranges from highveld in the west to lowveld in the east.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Eswatini's Sibebe Rock is the world's second-largest exposed granite rock (after Uluru/Ayers Rock in Australia).
Eswatini has one of the world's highest HIV rates – over 27% of adults.
The Umhlanga (Reed Dance) ceremony sees 80,000 young women dance before the king – the world's largest annual ceremony of its kind.

Botswana.tagline: Jewel of the Kalahari – Okavango Delta, Diamonds, and Africa's Conservation Model 🇧🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Gaborone is Botswana's capital, a modern city that grew rapidly after independence in 1966.
Botswana went from one of the world's poorest countries at independence to a middle-income country thanks to diamonds.
Botswana is one of Africa's longest-running continuous democracies.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Okavango Delta – The world's largest inland delta; a UNESCO World Heritage oasis in the Kalahari desert.
Chobe National Park – The world's highest concentration of elephants – over 120,000!
Makgadikgadi Pans – One of the world's largest salt flats; flamingos breed here seasonally.
Moremi Game Reserve – Africa's first reserve to be created by indigenous people.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Diamonds – Botswana is the world's largest diamond producer by value; Jwaneng is the world's richest diamond mine.
Tourism – High-value, low-volume ecotourism is a carefully managed model.
Beef – Botswana beef is exported to the EU.
Financial Services – Growing services economy.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Setswana and English are official languages.
The Tswana are the main group; the San (Bushmen) are the indigenous people of the Kalahari.
The San have the world's oldest genetic lineage and the most diverse click-consonant language.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Botswana covers 581,730 sq km in southern Africa.
A landlocked country bordered by South Africa, Zimbabwe, Namibia, and Zambia.
The Kalahari Desert covers 70% of the country; the Okavango River flows into the desert creating the delta.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Okavango Delta is one of the world's only major rivers that flows INTO a desert instead of to the sea.
Botswana transformed itself from Africa's poorest at independence to one of its wealthiest – entirely through diamond revenues.
Botswana's Jwaneng mine is the world's richest diamond mine by value.
The San (Bushmen) speak the world's most ancient language – with click consonants that predate all other human languages.

Namibia.tagline: Land of Empty Spaces – Namib Desert, Red Dunes, and Desert-Adapted Wildlife 🇳🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Windhoek is Namibia's capital, a clean, modern city with a distinct German colonial character.
Namibia has the lowest population density of any country in the world outside of Mongolia.
Namibia has some of the world's most spectacular desert landscapes.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sossusvlei – The iconic red sand dunes of Namib-Naukluft (Dune 45, Big Daddy) are among the world's tallest and most photogenic.
Etosha National Park – A massive salt pan reserve; one of Africa's best for lion and elephant viewing.
Fish River Canyon – The world's second-largest canyon (after the Grand Canyon) carved by the Fish River.
Skeleton Coast – A treacherous fog-shrouded Atlantic coast littered with shipwrecks and seal colonies.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Diamonds – Namibia's coastal diamond fields (alluvial) produce some of the world's finest gem diamonds.
Mining – Uranium (major producer), zinc, copper, and gold.
Fishing – Walvis Bay is one of southern Africa's most important fishing ports.
Tourism – Sossusvlei, Etosha, and Damaraland attract adventure travellers.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; Oshiwambo, Nama/Damara, Afrikaans, and other languages are widely spoken.
Namibia has diverse peoples including Ovambo, Nama, Damara, Herero, San, and German-Namibian communities.
The Himba people of the north maintain their traditional way of life, coating their skin and hair with ochre paste.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Namibia covers 824,292 sq km in southern Africa.
Bordered by Angola, Zambia, Botswana, South Africa, and the Atlantic Ocean.
The Namib Desert (the world's oldest desert, 55 million years) runs along the entire coastline.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Namib Desert is the world's oldest desert – it has been arid for 55 million years!
Namibia's dunes at Sossusvlei are among the world's tallest – up to 325m high and turning glowing red at sunrise.
Namibia has more cheetahs than any country in the world – about 3,000 of the world's 7,000 cheetahs live here.
Namibia was the first country in the world to put environmental protection in its constitution (1990).

Angola.tagline: Sleeping Giant – Oil Wealth, Kalandula Falls, and Rising Phoenix 🇦🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Luanda is Angola's capital, one of Africa's most expensive cities due to its oil wealth.
Angola endured a devastating 27-year civil war (1975–2002) and has been rebuilding since.
Angola is Africa's 2nd largest oil producer (after Nigeria).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Kalandula Falls – One of Africa's largest waterfalls by volume, a spectacular cascade in the northern highlands.
Kissama National Park – Recovering wildlife reserve near Luanda with elephants, hippos, and giant sable antelope.
Tundavala Fissure – A breathtaking escarpment dropping 1,000m near Lubango.
Ilha do Mussulo – A beautiful spit of sand and lagoon near Luanda.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Africa's 2nd largest oil producer; oil accounts for 90% of exports.
Diamonds – Angola is a major diamond producer (Catoca is one of the world's largest mines).
Agriculture – Coffee was once a major export; rebuilding agricultural sector.
Construction – Massive post-war rebuilding created a construction boom.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is the official language – Angola was a Portuguese colony for 500 years.
The Ovimbundu, Mbundu, and Bakongo are the three main ethnic groups.
Kizomba and Semba – Angolan music and dance styles – have become globally popular.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Angola covers 1.25 million sq km in southwestern Africa.
Bordered by the DRC, Republic of Congo, Zambia, and Namibia, with an Atlantic coast.
Cabinda is an exclave separated from Angola by DRC territory.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Angola's giant sable antelope (palanca negra gigante) is found ONLY in Angola and is the country's national symbol.
Angola has Africa's longest Atlantic coastline at 1,650 km of beaches.
The Angolan civil war lasted 27 years, killing 500,000+ people – one of Africa's most devastating conflicts.
Luanda was ranked the world's most expensive city for expatriates in 2017!

Comoros.tagline: Perfume Islands – Ylang-Ylang, Volcanic Peaks, and Indian Ocean Crossroads 🇰🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: Moroni on Grande Comore is the capital of the Union of the Comoros.
Comoros is an archipelago of four volcanic islands between Madagascar and the East African coast.
Comoros has had more coups per capita than any other country in the world!

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mount Karthala – An active volcano and the highest point in Comoros (2,361m); one of the world's largest calderas.
Chomoni Beach – A beautiful volcanic black sand beach on Grande Comore.
The Old Friday Mosque, Moroni – One of the oldest mosques in sub-Saharan Africa.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Ylang-Ylang – Comoros produces 80% of the world's ylang-ylang, used in Chanel No. 5 perfume.
Cloves & Vanilla – Major spice exports.
Fishing – Tuna fishing in the Mozambique Channel.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Comorian (Shikomori), Arabic, and French are official languages.
Comorians are a blend of African, Arab, Malagasy, and Indian ancestry.
Islam is central to Comorian identity; Arabic schooling and Islamic courts are standard.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Comoros covers 2,235 sq km of land across four main volcanic islands.
Located between the northern tip of Madagascar and the coast of Mozambique.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Comoros produces 80% of the world's ylang-ylang – used in the world's most iconic perfumes including Chanel No. 5!
The coelacanth – a fish thought extinct for 65 million years – was rediscovered alive near Comoros in 1938!
Comoros has had over 20 coups or coup attempts since independence – one of the world's most coup-prone countries.

National Tree 🌳.text: Coco de Mer / Coconut Palm (Cocos nucifera)

São Tomé and Príncipe.tagline: Chocolate Islands – Cocoa Estates, Cloud Forests, and Equatorial Tranquility 🇸🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: São Tomé is the capital city and largest town of this twin-island nation.
São Tomé and Príncipe was uninhabited until Portuguese colonisers arrived in the 1470s.
These volcanic islands sit almost exactly on the Equator in the Gulf of Guinea.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Pico de São Tomé – The island's highest peak (2,024m), draped in cloud forest.
Rolas Island – A tiny island that lies precisely on the Equator, with a monument marking 0° latitude.
Roças and Plantations – Historic colonial cocoa estates that produced the world's finest cocoa.
Bom Bom Island Resort – A remote private island in pristine waters off Príncipe.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Cocoa – São Tomé once produced 20% of the world's cocoa; artisan chocolate is a growing premium export.
Fishing – Tuna and other fish in the Gulf of Guinea.
Oil – Offshore oil potential is being explored.
Tourism – Ecotourism to forests and beaches is growing.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is the official language.
Santomeans are descendants of African slaves and Portuguese settlers; Forro, Angolar, and Principense creole languages are spoken.
São Tomé is known for its fine chocolate and laid-back, friendly culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: São Tomé and Príncipe covers 1,001 sq km – Africa's second-smallest country.
Two volcanic islands in the Gulf of Guinea, 250 km off Gabon's coast.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: In the 1800s, São Tomé was the world's largest cocoa producer!
Rolas Island in São Tomé sits exactly on the Equator – you can stand on the line between the Northern and Southern hemispheres!
São Tomé's 'Principe' island was where Arthur Eddington proved Einstein's theory of relativity during the 1919 solar eclipse.

France.tagline: Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité – Art, Fashion, and Joie de Vivre 🇫🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Paris is the capital of France and one of the world's most visited cities.
Known as the 'City of Light', Paris is a global centre for art, culture, cuisine, and fashion.
Paris has been a capital for over 2,000 years, originally a Celtic settlement called 'Lutetia'.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Eiffel Tower – Built in 1889, this iron tower is the world's most visited paid monument.
Louvre Museum – The world's largest art museum, housing the Mona Lisa and Venus de Milo.
Palace of Versailles – A stunning royal palace with magnificent gardens near Paris.
Mont-Saint-Michel – A magical island abbey rising from the sea in Normandy.
French Riviera (Côte d'Azur) – A glamorous Mediterranean coastline loved by celebrities.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Luxury Goods – France leads the world in luxury brands: Louis Vuitton, Chanel, Hermès, and Dior.
Tourism – France is the world's most visited country, welcoming 90+ million tourists yearly.
Aerospace – Airbus is headquartered in France, competing with Boeing for the world's largest aircraft maker.
Wine & Food – French wine, cheese, and cuisine are considered world benchmarks of fine food.
Nuclear Energy – France generates over 70% of its electricity from nuclear power.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is the official language, spoken by 300 million people worldwide as a result of French history.
France is one of the world's most ethnically diverse countries, with large communities from Africa, Asia, and the Caribbean.
French culture prizes philosophy, literature, cinema, and culinary arts.
The French baguette, croissant, and café culture are iconic parts of daily life.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: France covers 643,801 sq km, making it the largest country in Western Europe.
Bordered by Belgium, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Spain, and has coasts on the Atlantic Ocean and Mediterranean Sea.
Landscape includes the Alps, Pyrenees, Loire Valley, and the flat plains of northern France.
France also includes overseas territories in the Caribbean, South America, and Pacific.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: France has won more Nobel Prizes in Literature than any other country.
The French invented the cinema in 1895 with the Lumière Brothers.
France has the most UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Western Europe.
Camembert, Brie, Roquefort – France produces over 1,200 types of cheese!

Germany.tagline: Land of Ideas – Engineering Excellence and Beer Gardens 🇩🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Berlin is Germany's capital and largest city, a vibrant hub of art, history, and nightlife.
Berlin was divided by a wall from 1961–1989 during the Cold War; the Berlin Wall's fall was a historic moment.
Frankfurt, Munich, and Hamburg are other major German cities with global significance.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Neuschwanstein Castle – A fairy-tale castle in the Bavarian Alps that inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty castle.
Brandenburg Gate – A neoclassical monument in Berlin, symbol of German reunification.
Cologne Cathedral – A towering Gothic masterpiece that took 632 years to complete.
Black Forest – A mysterious fairy-tale forest, home to cuckoo clocks and traditional villages.
Rhine Valley – A scenic river valley dotted with medieval castles, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Automobiles – Germany is home to BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Volkswagen, Porsche, and Audi.
Engineering & Machinery – German engineering is world-renowned for precision and quality.
Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals – BASF, Bayer, and Merck are global leaders based in Germany.
Renewable Energy – Germany leads Europe in wind and solar energy production.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: German is the official language, spoken by 130+ million people as a native language in Europe.
Germany is home to 84 million people with large Turkish, Polish, and Syrian communities.
Oktoberfest in Munich is the world's largest folk festival, celebrating Bavarian culture with beer and music.
Germany gave the world Beethoven, Bach, Goethe, and Gutenberg (inventor of the printing press).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Germany covers 357,114 sq km in Central Europe.
Bordered by 9 countries: Denmark, Poland, Czech Republic, Austria, Switzerland, France, Luxembourg, Belgium, and Netherlands.
Northern Germany is flat plains; the south has the Bavarian Alps.
The Rhine, Elbe, and Danube are major rivers flowing through Germany.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Germany has over 1,500 different types of beer and 1,300 breweries!
The autobahn is Germany's famous highway system where some sections have no speed limit.
Germany invented the car, aspirin, the printing press, and the MP3 format!
Germans love bread – there are over 3,200 different types of bread in Germany.

United Kingdom.tagline: Great Britain – Rule the Waves, Lead the World 🇬🇧

Capital City 🏛️.text: London is the capital of the United Kingdom and one of the world's most influential cities.
It is home to Buckingham Palace, the Houses of Parliament, and the Tower of London.
The UK comprises four countries: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Big Ben & Houses of Parliament – The iconic clock tower beside the River Thames.
Stonehenge – A mysterious prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire, built over 5,000 years ago.
Edinburgh Castle – A dramatic castle perched on volcanic rock in Scotland's capital.
Buckingham Palace – The official royal residence of the British monarch.
Lake District – A stunning landscape of mountains and lakes in northern England.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Financial Services – London is one of the world's leading financial centres.
Creative Industries – Music, film, fashion, and media (BBC, Harry Potter, James Bond).
Aerospace & Defence – UK is a major manufacturer of aircraft engines (Rolls-Royce).
Pharmaceuticals – GSK and AstraZeneca are global pharmaceutical giants.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English originated in England and is now the world's most widely spoken language.
Welsh, Scottish Gaelic, Irish, and Cornish are also spoken by native communities.
The UK is incredibly multicultural with communities from every corner of the world.
British culture includes tea time, cricket, football, and the unique institution of the Royal Family.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: The UK covers 242,495 sq km, comprising the island of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.
Surrounded by the Atlantic Ocean, North Sea, English Channel, and Irish Sea.
Scotland has stunning Highlands and lochs; England has rolling countryside and the Peak District.
No point in the UK is more than 113 km from the sea.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The UK invented football (soccer), cricket, rugby, tennis, and golf!
The British Empire was once the largest empire in history, covering 25% of the world's land.
Shakespeare wrote 37 plays and invented over 1,700 words we use today, including 'lonely', 'bedroom', and 'generous'.
The London Underground (Tube) is the world's oldest metro system, opened in 1863.

National Animal 🐾.text: Lion (Panthera leo) – England; Red Dragon – Wales; Unicorn – Scotland

National Flower 🌸.text: Tudor Rose (England), Thistle (Scotland), Daffodil (Wales), Shamrock (N. Ireland)

Italy.tagline: Boot of Europe – Where Art, Food, and History are Everywhere 🇮🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Rome is Italy's capital and the 'Eternal City', with 2,800 years of continuous history.
Vatican City, the world's smallest country, sits entirely within Rome.
Italy was unified as a single nation only in 1861, before which it was many separate kingdoms.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Colosseum – A giant ancient amphitheatre in Rome where gladiators once fought.
Leaning Tower of Pisa – A campanile that leans at a 4-degree angle, begun in 1173.
Venice – A magical city built on 118 islands, connected by canals instead of roads.
Sistine Chapel – Michelangelo's breathtaking ceiling paintings in Vatican City.
Amalfi Coast – A stunning stretch of Mediterranean coastline with colourful cliffside villages.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Fashion & Design – Milan is the world's fashion capital; Gucci, Prada, Armani, and Versace are Italian.
Automobiles – Ferrari, Lamborghini, Maserati, and Alfa Romeo are all made in Italy.
Food & Wine – Italian cuisine (pizza, pasta, gelato) is the world's most popular.
Tourism – Italy is the 5th most visited country, drawing visitors to its art and history.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Italian is the official language, spoken by 65 million people.
Regional dialects like Venetian, Sicilian, and Neapolitan are still spoken.
Italy is the birthplace of the Renaissance – a golden age of art, science, and architecture.
Italian passion for family (la famiglia), food, football, and opera defines the culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Italy covers 301,340 sq km and is shaped like a high-heeled boot, jutting into the Mediterranean Sea.
The Alps form the northern border; the Apennine Mountains run through the centre.
Contains two independent states: Vatican City (smallest country) and San Marino.
Major islands: Sicily and Sardinia.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the world – 58 sites!
Pizza was invented in Naples, Italy, in the 18th century.
Leonardo da Vinci, Galileo, Columbus, and Marco Polo were all Italian!
Italy has 3 active volcanoes: Etna, Vesuvius, and Stromboli.

Russia.tagline: The Great Bear – Vast Lands, Deep History, Arctic Power 🇷🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Moscow is Russia's capital, the political and cultural centre of the country.
The Kremlin – a fortified complex – houses the President's offices and is the heart of Russian power.
St. Petersburg, the former imperial capital, is known as the 'Venice of the North' for its canals.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Red Square & St. Basil's Cathedral – Moscow's iconic square with its colourful onion-dome cathedral.
Lake Baikal – The world's deepest lake, containing 20% of the world's fresh surface water.
Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg – One of the world's largest art museums with 3 million items.
Trans-Siberian Railway – The world's longest railway, stretching 9,289 km across Russia.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Natural Resources – Russia holds the world's largest reserves of natural gas and is a top oil exporter.
Space Technology – Russia launched the first satellite (Sputnik) and first human (Gagarin) into space.
Military Technology – Russia produces advanced fighter jets, missiles, and submarines.
Agriculture – Russia is the world's largest wheat exporter.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Russian is the official language and the most spoken Slavic language in the world.
Russia has over 185 ethnic groups including Tatars, Ukrainians, Bashkirs, and Chechen peoples.
Russian literature is world-famous – Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Chekhov, and Pushkin are literary giants.
Ballet, classical music, and folk traditions are deeply rooted in Russian culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Russia covers 17.1 million sq km – by far the world's largest country, spanning 11 time zones!
Stretches from Eastern Europe across all of northern Asia to the Pacific Ocean.
Contains diverse biomes: Arctic tundra, Siberian taiga (largest forest on Earth), steppes, and mountains.
The Ural Mountains divide European Russia from Asian Russia (Siberia).

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Russia is so big it spans 11 time zones – when it's breakfast in Moscow, it's dinnertime in Vladivostok!
The Siberian taiga is the world's largest forest, bigger than the Amazon rainforest.
Russia launched the first ever satellite into space in 1957 and the first human in 1961.
Lake Baikal is so deep it could hold all of the Great Lakes in North America combined.

Greece.tagline: Cradle of Democracy – Ancient Wisdom, Turquoise Seas 🇬🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Athens is Greece's capital and one of the world's oldest cities, inhabited for over 3,000 years.
The Acropolis – a rocky hill with ancient temples – dominates Athens' skyline.
Athens was the birthplace of democracy, philosophy, theatre, and the Olympic Games.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: The Parthenon – An ancient temple atop the Acropolis, dedicated to goddess Athena, built in 447 BC.
Santorini – A volcanic island with iconic white-and-blue buildings perched on clifftops.
Delphi – Ancient oracle site in the mountains, once considered the centre of the world.
Meteora – Incredible monasteries built on top of towering rock pillars.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Shipping – Greece has the world's largest merchant shipping fleet.
Tourism – Greece attracts over 33 million tourists yearly to its islands and ancient sites.
Olive Oil & Olives – Greece is the world's 3rd largest olive oil producer.
Agriculture – Feta cheese, honey, and wine are globally recognised Greek products.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Greek is one of the world's oldest recorded languages, spoken for over 3,000 years.
Greek mythology (Zeus, Athena, Poseidon) has shaped Western literature, art, and science.
Greek philosophers – Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle – laid the foundations of Western thought.
Greeks are known for their warmth, love of food (mezze, souvlaki, baklava), and lively family gatherings.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Greece covers 131,957 sq km in southeastern Europe, surrounded by three seas.
Has over 6,000 islands, of which about 227 are inhabited.
80% of Greece is mountainous; Mount Olympus (2,917m) is the highest peak and home of the Greek gods in mythology.
Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers and mild winters.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Greece is the birthplace of the Olympic Games, first held in Olympia in 776 BC.
The Greek alphabet is the ancestor of Latin and most European alphabets used today.
Greece has the longest coastline in Europe due to its many islands.
More than 160,000 English words come from Greek origins!

Spain.tagline: Passion and Fiesta – Flamenco, Football, and Sun-Drenched Coasts 🇪🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Madrid is Spain's capital and largest city, home to world-class art museums and a royal palace.
Barcelona, on the Mediterranean coast, is famous for Antoni Gaudí's surreal architecture.
Spain has 17 autonomous communities, each with distinct culture, food, and traditions.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sagrada Família, Barcelona – Gaudí's extraordinary unfinished cathedral, under construction since 1882.
Alhambra, Granada – A stunning Moorish palace complex with intricate Islamic art and gardens.
Prado Museum, Madrid – One of the world's greatest art museums with works by Velázquez, Goya, and El Greco.
Camino de Santiago – A medieval pilgrimage route walked by hundreds of thousands each year.
Costa del Sol & Balearic Islands – Sun-soaked beaches and islands beloved by tourists worldwide.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Spain is the world's 2nd most visited country, welcoming 80+ million tourists a year.
Olive Oil – Spain is the world's largest olive oil producer.
Automotive – Major European car manufacturer with SEAT, Ford, and Volkswagen factories.
Fashion & Design – Zara (Inditex) is the world's largest fashion retailer, headquartered in Spain.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Castilian Spanish is the official language; Catalan, Galician, and Basque are also official in their regions.
Spain exported the Spanish language to the Americas; 500 million people worldwide speak Spanish.
Flamenco – a passionate dance of guitar, singing, and footwork – is UNESCO-recognised cultural heritage.
Siesta (afternoon rest), tapas culture, and late-night dining are beloved Spanish traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Spain covers 505,990 sq km, the 4th largest country in Europe.
Located on the Iberian Peninsula, bordered by France, Portugal, Andorra, and Gibraltar.
Coastlines on the Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea, and Bay of Biscay.
The Pyrenees Mountains form a natural border with France; the Canary Islands are in the Atlantic near Africa.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Spain has the most UNESCO Biosphere Reserves of any country in the world.
