La Tomatina – an annual festival where people throw 150,000 tomatoes at each other – takes place in Buñol!
Spain's Real Madrid and FC Barcelona are among the world's two most valuable football clubs.
Don Quixote by Miguel de Cervantes is considered the world's first modern novel, written in Spain in 1605.

Portugal.tagline: Nation of Navigators – Fado, Pastéis, and the Edge of the World 🇵🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Lisbon is Portugal's capital, one of Europe's oldest cities, built on seven hills overlooking the Tagus river.
Porto is the 2nd city, famous for port wine, colourful tiled buildings, and the Douro River valley.
Lisbon was the capital of one of history's greatest maritime empires, reaching from Brazil to Japan.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Tower of Belém – A 16th-century fortified tower from which explorers set sail into the unknown.
Jerónimos Monastery – A UNESCO World Heritage Manueline-style monastery in Lisbon.
Pena Palace, Sintra – A fairy-tale colourful palace on a rocky peak, visible from Lisbon.
Douro Valley – UNESCO-listed terraced vineyards producing the world's great port and Douro wines.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Cork – Portugal produces over 50% of the world's cork, from ancient cork oak forests.
Tourism – Lisbon, Algarve beaches, and Douro Valley attract growing numbers of visitors.
Renewable Energy – Portugal regularly generates 100% of its electricity from renewables for days at a time.
Wine & Food – Port wine, Vinho Verde, bacalhau (salted cod), and pastéis de nata are world-famous.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is spoken by 260 million people worldwide – from Brazil to Mozambique to Macau.
Fado – a melancholic music tradition of saudade (longing) – is UNESCO world heritage.
The Portuguese were the first Europeans to reach India, Japan, and Brazil.
Portuguese culture values family, the sea, and a laid-back warmth called 'saudade'.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Portugal covers 92,212 sq km on the Iberian Peninsula, the westernmost country of mainland Europe.
Bordered only by Spain, with a long Atlantic Ocean coastline.
Includes the Azores and Madeira islands in the Atlantic Ocean.
Cape Roca is the westernmost point of continental Europe – once believed to be the 'Edge of the World'.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Portugal is the world's oldest nation-state with borders unchanged since 1139!
The Portuguese navigator Ferdinand Magellan led the first voyage to circumnavigate the Earth.
Portugal produces more cork than the rest of the world combined.
Vasco da Gama was the first European to reach India by sea, opening the lucrative spice trade in 1498.

Netherlands.tagline: Land of Tulips – Windmills, Masters, and the World's Cyclists 🇳🇱

Capital City 🏛️.text: Amsterdam is the constitutional capital and most famous city, known for its canals, museums, and bicycles.
The Hague is the seat of government, parliament, and home to the International Court of Justice.
Rotterdam has the largest port in Europe and is known for bold, innovative architecture.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Keukenhof Gardens – The world's largest flower garden with 7 million tulip and spring bulbs.
Rijksmuseum – Home to Rembrandt's Night Watch and Vermeer's masterpieces.
Kinderdijk Windmills – 19 historic windmills in a UNESCO-listed polder landscape.
Anne Frank House – Where Anne Frank hid during WWII and wrote her world-famous diary.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Port of Rotterdam – The largest port in Europe, handling 7 million containers a year.
Flowers & Horticulture – Netherlands is the world's largest flower exporter; the global flower auction is in Aalsmeer.
Technology & Semiconductors – ASML makes the machines that make all the world's advanced microchips.
Agriculture – Netherlands is the world's 2nd largest food exporter despite being a small country!

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Dutch (Nederlands) is the official language, spoken by 23 million people.
The Dutch are the world's tallest people on average, standing 182.9cm for men.
Cycling is a way of life – there are more bikes than people in the Netherlands!
Dutch Golden Age (1600s) produced Rembrandt, Vermeer, and the Dutch East India Company – one of history's most powerful corporations.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Netherlands covers 41,543 sq km in northwestern Europe – one of the world's most densely populated countries.
About 26% of the country is below sea level, held back by an elaborate system of dikes and pumps.
Bordered by Germany, Belgium, and the North Sea.
Ongoing land reclamation from the sea has created new land areas called 'polders'.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Netherlands reclaimed land from the sea to create entire provinces – 26% of the country is below sea level!
The Dutch invented the stock market in 1602 with the Dutch East India Company's first public shares.
There are 23 million bicycles for 17 million people in the Netherlands.
Van Gogh, Rembrandt, and Vermeer are all Dutch masters who changed the history of art.

Sweden.tagline: Nordic Spirit – Vikings, ABBA, IKEA, and Midnight Sun 🇸🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Stockholm is Sweden's capital, built across 14 islands where Lake Mälaren meets the Baltic Sea.
Known as the 'Venice of the North' for its water-surrounded old town (Gamla Stan).
Stockholm hosts the annual Nobel Prize ceremonies every December.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Gamla Stan (Old Town) – Stockholm's medieval island city with cobblestone streets and coloured buildings.
ICEHOTEL, Jukkasjärvi – A hotel rebuilt from ice every winter, the world's first ice hotel.
Abisko National Park – One of the world's best places to see the Northern Lights.
Vasa Museum – A perfectly preserved 17th-century warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Innovation – Sweden has the most unicorn companies (billion-dollar startups) per capita in the world.
IKEA, Spotify, H&M, Volvo, and Ericsson are all Swedish global brands.
Forestry & Paper – Major exporter of timber and paper products.
Defence & Engineering – Advanced defence technology and precision manufacturing.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Swedish is the official language; English is spoken fluently by almost all Swedes.
The Sami people are Sweden's indigenous reindeer-herding community in the far north.
Swedish culture values equality (Lagom – moderation and balance), nature, and design.
ABBA, Robyn, Avicii, and Zara Larsson – Sweden punches way above its weight in pop music globally.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Sweden covers 450,295 sq km in northern Europe on the Scandinavian Peninsula.
Borders Norway and Finland; has long coastlines on the Baltic Sea.
Covered 63% by boreal forests; thousands of lakes and islands dot the landscape.
Above the Arctic Circle, Sweden experiences the midnight sun in summer and polar night in winter.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Sweden gave the world IKEA, Spotify, Minecraft, Skype, and the safety match!
Sweden has 270,000 islands – and Swedes have the legal 'right to roam' anywhere in nature.
Sweden is one of the world's most equal societies and consistently ranks among the happiest countries.
Alfred Nobel – who invented dynamite – was Swedish; he created the Nobel Prizes to leave a peaceful legacy.

Poland.tagline: Phoenix Nation – Resilience, Pierogi, and Chopin's Soul 🇵🇱

Capital City 🏛️.text: Warsaw is Poland's capital, completely rebuilt after being 85% destroyed in World War II.
Krakow is Poland's former royal capital and one of Europe's most beautifully preserved medieval cities.
Poland was erased from the map for 123 years (1795–1918) and still survived as a nation through culture and spirit.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Wawel Castle, Krakow – The royal castle of Poland's kings on a limestone hill above the Vistula river.
Auschwitz-Birkenau – The largest Nazi concentration camp, now a UNESCO site and solemn memorial.
Wieliczka Salt Mine – A UNESCO site with underground chapels, chandeliers, and lakes carved entirely in salt.
Białowieża Forest – Europe's last primeval forest, home to the European bison.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Manufacturing – Poland is a major European manufacturer of cars, furniture, and electronics.
IT & Technology – Warsaw and Krakow are major tech hubs attracting global companies.
Agriculture – Poland is a top European producer of apples, potatoes, and dairy.
Coal & Energy – Poland is the EU's largest coal producer, transitioning to renewables.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Polish is the official language, known for its complex grammar and consonant clusters.
Poland is almost ethnically homogeneous today – over 97% Polish – a result of WWII's terrible changes.
Polish culture gave the world Chopin (composer), Copernicus (astronomer), and Marie Curie (scientist).
Pierogi (dumplings), żurek soup, bigos, and kielbasa sausage are beloved Polish dishes.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Poland covers 312,696 sq km in central Europe.
Bordered by Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, and Russia (Kaliningrad).
The North European Plain gives Poland mostly flat terrain with the Tatra Mountains in the south.
The Vistula and Oder are Poland's two major rivers.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Marie Curie, the only person to win Nobel Prizes in TWO different sciences, was Polish!
Copernicus, who proved the Earth revolves around the Sun, was Polish.
Poland was invaded and occupied by Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union simultaneously in 1939.
Warsaw's Old Town was rebuilt brick by brick after WWII using 18th-century paintings as blueprints!

Ukraine.tagline: Sunflower Heartland – Breadbasket of Europe and Brave Spirit 🇺🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Kyiv (Kiev) is Ukraine's capital, one of Eastern Europe's oldest cities with over 1,500 years of history.
Kyiv was the capital of the ancient Kyivan Rus state, the predecessor of modern Russia and Ukraine.
Kharkiv, Dnipro, and Lviv are other major Ukrainian cities with distinct characters.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Saint Sophia Cathedral, Kyiv – An 11th-century UNESCO World Heritage cathedral with golden domes.
Kyiv Pechersk Lavra (Monastery of the Caves) – A stunning monastery complex with underground caves.
Lviv Old Town – A beautifully preserved Central European city centre, UNESCO-listed.
Carpathian Mountains – A beautiful mountain range with skiing, hiking, and traditional villages.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Ukraine is called the 'Breadbasket of Europe', producing 10% of the world's wheat.
IT Industry – Kyiv is a major global tech hub with thousands of software developers.
Steel & Mining – Rich iron ore deposits and major steel production capacity.
Sunflower Oil – Ukraine is the world's largest exporter of sunflower oil.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Ukrainian is the official language; Russian is widely spoken especially in eastern cities.
Ukrainians are the largest Slavic people by national borders after Russians.
Embroidery (vyshyvanka), hopak dance, and bandura music are treasured cultural traditions.
Ukrainian cuisine includes borscht (beetroot soup), varenyky (dumplings), and salo (cured fat).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Ukraine covers 603,550 sq km, the largest country entirely within Europe.
Bordered by Russia, Belarus, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, and Moldova.
The vast Pontic steppe – fertile flat grasslands – has made Ukraine one of the world's most productive farmlands.
The Danube delta and Black Sea coastline are in the south.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Ukraine is the largest country located entirely within Europe.
Ukraine's flag – blue and yellow – represents the sky above the golden wheat fields.
The Chernobyl nuclear disaster (1986) happened in northern Ukraine and created an accidental wildlife refuge.
Ukraine has 7 UNESCO World Heritage Sites and has produced world chess champions, scientists, and artists.

Norway.tagline: Land of Fjords – Vikings, Northern Lights, and the Happiest Nation 🇳🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Oslo is Norway's capital, a modern city surrounded by fjords and forested hills.
Bergen is Norway's 'gateway to the fjords', a colourful Hanseatic port city.
Norway consistently ranks as one of the world's wealthiest and happiest countries.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Geirangerfjord – UNESCO World Heritage fjord with dramatic waterfalls and sheer cliff walls.
Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) – Norway's Tromsø and Lofoten are among the world's best viewing spots.
Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock) – A flat-topped cliff 604m above Lysefjord.
Lofoten Islands – Dramatic archipelago of fishing villages, jagged peaks, and midnight sun.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – Norway is Western Europe's largest oil producer; the Government Pension Fund is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund ($1.4 trillion).
Fisheries – Norway is the world's 2nd largest seafood exporter; salmon farming was pioneered here.
Hydropower – 98% of Norway's electricity comes from hydropower.
Maritime & Shipping – Major global shipping and shipbuilding nation.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Norwegian is the official language; Sami is co-official in several municipalities.
The Sami are Norway's indigenous reindeer-herding people of the Arctic north.
Norwegian culture values friluftsliv (outdoor life) – hiking, skiing, and time in nature is a national philosophy.
Norway gave the world the Nobel Peace Prize – the ceremony is held in Oslo every December.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Norway covers 385,207 sq km in northern Europe on the Scandinavian Peninsula.
Has one of the world's longest coastlines at 83,000 km including fjords and islands.
Shares the Scandinavian Peninsula with Sweden and Finland.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Norway saved up its oil wealth – its sovereign fund is the world's largest at $1.4 trillion (worth $250,000 per Norwegian citizen)!
Norway has 1,190 fjords – formed when glaciers carved valleys that filled with seawater.
Svalbard (part of Norway) requires you to carry a rifle outside settlements because of polar bear encounters!
Norway has given away more Nobel Peace Prizes than any institution in history.

Denmark.tagline: Happiest Kingdom – Hygge, LEGO, Vikings, and Fairytale Castles 🇩🇰

Capital City 🏛️.text: Copenhagen is Denmark's capital, a beautifully liveable city of canals, bicycles, and world-class design.
Denmark is a constitutional monarchy; Queen Margrethe II recently abdicated in favour of King Frederik X.
Denmark consistently tops global happiness rankings.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Nyhavn – Copenhagen's iconic coloured canal houses, once a sailors' quarter.
The Little Mermaid statue – A tiny but world-famous bronze statue in Copenhagen Harbour.
Kronborg Castle – The real castle that inspired Shakespeare's Hamlet.
LEGOLAND, Billund – The original LEGO theme park, near the town where LEGO was invented.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Wind Energy – Denmark is a world leader in wind energy; Vestas and Ørsted are global companies.
Pharmaceuticals – Novo Nordisk (diabetes and obesity drugs) is Europe's most valuable company.
Food & Agriculture – Bacon, cheese, and craft beer; Denmark produces 5x more pork than its population eats.
Shipping – Maersk is the world's largest container shipping company, Danish-owned.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Danish is the official language, closely related to Norwegian and Swedish.
'Hygge' – the Danish concept of cosy togetherness and contentment – has become a global lifestyle trend.
Denmark is home to one of Europe's oldest royal families (1,000+ years).
Hans Christian Andersen (The Little Mermaid, The Ugly Duckling) and Søren Kierkegaard were Danish.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Denmark covers 43,094 sq km on the Jutland Peninsula and 100 islands.
Bordered by Germany to the south; sea borders with Sweden and Norway.
Includes Greenland and the Faroe Islands as autonomous territories.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: LEGO was invented in Denmark in 1932 – 'LEGO' comes from Danish 'leg godt' meaning 'play well'.
Denmark's Greenland is the world's largest island (if you don't count Australia as an island).
Denmark is the world's happiest country according to multiple UN World Happiness Reports.
Denmark gets over 50% of its electricity from wind power.

Finland.tagline: Land of a Thousand Lakes – Sauna Nation, Santa's Home, and Northern Lights 🇫🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: Helsinki is Finland's capital, a design-forward city on a Baltic Sea peninsula with neo-classical architecture.
Rovaniemi in Lapland is the official hometown of Santa Claus.
Finland is the world's happiest country according to the 2023 UN World Happiness Report (7 years running).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Suomenlinna Sea Fortress – UNESCO World Heritage island fortress guarding Helsinki Harbour.
Santa Claus Village, Rovaniemi – Exactly on the Arctic Circle; you can meet Santa and cross the line.
Koli National Park – Forested hills overlooking Lake Pielinen; inspiration for Finnish national romanticism.
Nuuksio National Park – Forested lakes just 30 minutes from Helsinki centre.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Technology – Nokia, Linux, and Rovio (Angry Birds) are Finnish innovations.
Paper & Timber – Finland has 75% forest cover; a major pulp and paper producer.
Design & Engineering – Finnish design (Marimekko, Fiskars, Iittala) is world-renowned.
Clean Technology – A global leader in clean tech and renewable energy solutions.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Finnish and Swedish are both official languages.
Finnish is unrelated to most European languages; it's part of the Uralic language family.
Sauna is Finland's greatest cultural institution – there are 3.3 million saunas for 5.5 million Finns!
The Sami (Saami) are Finland's indigenous people of the north.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Finland covers 338,145 sq km in northern Europe.
Bordered by Sweden, Norway, Russia, and the Baltic Sea/Gulf of Finland.
Has 188,000 lakes – one of the world's most lake-rich countries.
One-third of Finland lies above the Arctic Circle.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Finland is the world's happiest country (7 consecutive years in the UN ranking).
Finland has 3.3 million saunas – more than one per household!
Santa Claus's official home is in Rovaniemi, Finland, exactly on the Arctic Circle.
Finland was the first country to give women full political rights (vote AND stand for election) in 1906.

Austria.tagline: Alpine Republic – Mozart, Schnitzel, Skiers, and the Habsburg Empire 🇦🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Vienna is Austria's capital, the former centre of the vast Habsburg Empire and a city of palaces, opera, and coffee houses.
Vienna is consistently ranked the world's most liveable city.
Salzburg is Mozart's birthplace and the setting for The Sound of Music.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Schönbrunn Palace – The Habsburg imperial summer palace with 1,441 rooms, UNESCO World Heritage.
St Stephen's Cathedral (Stephansdom) – Vienna's Gothic heart, 137m high.
Hohensalzburg Castle – One of the world's best-preserved medieval castles, dominating Salzburg.
Hallstatt – A picturesque alpine lake village, one of the world's most photographed places.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Alpine skiing, Vienna's culture, and the Sound of Music trail attract millions.
Banking & Finance – Vienna is a major banking centre.
Industry – Steel, machinery, chemicals, and electronics.
Agriculture – Wine (Grüner Veltliner), cheese, and Wiener Schnitzel culture.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: German is the official language; Austrian German has distinct dialects and vocabulary.
Austria gave the world Mozart, Haydn, Schubert, and Strauss – arguably the greatest musical legacy of any nation.
Viennese coffeehouse culture (Kaffeehauskultur) is UNESCO-recognised heritage.
Austria hosted the first-ever modern Olympic Games... wait, that was Athens. Austria DID host the first Winter Olympics (1964).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Austria covers 83,871 sq km in central Europe.
A landlocked country bordered by Germany, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Italy, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein.
The Alps cover 62% of Austria's territory.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Vienna has been voted the world's most liveable city multiple times.
Adolf Hitler was Austrian, not German.
Austria has given the world psychoanalysis (Sigmund Freud), Red Bull energy drinks, and the Arnold Schwarzenegger physique!
Austria's Hallstatt village was so popular with Chinese tourists that China built an exact replica of it in Guangdong province!

Switzerland.tagline: Heart of Europe – Alps, Watches, Chocolate, and Eternal Neutrality 🇨🇭

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bern is Switzerland's federal capital; Geneva and Zurich are the international and financial capitals.
Geneva hosts the UN's European headquarters, Red Cross, and hundreds of international organisations.
Switzerland has been neutral in all European wars since 1815 – over 200 years of peace.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Matterhorn – The iconic pyramid-shaped peak (4,478m) on the Swiss-Italian border, one of the Alps' most recognisable mountains.
Jungfraujoch – The highest railway station in Europe at 3,454m, with glaciers and alpine panoramas.
Lake Geneva (Lac Léman) – A crescent-shaped lake beneath the Alps with the Jet d'Eau fountain.
Old City of Bern – A UNESCO World Heritage medieval city with 6km of arcaded walkways.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Banking & Finance – Swiss banks manage 25% of all global cross-border private assets.
Pharmaceuticals – Novartis and Roche (headquartered in Basel) are two of the world's largest pharma companies.
Watchmaking – Swiss watches (Rolex, Omega, Swatch) are the world standard for precision timekeeping.
Chocolate – Lindt, Nestlé, Toblerone – Switzerland produces some of the world's finest chocolate.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Switzerland has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh.
Swiss culture is famously precise, private, and quality-obsessed – 'Swiss quality' is a global standard.
The Red Cross was founded in Geneva in 1863 by Swiss businessman Henry Dunant.
Switzerland invented Velcro, LSD, the World Wide Web (Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in Geneva).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Switzerland covers 41,285 sq km in the heart of Europe.
A landlocked country bordered by France, Germany, Austria, Liechtenstein, and Italy.
The Alps cover 65% of Switzerland; rivers flowing to the North Sea, Mediterranean, and Black Sea all start here.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The World Wide Web was invented at CERN in Geneva, Switzerland in 1989!
Switzerland hasn't been involved in a foreign war since 1815 – over 200 years of neutrality.
Swiss banks are so secretive that numbered accounts were standard – though secrecy laws have been reformed recently.
Switzerland has a law requiring every citizen to have access to a nuclear bunker – 300,000+ shelters for 8.7 million people.

Belgium.tagline: Chocolate, Waffles, Beer, and the Heart of Europe 🇧🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Brussels is Belgium's capital and the de facto capital of the European Union.
Bruges (Brugge) is a perfectly preserved medieval city of canals, often called the 'Venice of the North'.
Belgium is home to more comic strip artists per square km than any country in the world.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Grand Place, Brussels – One of Europe's most magnificent medieval squares, UNESCO World Heritage.
Atomium – A giant molecular model built for the 1958 Brussels World Expo, now an iconic museum.
Bruges Medieval Centre – UNESCO World Heritage; perfectly preserved medieval Flemish city.
Battlefields of Ypres/Flanders – WWI's most devastating front; 600,000 died here.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Chocolate – Belgian chocolate is the world's gold standard; over 170,000 tonnes produced annually.
Beer – Belgium has over 1,500 types of beer; Trappist beers are among the world's most prized.
Diamonds – Antwerp processes 80% of the world's rough diamonds.
Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals – UCB and other major pharma companies.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Belgium has three official languages: French, Dutch (Flemish), and German – reflecting deep cultural divisions.
The language divide between Flanders (Dutch) and Wallonia (French) has made Belgium the world record holder for longest period without a government (589 days)!
Belgium gave the world the saxophone (Adolphe Sax), Audrey Hepburn, and Tintin!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Belgium covers 30,528 sq km in northwestern Europe.
Bordered by Netherlands, Germany, Luxembourg, and France, with a North Sea coastline.
Flat lowlands in the north; Ardennes forested plateau in the south.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Belgium went 589 days without a government (2010–2011) and society functioned perfectly – a world record!
Antwerp handles 80% of the world's rough diamonds – making it the diamond capital of the world.
The saxophone was invented by Belgian Adolphe Sax in 1840.
Belgium produces 220,000 tonnes of chocolate annually – more than any other country in the world.

National Animal 🐾.text: Lion (Panthera leo) – golden lion on black field

Ireland.tagline: Emerald Isle – Cliffs of Moher, Guinness, and the Celtic Spirit 🇮🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Dublin is Ireland's capital, a city of literary pubs, Georgian squares, and Viking heritage.
Ireland is the birthplace of Oscar Wilde, James Joyce, W.B. Yeats, and Samuel Beckett – an extraordinary literary legacy.
Ireland (Éire) gained independence from Britain in 1922; Northern Ireland remains part of the UK.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Cliffs of Moher – Dramatic 214m sea cliffs on Ireland's Atlantic coast, a natural wonder.
Ring of Kerry – A scenic drive through the mountains, lakes, and coastal views of County Kerry.
Newgrange – A 5,200-year-old megalithic tomb, older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian pyramids.
Trinity College Library – Houses the illuminated Book of Kells, an 800 AD masterpiece of Celtic art.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Technology – Dublin is 'Silicon Docks'; Google, Facebook, Apple, and Microsoft have their European HQs here.
Pharmaceuticals – Ireland produces 40% of all pharmaceuticals sold in the EU.
Agriculture – Irish beef, dairy (Kerrygold butter), and whiskey are world-famous.
Tourism – The Wild Atlantic Way, castles, and pub culture draw millions.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Irish (Gaeilge) and English are both official languages; Irish is spoken as a daily language in Gaeltacht regions.
Irish culture values storytelling, music (fiddle, uilleann pipes), and pub culture as social arts.
Ireland has given the world Guinness, whiskey, U2, Riverdance, and St Patrick's Day celebrations on every continent!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Ireland covers 70,273 sq km on the island of Ireland in the North Atlantic.
Bordered by the Atlantic Ocean, Celtic Sea, Irish Sea, and shares the island with Northern Ireland (UK).
The Gulf Stream makes Ireland unusually mild and green for its latitude – hence 'Emerald Isle'.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Great Famine (1845–52) killed 1 million Irish and caused 2 million to emigrate – halving the population.
Ireland's population is still smaller today than before the Famine – the only European country with this feature.
Newgrange (3200 BC) is older than both Stonehenge and the Pyramids of Giza!
On St Patrick's Day, Chicago dyes its river green and Sydney Harbour Bridge is lit green – celebrating Irish heritage worldwide.

Czech Republic.tagline: Bohemian Rhapsody – Prague's Spires, Pilsner Beer, and Kafka's Maze 🇨🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Prague is Czechia's capital, one of Europe's most beautifully preserved medieval cities.
Prague's Old Town, Charles Bridge, and Prague Castle make it one of the most visited cities in Europe.
Czechia (Czech Republic) was part of Czechoslovakia until 1993, when it peacefully split from Slovakia.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Prague Old Town & Astronomical Clock – A UNESCO-listed medieval city with the world's oldest functioning astronomical clock (1410).
Charles Bridge – A 14th-century stone bridge lined with 30 Baroque statues over the Vltava River.
Prague Castle – The world's largest ancient castle by area.
Český Krumlov – A fairy-tale UNESCO-listed Baroque town surrounding a massive castle on a river bend.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Engineering – Škoda (cars), and high-quality industrial machinery production.
Beer – Czechia has the highest beer consumption per capita in the world; Pilsner lager was invented in Plzeň in 1842.
Technology – A growing IT and fintech sector in Prague.
Tourism – Prague is one of Europe's most visited cities.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Czech is the official language, a West Slavic language.
Czech culture produced Franz Kafka, Milan Kundera, and the Prague Spring of 1968.
Czech crystal glassware and Bohemian garnets are luxury exports worldwide.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Czechia covers 78,866 sq km in central Europe.
A landlocked country bordered by Germany, Poland, Slovakia, and Austria.
The Bohemian Basin is surrounded by mountain ranges on all sides.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Czechia drinks more beer per person than any other country in the world!
Pilsner lager beer style was invented in Plzeň (Pilsen), Czechia in 1842.
Prague Castle is the world's largest coherent castle complex.
The Velvet Revolution of 1989 toppled communism without a single shot fired – the most peaceful revolution in history.

Romania.tagline: Land of Dracula – Transylvanian Castles, Carpathians, and Painted Monasteries 🇷🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bucharest is Romania's capital, nicknamed 'Little Paris' for its grand boulevards and Belle Époque architecture.
Transylvania – the legendary land of Dracula – is a real, beautiful region in the Carpathian mountains.
Romania joined the EU in 2007.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Bran Castle (Dracula's Castle) – Medieval fortress associated with Vlad the Impaler.
Painted Monasteries of Bucovina – UNESCO World Heritage 15th-16th century monasteries with vivid exterior frescoes.
Transfăgărășan Road – Top Gear called it the world's best driving road through the Carpathians.
Danube Delta – UNESCO World Heritage; Europe's best birding and wildlife wetland.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: IT & Tech – Romania has some of Europe's fastest internet; Bucharest is a growing tech hub.
Agriculture – Wheat, maize, sunflowers, and wine.
Automotive – Ford and Dacia (Renault) manufacture here.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Romanian is the official language, a Romance language descended from Latin.
Romania is the largest Eastern European country where a Romance language is spoken.
Vlad Tepes (the Impaler) – the real Dracula – was a 15th-century Wallachian prince known for impaling enemies.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Romania covers 238,397 sq km in southeastern Europe.
The Carpathian Mountains form a great arc through the centre.
Bordered by Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria, Moldova, Ukraine, and the Black Sea.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Vlad the Impaler's method of impaling enemies on stakes is the inspiration for Bram Stoker's Dracula.
Romania's Palace of the Parliament is the world's heaviest building and second largest administrative building.
Romania has more bears, wolves, and lynx than any other European country outside Russia.
Nadia Comaneci scored the first ever perfect 10 in Olympic gymnastics history in 1976!

Hungary.tagline: Heart of the Carpathian Basin – Thermal Spas, Goulash, and the Danube 🇭🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Budapest is Hungary's magnificent capital, formed by uniting Buda (hilly, historic) and Pest (flat, modern) across the Danube in 1873.
Budapest is called the 'Paris of the East' for its grand architecture.
Hungary was the eastern half of the Austro-Hungarian Empire.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Parliament Building – One of Europe's largest and most stunning parliament buildings, overlooking the Danube.
Buda Castle – A UNESCO World Heritage castle complex on Castle Hill.
Széchenyi Thermal Baths – Budapest's grandest thermal spa, built in 1913.
Lake Balaton – Central Europe's largest lake; Hungary's 'inland sea'.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Automotive – Hungary produces more cars per capita than almost any other country; Audi, Mercedes, BMW all have plants here.
Agriculture – Hungary is a major grain, sunflower oil, and wine producer.
Tourism – Budapest and Lake Balaton attract millions.
Electronics – Samsung, Bosch, and GE have major facilities.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Hungarian (Magyar) is the official language, completely unrelated to any neighbouring language; it's Uralic like Finnish.
Hungarians call themselves 'Magyar'; Hungary is 'Magyarország'.
Hungarian cuisine – goulash, paprikash, lángos – uses paprika extensively; Hungary introduced paprika to European cooking.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Hungary covers 93,028 sq km in central Europe.
A landlocked country bordered by Austria, Slovakia, Ukraine, Romania, Serbia, Croatia, and Slovenia.
The Carpathian Basin; the Danube and Tisza rivers flow through the flat plains.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Budapest has more thermal springs than any other capital city in the world – 118 springs and wells!
Hungarians have won the most Nobel Prizes per capita of any nation.
The Rubik's Cube was invented by Hungarian professor Ernő Rubik in 1974.
Hungary's population has been decreasing for decades; it has one of Europe's lowest birth rates.

Serbia.tagline: Crossroads of Civilisations – Novi Sad, Belgrade Nightlife, and Balkan Spirit 🇷🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Belgrade (Beograd – 'White City') is Serbia's capital, one of Europe's oldest continuously inhabited cities.
Novi Sad hosts EXIT Festival, one of Europe's biggest music festivals.
Serbia is the spiritual and political heart of the Western Balkans.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Belgrade Fortress (Kalemegdan) – A massive fortress at the confluence of the Sava and Danube rivers with 2,000+ years of history.
Fruška Gora Monasteries – 16 Serbian Orthodox monasteries in a wine-producing national park.
Đavolja Varoš (Devil's Town) – Natural rock columns formed by erosion, a dramatic landscape.
Uvac Canyon – A dramatic canyon with wild Griffon vultures and crystal blue river.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Serbia is a major fruit, grain, and raspberry producer.
Mining – Copper and zinc from Bor, one of Europe's largest copper mines.
IT & Services – Growing tech outsourcing sector.
Automotive – Fiat's only Eastern European plant is in Kragujevac.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Serbian is the official language, written in both Cyrillic and Latin scripts.
Serbia has significant Hungarian, Bosniak, Roma, and other minority communities.
Nikola Tesla (electricity pioneer) was born in Serbia. Tesla's alternating current powers the world!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Serbia covers 77,474 sq km in the Western Balkans.
A landlocked country bordered by Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, North Macedonia, Kosovo, Montenegro, Bosnia, and Croatia.
The Danube, Sava, and Morava rivers shape the country's geography.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Nikola Tesla, who invented alternating current (AC electricity) and wireless transmission, was Serbian!
Belgrade's Kalemegdan fortress has been conquered 40 times and rebuilt 38 times in 2,000 years!
Serbia is one of the world's top raspberry exporters – shipping over 90,000 tonnes a year.
EXIT Festival in Novi Sad was started by students as a protest against Milošević – now one of Europe's biggest music events!

Croatia.tagline: Pearl of the Adriatic – Dubrovnik, Plitvice Lakes, and 1,200 Islands 🇭🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Zagreb is Croatia's capital, a Central European city of Austro-Hungarian architecture and cafe culture.
Dubrovnik on the Adriatic is one of the world's most perfectly preserved walled medieval cities.
Croatia joined the EU in 2013 and adopted the Euro in 2023.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Dubrovnik Old City – A UNESCO World Heritage walled city on a rocky Adriatic promontory; the 'Pearl of the Adriatic'.
Plitvice Lakes National Park – UNESCO World Heritage cascading turquoise lakes connected by waterfalls.
Diocletian's Palace, Split – A UNESCO World Heritage 4th-century Roman palace where 3,000 people still live inside.
Hvar Island – A glamorous Adriatic island of lavender fields, medieval towns, and yacht parties.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Croatia's Adriatic coast is one of Europe's most popular destinations.
Shipbuilding – A historic and continuing industry.
Agriculture – Olive oil, wine, and lavender from Dalmatia.
IT & Technology – A growing tech scene.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Croatian is the official language.
Croatia invented the necktie (cravat) – Croatian soldiers' neck scarves became fashionable in 17th-century France!
Marco Polo – the famous explorer – was born on the Croatian island of Korčula.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Croatia covers 56,594 sq km in southeastern Europe.
Has 1,244 islands along its Adriatic coastline.
Bordered by Slovenia, Hungary, Serbia, Bosnia, and Montenegro.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The necktie (cravat) was invented in Croatia – 'cravat' comes from 'Croat'!
Dubrovnik's walls have never been breached by an enemy – they're in such good shape they're still complete today.
Croatia has 10 UNESCO World Heritage sites, remarkable for a country of 4 million people.
The TV show Game of Thrones filmed extensively in Dubrovnik and Split – tourism increased 300% afterwards!

Bulgaria.tagline: Land of Roses – Thracian Treasures, Black Sea Coast, and Rose Valley 🇧🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Sofia is Bulgaria's capital and largest city, at the foot of Vitosha Mountain.
Bulgaria is one of Europe's oldest countries; the Bulgarian state has existed since 681 AD.
The Cyrillic alphabet was created by Saints Cyril and Methodius, Bulgarian scholars.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Rila Monastery – Bulgaria's most sacred site, a UNESCO World Heritage Orthodox monastery in the Rila Mountains.
Thracian Tomb of Kazanlak – UNESCO World Heritage; a 2,300-year-old Thracian tomb with stunning frescoes.
Nessebar Old Town – A UNESCO island city with ancient Greek, Roman, and Byzantine ruins.
Rose Valley (Kazanlak) – Produces 85% of the world's rose oil, used in the finest perfumes.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Rose Oil – Bulgaria produces 70-85% of the world's rose oil (attar of roses), essential for perfumes.
IT & Software – Sofia has a booming software development sector.
Agriculture – Wine, wheat, sunflowers, and tobacco.
Tourism – Black Sea beaches and ski resorts.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Bulgarian is the official language, written in Cyrillic.
The Cyrillic alphabet – used by Russians, Serbs, Ukrainians and others – was invented by Bulgarians!
Bulgarians shake their head to say 'yes' and nod to say 'no' – the opposite of most of the world!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Bulgaria covers 110,879 sq km in southeastern Europe.
Bordered by Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Greece, and Turkey, with a Black Sea coast.
The Balkan Mountains run east-west through the centre; the Danube forms the northern border.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Cyrillic alphabet was invented by Saints Cyril and Methodius in Bulgaria in the 9th century!
Bulgaria shakes its head for YES and nods for NO – the opposite of the rest of the world!
Bulgaria's Rose Valley produces most of the world's rose oil – 1 gram requires 4,000 hand-picked roses!
Bulgaria is one of Europe's oldest countries – the Bulgarian state was recognised in 681 AD.

Albania.tagline: Land of Eagles – Ionian Riviera, Ottoman Bazaars, and Bunkers Everywhere 🇦🇱

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tirana is Albania's capital, a colourful city of pastel buildings.
Albania was the most isolated country in Europe under communist dictator Enver Hoxha (1944–1985).
Albania has 173,000 concrete bunkers built by the paranoid communist regime – about one per family!

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Butrint – UNESCO World Heritage ancient Greek, Roman, Byzantine, and Venetian ruins on a lake.
Gjirokastër – UNESCO World Heritage Ottoman-era stone city with a massive fortress.
Albanian Riviera – Stunning Ionian coastline with turquoise water and hidden beaches.
Valbona & Theth – Dramatic Albanian Alps with traditional stone guest houses (bujtinat).

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Albania's coastline and mountain scenery are among Europe's last undiscovered gems.
Remittances – Over 1 million Albanians work abroad.
Mining – Chrome, copper, and oil.
Agriculture – Olives, wine, and citrus from the Adriatic lowlands.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Albanian (Shqip) is the official language, one of the most unique Indo-European languages with no close relatives.
Albanians call themselves 'Shqiptarë' (Sons of the Eagles) – the eagle on the flag reflects this.
The Kanun – an ancient Albanian code of honour and law – governs traditional mountain communities.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Albania covers 28,748 sq km in southeastern Europe.
Bordered by Montenegro, Kosovo, North Macedonia, and Greece; coastlines on the Adriatic and Ionian Seas.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Albania has 173,000 concrete bunkers – 1 per family – built by the communist regime against an imagined invasion that never came.
Mother Teresa was of Albanian descent (born in Skopje to Albanian parents).
Albania was Europe's last country to open to tourism after communism ended in 1992.
Albania's coastline gets 300 days of sunshine per year and remains one of Europe's most affordable destinations.

Belarus.tagline: Lungs of Europe – Primeval Forests, Soviet Monuments, and Resilient Culture 🇧🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Minsk is Belarus's capital, a city largely rebuilt in grand Soviet Stalinist style after WWII destroyed it.
Belarus is sometimes called 'Europe's Last Dictatorship' under President Lukashenko (since 1994).
Belarus means 'White Russia'; it was the most devastated of all Soviet republics in WWII.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Białowieża Forest – Europe's last primeval forest, shared with Poland, UNESCO World Heritage; home to European bison.
Mir Castle – A UNESCO World Heritage Gothic-Renaissance castle.
Nesvizh Castle – UNESCO World Heritage Baroque palace of the Radziwiłł family.
Brest Fortress – A WWII memorial to the heroic defence of the fortress against Nazi invasion in 1941.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Heavy Industry – Soviet-era factories produce tractors (Belarus makes 10% of world tractors), trucks, and machinery.
Potash – Belarus is one of the world's top potash (fertilizer) producers.
IT – Belarus has a thriving IT sector; Viber and EPAM were founded here.
Agriculture – Dairy and potato production.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Belarusian and Russian are both official languages.
Belarusians are the only Eastern European people who do not have their language in sole official use.
Marc Chagall, the painter, was born in Vitebsk, Belarus.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Belarus covers 207,600 sq km in Eastern Europe.
A landlocked country bordered by Russia, Ukraine, Poland, Lithuania, and Latvia.
Mostly flat; the Polesie swamps are one of Europe's largest wetlands.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Belarus produces around 10% of the world's tractors – Minsk Tractor Works is one of the world's largest.
Białowieża Forest has the world's largest remaining wild population of European bison.
Belarus was the most devastating battleground in WWII – 25% of its population died.
Viber messenger app, used by 1 billion people, was founded by Belarusians.

Slovakia.tagline: Heart of Central Europe – Castles, Caves, and Carpathian Adventures 🇸🇰

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bratislava is Slovakia's capital, a charming city on the Danube just 60 km from Vienna.
Slovakia peacefully separated from Czech Republic in 1993 – the 'Velvet Divorce'.
Slovakia has more castles per square kilometre than any other country in the world.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: High Tatras – Slovakia's dramatic alpine peaks, the highest range in the Carpathians.
Bojnice Castle – A romantic fairy-tale castle on a limestone hill.
Spišský Hrad – UNESCO World Heritage; one of Central Europe's largest castle ruins.
Dobšiná Ice Cave – UNESCO World Heritage; a spectacular cave of permanent ice formations.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Automotive – Slovakia produces more cars per capita than any other country; VW, Kia, Stellantis all have plants here.
Electronics – Samsung, Sony.
Steel – US Steel's largest European plant is in Košice.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Slovak is the official language.
Slovakia has Hungarian, Romani, Czech, and Ruthenian minorities.
Slovak folk culture – embroidery, folk music, and log cabin architecture – is richly preserved.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Slovakia covers 49,035 sq km in central Europe.
Landlocked, bordered by Czech Republic, Austria, Hungary, Ukraine, and Poland.
The Carpathian Mountains cover most of the country.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Slovakia produces more cars per person than any other country in the world!
Slovakia has more castles and castle ruins per capita than any country in the world.
Andy Warhol's parents were Slovak immigrants; he visited Slovakia before his death.
Bratislava is the only capital city in the world that borders two separate foreign countries (Austria and Hungary).

Slovenia.tagline: Green Heart of Europe – Lake Bled, Alpine Villages, and Honey Bees 🇸🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: Ljubljana is Slovenia's charming capital, a walkable city of baroque architecture and riverside cafes.
Slovenia has one of the highest standards of living in Central/Eastern Europe.
Slovenia is small but astonishingly diverse – Alps, karst caves, vineyards, and Adriatic coast in one country.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Lake Bled – A glacial lake with an island church and a clifftop castle, one of Europe's most romantic views.
Postojna Cave – One of Europe's longest cave systems; the olm (human fish) lives only in Slovenian caves.
Triglav National Park – Slovenia's only national park, centred on Mount Triglav (2,864m).
Predjama Castle – A castle built inside a cave mouth in a 123m cliff face.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Industry – Precision manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, and electronics.
Tourism – Lake Bled, caves, and ski resorts.
Wine – Quality wines from Brda, Štajerska, and Kras regions.
Beekeeping – Slovenia has the most beekeepers per capita and produces exceptional honey.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Slovenian is the official language.
Slovenia has a proud beekeeping tradition – the Carniolan bee is world-famous for its productivity and gentle nature.
Slovenia was the first former Yugoslav republic to join the EU and NATO.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Slovenia covers just 20,273 sq km – one of Europe's smallest countries.
Bordered by Italy, Austria, Hungary, and Croatia; a small Adriatic coast.
One of Europe's most forested countries – 60% covered in forest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Slovenia's Postojna Cave has the olm – a blind cave salamander called 'the human fish' that lives 100+ years!
Slovenia is 60% forested – one of the most forested countries in Europe.
Slovenia is the world's first country to declare itself a 'green country' in its tourism branding.
Melania Trump (US First Lady 2017–2021) is from Sevnica, Slovenia!

Bosnia and Herzegovina.tagline: Bridge of Civilisations – Mostar, Ottoman Heritage, and Balkan Soul 🇧🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Sarajevo is the capital, a city where East meets West – minarets and church towers stand side by side.
Sarajevo hosted the 1984 Winter Olympics and was besieged for 44 months in the 1990s war.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in 1914 triggered World War I.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Stari Most (Old Bridge), Mostar – A UNESCO World Heritage 16th-century Ottoman bridge; symbol of reconciliation.
Baščaršija Bazaar, Sarajevo – A 15th-century Ottoman bazaar quarter, the heart of old Sarajevo.
Kravice Waterfalls – A stunning series of waterfalls in a natural amphitheatre.
Konjic Sutjeska – UNESCO-candidate primeval forest Perućica, one of Europe's last primeval forests.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Steel & Mining – Major steel production in Zenica.
Timber – Extensive forests provide timber and wood products.
Tourism – Sarajevo, Mostar, and mountains attract cultural and ski tourists.
Agriculture – Fruits, vegetables, and honey from the fertile valleys.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian are all official languages (mutually intelligible).
Bosnia has three constituent peoples: Bosniaks (Muslim), Serbs (Orthodox), and Croats (Catholic).
The unique Bosnian coffee ceremony – served in a džezva with a sugar cube and water – is a cultural ritual.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina covers 51,197 sq km in the Western Balkans.
Bordered by Croatia, Serbia, and Montenegro; a tiny Adriatic coastline near Neum.
Mountainous interior; the Dinaric Alps and Bosnia River valley dominate the landscape.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo in 1914 started World War I – a single pistol shot changed the world.
Mostar's Old Bridge was destroyed in 1993 and rebuilt stone by stone using the original techniques, reopening in 2004.
Sarajevo hosted the Winter Olympics in 1984 – the only Balkan or Muslim-majority city to host the games.

North Macedonia.tagline: Land of Alexander the Great – Lakes, Byzantine Churches, and Balkan Warmth 🇲🇰

Capital City 🏛️.text: Skopje is North Macedonia's capital, known for its enormous statues and eclectic 'Skopje 2014' project.
North Macedonia gained independence from Yugoslavia in 1991 and joined NATO in 2020.
Alexander the Great was born in Pella, ancient Macedonia – claimed as a cultural hero by North Macedonia.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Ohrid – A UNESCO World Heritage lake city often called the 'Jerusalem of the Balkans' for its 365 churches.
Lake Ohrid – One of Europe's oldest lakes (2-3 million years), UNESCO World Heritage.
Matka Canyon – A dramatic canyon with caves and a medieval monastery near Skopje.
Kokino Observatory – A 3,800-year-old Bronze Age astronomical observatory, recognised by NASA.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Wine, grapes, tobacco, and peppers.
Mining – Lead, zinc, copper, and iron ore.
IT – Growing outsourcing and software development sector.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Macedonian is the official language, a South Slavic language.
North Macedonia has a significant Albanian minority (about 25%).
Mother Teresa was born in Skopje to Albanian parents in 1910.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: North Macedonia covers 25,713 sq km in the Western Balkans.
A landlocked country bordered by Serbia, Kosovo, Albania, Greece, and Bulgaria.
Lake Ohrid and Lake Prespa are shared with Albania and Greece.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lake Ohrid is 2-3 million years old – one of the world's oldest lakes, with many endemic species.
Kokino Observatory is the world's 4th oldest astronomical observatory, recognised by NASA.
Mother Teresa was born in Skopje, North Macedonia.
North Macedonia was the only former Yugoslav republic to gain independence peacefully.

Montenegro.tagline: Black Mountain – Adriatic Fjords, Medieval Walls, and Wild Tara Canyon 🇲🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Podgorica is Montenegro's capital and largest city.
Cetinje is the historic capital and seat of Montenegro's former royal family.
Montenegro declared independence from Serbia-Montenegro in 2006.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Kotor Old Town – A UNESCO World Heritage medieval walled city in a dramatic bay.
Tara River Canyon – Europe's deepest canyon (1,300m), a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Durmitor National Park – UNESCO World Heritage mountain park with glacial lakes and skiing.
Bay of Kotor – Often called Europe's southernmost fjord; one of the most beautiful bays on earth.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Montenegro's Adriatic coast and Bay of Kotor attract growing numbers.
Aluminium – The KAP aluminium plant in Podgorica was once the country's largest employer.
Agriculture – Olive oil, wine, and prosciutto from the Adriatic coast.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Montenegrin, Serbian, Bosnian, and Croatian are all official languages.
Montenegro means 'Black Mountain' in Italian (Crna Gora in Montenegrin).
Montenegrins have one of the highest average heights in the world.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Montenegro covers 13,812 sq km – one of Europe's smallest countries.
Bordered by Croatia, Bosnia, Serbia, Kosovo, and Albania; Adriatic coast in the west.
Dramatic geography from the Adriatic coast to high Dinaric Alps in just 50 km.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Montenegro's Tara River Canyon is Europe's deepest canyon at 1,300m – deeper than the Grand Canyon in some places!
Montenegro is one of the world's most ecologically diverse countries relative to its size.
Montenegro means 'Black Mountain' – named for the dark appearance of Mount Lovćen.
Montenegro has a constitution that mandates 9% of GDP must go to environmental protection.

Kosovo.tagline: Newborn Nation – Medieval Monasteries, Pristina Youth, and Balkan Resilience 🇽🇰

Capital City 🏛️.text: Pristina is Kosovo's capital, a young and rapidly developing city.
Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, recognised by over 100 countries.
Kosovo has one of Europe's youngest populations – over 60% under 35.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Newborn Monument, Pristina – A giant yellow 'NEWBORN' sculpture unveiled on independence day.
Dečani Monastery – A UNESCO World Heritage Serbian Orthodox monastery from the 14th century.
Prizren – Kosovo's most beautiful historic city with Ottoman bazaars and Byzantine churches.
Accursed Mountains (Prokletije) – Dramatic Albanian Alps shared with Albania and Montenegro.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Remittances – Kosovo's diaspora (mostly in Germany and Switzerland) sends significant funds.
Mining – Kosovo has some of the world's largest lignite reserves.
Agriculture – Fruits, vegetables, and wine.
Services – Growing IT and service sectors.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Albanian and Serbian are official languages.
Kosovo is predominantly ethnic Albanian (93%) with Serbian and other minorities.
Kosovo has the youngest population in Europe.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Kosovo covers 10,887 sq km in the Western Balkans.
Landlocked, surrounded by Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania, and Montenegro.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Kosovo is the world's newest UN-recognised country (2008).
Mother Teresa was of Albanian descent (the ethnicity dominant in Kosovo).
Kosovo has one of Europe's youngest populations – a stark contrast to ageing Western Europe.

Moldova.tagline: Land of Wine – Largest Wine Cellar, Peaceful Vineyards, and Transnistria 🇲🇩

Capital City 🏛️.text: Chișinău is Moldova's capital, a city of Soviet-era architecture and vibrant wine culture.
Moldova has the Transnistria region – a Russian-backed breakaway state with Soviet-era symbols still in use.
Moldova is the poorest country in Europe by GDP per capita.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Cricova Wine Cellars – A labyrinth of wine cellars stretching 120 km underground, the world's largest wine cellar.
Mileștii Mici – The world's largest wine collection (Guinness Record) with 1.5 million bottles.
Orheiul Vechi – A cliff monastery complex in a scenic river bend, thousands of years inhabited.
Transnistria – A frozen-in-time Soviet breakaway state with its own currency, police, and army.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Wine – Moldova has one of the world's highest percentages of land under vine; wine is a major export.
Agriculture – Fruits, vegetables, grain, and sunflower seeds.
IT – A growing IT outsourcing sector in Chișinău.
Remittances – Over 1 million Moldovans work abroad.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Romanian (Moldovan) is the official language.
Russian is widely spoken, especially in cities and Transnistria.
Moldova has a rich folk tradition of music, embroidery, and winemaking.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Moldova covers 33,846 sq km between Romania and Ukraine.
A landlocked country; one of Europe's smallest.
Rolling hills and valleys with the Dniester and Prut rivers forming its borders.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Moldova has the world's largest wine collection – 1.5 million bottles in Mileștii Mici wine cellars (Guinness Record)!
Transnistria uses Soviet-era symbols, currency, and statues of Lenin – a time capsule of the USSR.
Moldova is the poorest country in Europe yet produces some of the world's finest wine.

Estonia.tagline: Digital Republic – Tallinn's Medieval Spires, Bogs, and E-Government Pioneers 🇪🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tallinn is Estonia's capital, a medieval walled city with an extraordinarily well-preserved Old Town.
Estonia is the world's most advanced digital society – voting, taxes, healthcare all done online.
Skype was invented in Estonia; Wise (financial transfers) and Bolt (ride-hailing) are Estonian startups.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Tallinn Old Town – A UNESCO World Heritage medieval city with towers, spires, and cobblestone streets.
Lahemaa National Park – Estonia's largest national park of coastal forests and manor houses.
Soomaa National Park – Bog landscapes unique to northern Europe; canoe safaris in flooded forests in spring.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Digital Technology – Estonia leads the world in e-governance; Skype, Wise, and Bolt all started here.
Oil Shale – Energy production from oil shale deposits.
Timber & Wood Products – Forest covers 50% of Estonia.
Tourism – Tallinn's Old Town and digital tourism.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Estonian is the official language, related to Finnish; one of Europe's most unique languages.
Estonia has a significant Russian-speaking minority (about 25%).
Estonian Song Festivals – mass choral singing – are UNESCO heritage; the 1988 Singing Revolution helped regain independence!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Estonia covers 45,228 sq km in northern Europe on the Baltic Sea.
Bordered by Latvia and Russia; includes 2,222 islands.
Flat, forested country with 22% covered by bogs and wetlands.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Skype was invented in Estonia and Wise (formerly TransferWise) was co-founded by an Estonian.
Estonia regained independence from the USSR partly through The Singing Revolution – 300,000 Estonians sang national songs in defiance!
Estonia is ranked the world's most digital society – you can even vote in elections from your phone.
Estonia has more than 2,000 islands along its Baltic Sea coastline.

Latvia.tagline: Baltic Amber – Art Nouveau Capital, Song Festivals, and Baltic Forests 🇱🇻

Capital City 🏛️.text: Riga is Latvia's capital and the largest city in the Baltic states.
Riga has the world's largest collection of Art Nouveau architecture – over 800 buildings.
Latvia regained independence from the USSR in 1991 after the Singing Revolution.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Riga Old Town – UNESCO World Heritage medieval city and Art Nouveau showpiece.
Gauja National Park – Latvia's oldest and largest national park of forests and medieval castles.
Rundale Palace – An 18th-century Baroque palace called the 'Versailles of Latvia'.
Jūrmala – A resort town of wooden Art Nouveau beach villas along the Gulf of Riga.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Timber & Wood Products – Latvia's forests cover 54% of the country; timber is a major export.
IT & Technology – Growing tech sector in Riga.
Food – Latvian dairy (especially butter and cheese), fish, and craft spirits.
Transport & Logistics – Strategic Baltic position.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Latvian is the official language, one of the world's oldest living languages (Baltic branch of Indo-European).
Latvia has a significant Russian-speaking minority.
Latvian amber – fossilised Baltic tree resin – has been traded for 13,000 years.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Latvia covers 64,589 sq km on the eastern Baltic Sea.
Bordered by Estonia, Russia, Belarus, and Lithuania.
Flat, forested country with the Western Dvina (Daugava) River as its main waterway.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Riga has more Art Nouveau buildings than any other city in the world – over 800!
Latvia has one of the world's oldest living languages – Latvian is extremely close to proto-Indo-European, the ancestor of most European languages.
Latvia has the highest ratio of female to male population in the world – legacy of WWII losses.

Lithuania.tagline: Land of Amber – Hill of Crosses, Baroque Vilnius, and Baltic Shores 🇱🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Vilnius is Lithuania's capital, a UNESCO World Heritage Baroque city of spires and cobblestone streets.
Lithuania declared independence from the Soviet Union in 1990 – the first Soviet republic to do so.
Lithuania was once one of Europe's largest empires (14th–16th century), stretching from the Baltic to the Black Sea.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Vilnius Old Town – UNESCO World Heritage; the largest Baroque old town in northern Europe.
Hill of Crosses – A pilgrimage site with over 100,000 crosses planted on a small hill as a symbol of peaceful resistance.
Trakai Island Castle – A stunning red-brick castle on an island in a lake system.
Curonian Spit – UNESCO World Heritage; a narrow sandy peninsula of giant dunes and pine forests.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: IT & Fintech – Vilnius is a growing fintech hub; many banks have European HQs here.
Laser Technology – Lithuanian laser companies produce 30% of the world's scientific lasers.
Timber – Forests cover 33% of Lithuania.
Agriculture – Amber, linen, and dairy.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Lithuanian is the official language, considered the most archaic living Indo-European language.
Lithuanian is so ancient it retains features from 3,500 BC proto-Indo-European.
Amber – fossilised tree resin – has been collected and traded from Lithuania's Baltic coast for 13,000 years.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Lithuania covers 65,300 sq km on the eastern Baltic Sea.
Bordered by Latvia, Belarus, Poland, Russia (Kaliningrad exclave), and the Baltic Sea.
The geographic centre of Europe (by one calculation) is in Lithuania, near Vilnius.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Lithuania was the first Soviet republic to declare independence (1990), defying Gorbachev.
Lithuanian is so ancient that linguists use it to reconstruct the original proto-Indo-European language spoken 5,000 years ago.
The geographic centre of Europe is in Lithuania – there's a monument marking the spot.
Lithuania produces 30% of the world's scientific lasers – from a country of 3 million people!

Iceland.tagline: Land of Fire and Ice – Geysers, Northern Lights, and Viking Heritage 🇮🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Reykjavík is Iceland's capital and the world's northernmost national capital.
Iceland runs on 100% renewable energy from geothermal and hydropower.
Iceland is the most sparsely populated country in Europe.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) – Iceland's dark winters offer spectacular aurora displays.
Golden Circle – Þingvellir (world's oldest parliament), Geysir (original geyser), and Gullfoss waterfall.
Blue Lagoon – A famous geothermal spa in a lava field with milky-blue waters.
Vatnajökull – Europe's largest glacier, covering 8% of Iceland.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Fishing – Fishing and fish processing account for 40% of Iceland's exports.
Aluminium Smelting – Cheap geothermal power attracts aluminium smelters.
Tourism – The Golden Circle, Northern Lights, and Ring Road drive major tourism.
Geothermal Energy – Iceland exports geothermal technology worldwide.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Icelandic is the official language; it has changed so little that Icelanders can read 800-year-old Viking sagas.
Iceland was settled by Vikings from Norway and Celtic people from the British Isles in the 9th century.
The Althing – Iceland's parliament, founded in 930 AD – is the world's oldest continuously functioning parliament.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Iceland covers 103,000 sq km in the North Atlantic.
Situated on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge; volcanically active with 30+ active volcanic systems.
One-tenth of the island is covered by glaciers.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Iceland's Althing parliament (930 AD) is the world's oldest continuously operating parliament!
Iceland runs on 100% renewable energy – geothermal and hydropower.
Iceland has never had a standing army – it has the world's oldest parliament but no military.
Iceland's phone book is listed by first name, not surname, because surnames change with each generation (patronymic system)!

Luxembourg.tagline: Green Heart of Europe – Richest Nation, Fairytale Castles, and Banking Capital 🇱🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Luxembourg City is both the capital and a UNESCO World Heritage site for its dramatic clifftop fortifications.
Luxembourg is the world's only Grand Duchy and one of Europe's smallest countries.
Luxembourg has the world's highest GDP per capita (official residents).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Luxembourg City Old Quarters and Fortifications – UNESCO World Heritage clifftop citadel.
Vianden Castle – A stunning medieval castle on a hill above the Our River.
Mullerthal (Little Switzerland) – Sandstone rock formations and forested hiking trails.
Echternach – The oldest city in Luxembourg with a famous dancing procession.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Finance – Luxembourg manages the most investment funds in Europe and the most in the world after the USA.
Steel – Luxembourg's ARBED (now part of ArcelorMittal) was once Europe's largest steel company.
Technology – Amazon, PayPal, Skype's parent, and Spotify are all registered in Luxembourg.
Space Mining – Luxembourg is Europe's hub for asteroid and space resource mining plans!

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Luxembourgish, French, and German are all official languages.
Luxembourg is one of the world's most multilingual societies.
About 47% of Luxembourg's population are non-citizen residents.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Luxembourg covers just 2,586 sq km – one of Europe's smallest countries.
Bordered by Belgium, France, and Germany.
The Ardennes plateau in the north and Moselle valley in the east.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Luxembourg is the world's only Grand Duchy (ruled by a Grand Duke).
Luxembourg has the highest GDP per capita in the world.
Spotify, PayPal, and Amazon's European headquarters are all in Luxembourg (for tax reasons).
Luxembourg was a founding member of the EU, NATO, and the UN.

Malta.tagline: Crossroads of the Mediterranean – Knights, Megalithic Temples, and Azure Waters 🇲🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Valletta is Malta's capital, the smallest EU capital city and a UNESCO World Heritage Baroque masterpiece.
Malta is one of the world's most densely populated countries.
Malta was the most bombed country per square km in WWII; it was awarded the George Cross by Britain.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Valletta – A UNESCO World Heritage Baroque capital city built by the Knights of St John.
Megalithic Temples (Ħaġar Qim, Mnajdra) – UNESCO World Heritage; older than Stonehenge and the Pyramids!
Azure Window (collapsed in 2017) – A famous limestone arch that was a natural wonder.
Mdina – A medieval silent city of 300 residents in a fortified hilltop; used in Game of Thrones.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Malta's history, diving, and Valletta attract over 2 million visitors.
Online Gaming & iGaming – Malta is Europe's iGaming capital.
Financial Services – A major EU financial centre.
Electronics – Precision engineering and electronics manufacturing.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Maltese and English are both official languages.
Maltese is the only Semitic language written in the Latin script and an official EU language.
Malta's Knights of St John (Knights Hospitaller) ruled Malta from 1530 to 1798 – their legacy shapes the whole island.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Malta covers just 316 sq km – one of the world's smallest countries.
A Mediterranean archipelago 80 km south of Sicily.
Three inhabited islands: Malta, Gozo, and Comino.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Malta's megalithic temples are over 5,500 years old – older than Stonehenge and the Egyptian Pyramids!
Malta's Maltese language is the only Semitic language written in the Latin alphabet and an official EU language.
Malta was the most bombed country per square km in WWII and received the George Cross – the highest civilian award.
Valletta is Europe's smallest capital city by area.

Vatican City.tagline: Smallest State, Greatest Spiritual Power – St Peter's, Sistine Chapel, and the Pope 🇻🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Vatican City is both the country and its capital – the world's smallest sovereign state.
It is the headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church and the home of the Pope.
Vatican City became an independent state in 1929 via the Lateran Treaty with Italy.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: St Peter's Basilica – The world's largest church, built over the tomb of Saint Peter.
Sistine Chapel – Michelangelo's breathtaking ceiling frescoes (1508–1512) and The Last Judgement.
Vatican Museums – Among the world's greatest art collections with 20,000 works on display.
St Peter's Square – Bernini's magnificent colonnade embracing 400,000 people.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Religious Activities – The Vatican's 'economy' is largely donations, museum admissions, and philately.
Publishing – L'Osservatore Romano (newspaper) and Vatican Radio broadcast globally.
Tourism – 6 million visitors per year to the museums alone.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Latin is the official language; Italian is used in daily administration.
The Swiss Guard – founded in 1506 – is the world's smallest and oldest army, protecting the Pope.
The Pope is elected by the College of Cardinals in a secret conclave; white smoke signals a new Pope.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Vatican City covers just 0.44 sq km – the world's smallest country by area and population.
Entirely surrounded by Rome, Italy, within the Tiber River bend.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Vatican City is the world's smallest country – you could walk around its entire border in 40 minutes!
The Vatican has its own ATMs with instructions in Latin – the only country in the world to do this.
Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling lying on his back for 4 years (1508–1512).
The Vatican has the world's highest crime rate per capita – mostly pickpocketing from the 6 million tourists!

San Marino.tagline: Most Serene Republic – World's Oldest Republic on a Mountain Top 🇸🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: San Marino City (City of San Marino) is the capital, perched on Monte Titano.
San Marino claims to be the world's oldest republic, founded in 301 AD.
San Marino is an enclave entirely surrounded by Italy.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Three Towers of San Marino – UNESCO World Heritage three medieval towers on Monte Titano's peaks.
Piazza della Libertà – The main square with the Government Palace and changing of the guard.
State Museum of San Marino – Coins, stamps, and the history of the world's oldest republic.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – 3 million visitors a year for its tiny population of 34,000.
Finance & Banking – Favourable financial conditions attract businesses.
Ceramics & Handicrafts – Traditional crafts exported worldwide.
Philately & Coins – San Marino stamps and coins are coveted by collectors.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Italian is the official language.
Sammarinese culture is deeply Catholic and proud of its ancient republican tradition.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: San Marino covers just 61 sq km – the world's 5th smallest country.
Entirely surrounded by Italy, near Rimini on the Adriatic coast.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: San Marino has been a republic since 301 AD – over 1,700 years, the world's oldest!
During WWII, San Marino sheltered 100,000 refugees – 3x its population – and was never invaded.
San Marino has more cars than people and has the highest car ownership rate in the world!
San Marino's Formula 1 Grand Prix was famously NOT held in San Marino – it was at Imola in Italy!

Monaco.tagline: Playground of the Rich – Formula 1 Streets, Casino, and Mediterranean Glamour 🇲🇨

Capital City 🏛️.text: Monaco is a city-state; its capital is Monaco-Ville (the Old Town on the Rock).
Monaco is the world's second smallest country and the world's most densely populated.
Monaco has the world's highest GDP per capita and more millionaires per square metre than anywhere else.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Casino de Monte-Carlo – The legendary casino that inspired James Bond's gaming scenes.
Monaco Grand Prix – F1's most prestigious race through the city streets, held since 1929.
Palace of Monaco – The royal palace of the ruling Grimaldi family (rulers since 1297).
Oceanographic Museum – Founded by Prince Albert I; one of the world's finest marine museums.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Finance – Zero income tax makes Monaco a magnet for millionaires and billionaires.
Tourism – The casino, F1 Grand Prix, and superyacht culture.
Real Estate – Monaco has some of the world's most expensive property.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: French is the official language.
Only 9,000 of Monaco's 39,000 residents are Monégasque citizens; the rest are wealthy foreigners.
The Grimaldi family has ruled Monaco since 1297 – the world's longest-reigning royal dynasty!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Monaco covers just 2.02 sq km – the world's second smallest country.
Bordered entirely by France and the Mediterranean Sea.
Due to land reclamation, Monaco has expanded its area by 6% since the 1960s.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Monaco is the world's most densely populated country – 39,000 people in 2 sq km!
The Grimaldi family has ruled Monaco since 1297 – over 700 years, the world's longest-reigning ruling family.
Monaco has zero income tax – that's why so many billionaires live there!
The Monaco Grand Prix is the only Formula 1 race through active city streets.

Liechtenstein.tagline: Alpine Micro-State – Castles, Dentists, and the Prince's Private Country 🇱🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: Vaduz is Liechtenstein's capital, a tiny city of 5,500 people below the prince's castle.
Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world (surrounded by landlocked countries).
It has no airport, no motorway, and the prince lives in a castle overlooking the capital.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Vaduz Castle – The prince's private residence, overlooking the Rhine Valley and Vaduz.
Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein – An art museum with a world-class modern and contemporary art collection.
Malbun Ski Resort – A charming small ski resort in the Alps above Vaduz.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Precision Manufacturing – Liechtenstein has more registered companies than citizens; specialises in dental equipment, industrial tools.
Finance – Low taxes attract businesses and wealth management.
Tourism – Castle, art museum, and hiking.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: German is the official language.
Liechtenstein has more companies registered than it has residents – a tiny corporate powerhouse.
Liechtenstein fields an Olympic team and has won 10 Winter Olympic medals – extraordinary for a tiny country!

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Liechtenstein covers just 160 sq km in the Alps.
One of only two doubly landlocked countries (surrounded by landlocked Switzerland and Austria).
The Rhine River forms the western border with Switzerland.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Liechtenstein is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world!
In 1866, Liechtenstein sent 80 soldiers to war with Austria. They returned 81 – having made a friend in Italy!
Liechtenstein has more registered businesses than people and one of the world's highest GDPs per capita.
You can rent the entire country of Liechtenstein for private events for €70,000 per night!

Andorra.tagline: Tiny Pyrenean Co-Principality – Skiing, Duty-Free Shopping, and Mountain Trails 🇦🇩

Capital City 🏛️.text: Andorra la Vella is Andorra's capital and the highest capital city in Europe (1,023m).
Andorra is a co-principality – co-ruled by the Bishop of Urgell (Spain) and the President of France.
It has no income tax and is a duty-free haven attracting shoppers from across Europe.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Vallnord & Grandvalira Ski Resorts – Major Pyrenean ski areas with over 300 km of pistes.
Casa de la Vall – Historic parliament building from the 16th century.
Madriu-Perafita-Claror Valley – UNESCO World Heritage alpine landscape.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Skiing, hiking, and duty-free shopping drive 80% of GDP.
Retail & Duty-Free – Lower taxes attract cross-border shoppers from France and Spain.
Banking – Small but significant financial sector.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Catalan is the only official language – the only country where Catalan has this status.
Andorran culture is Catalan; Spanish, French, and Portuguese are widely spoken.
Andorra has one of the world's highest life expectancies (average 83 years).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Andorra covers 468 sq km in the Pyrenees mountains.
Landlocked between France and Spain.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Andorra is co-ruled by the French President and a Spanish Bishop – the world's only co-principality!
Andorra has the world's longest average life expectancy (83 years) – attributed to mountain life and low stress.
Catalan is Andorra's only official language – the only country where Catalan holds sole official status.
Andorra la Vella is Europe's highest capital city at 1,023m above sea level.

United States of America.tagline: Land of the Free – Innovation, Dreams, and Endless Horizons 🇺🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Washington D.C. is the capital of the USA, home to the White House, Congress, and the Supreme Court.
New York City is the most famous American city, known for the Statue of Liberty, Times Square, and Wall Street.
The USA has 50 states and one federal capital district (D.C.).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Statue of Liberty – A gift from France, standing in New York Harbor as a symbol of freedom.
Grand Canyon – A breathtaking gorge carved by the Colorado River, one mile deep and 446 km long.
Yellowstone National Park – The world's first national park, with geysers, hot springs, and bears.
Mount Rushmore – The faces of four US presidents carved into a South Dakota mountainside.
NASA Kennedy Space Centre – Where humans first launched to the Moon.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Technology – Silicon Valley is home to Apple, Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta.
Aerospace & Defence – NASA, Boeing, and Lockheed Martin lead global space and defence.
Entertainment – Hollywood is the world's most influential film and TV industry.
Agriculture – USA is the world's top producer of soybeans, corn, and beef.
Finance – New York's Wall Street is the world's largest stock market.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is the most widely spoken language; Spanish is spoken by over 40 million Americans.
