Native Americans (First Nations) were the original inhabitants of the land, with over 500 tribes recognised today.
The USA is a 'melting pot' of cultures from Europe, Africa, Asia, and the Americas.
American culture exports – jazz, hip-hop, baseball, basketball, and Hollywood – dominate global pop culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: The USA covers 9.8 million sq km, making it the world's 3rd largest country.
Spans from Atlantic to Pacific Oceans, with Alaska in the far northwest and Hawaii in the Pacific.
Geography includes the Rocky Mountains, Mississippi River, Great Plains, and Florida Everglades.
Climates range from Arctic (Alaska) to tropical (Hawaii, Florida) to desert (Arizona).

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The USA put a man on the Moon in 1969 – a feat no other country has matched!
Americans eat 3 billion pizzas per year – about 23 pounds per person!
The US economy is the world's largest, producing about 25% of global GDP.
The Library of Congress is the world's largest library with over 170 million items.

Canada.tagline: True North Strong and Free – Nature's Last Frontier 🇨🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Ottawa is Canada's capital, a bilingual city where English and French are equally official.
Toronto is Canada's largest city and most diverse, home to over 200 ethnic communities.
Vancouver, Montreal, and Calgary are other major Canadian cities.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Niagara Falls – One of the world's most powerful waterfalls, straddling the Canada-US border.
Banff National Park – A UNESCO World Heritage Site with turquoise lakes and the Canadian Rockies.
CN Tower, Toronto – Once the world's tallest free-standing structure (1976–2007).
Northern Lights (Aurora Borealis) – Best viewed from Yukon or Northwest Territories.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Natural Resources – Canada is a top producer of oil, natural gas, uranium, and timber.
Agriculture – Canada is a major exporter of wheat, canola, and maple syrup (Canada produces 71% of the world's maple syrup!).
Technology & AI – Toronto and Montreal are emerging global AI research hubs.
Film & Entertainment – Vancouver is Hollywood's favourite filming location (called 'Hollywood North').

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English and French are Canada's official languages; Quebec is a predominantly French-speaking province.
Indigenous peoples (First Nations, Métis, and Inuit) have lived in Canada for over 15,000 years.
Canada is officially multicultural, welcoming immigrants from every country in the world.
Hockey is Canada's national sport and a source of immense national pride.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Canada is the world's 2nd largest country by area at 10 million sq km.
Has the world's longest coastline (202,080 km) and the world's most lakes.
Borders only the USA to the south and shares the world's longest international border.
Geography ranges from Arctic tundra to Rocky Mountains to temperate rainforests.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Canada has more lakes than all other countries in the world combined!
Basketball was invented by a Canadian (James Naismith) in 1891.
Canada produces 71% of the world's maple syrup.
Canadians say 'sorry' so often that it became a legal issue – the 'Apology Act' in Ontario clarifies that saying sorry isn't an admission of guilt!

Mexico.tagline: Land of Colour – Ancient Civilisations and Vibrant Fiestas 🇲🇽

Capital City 🏛️.text: Mexico City is one of the world's largest cities with over 21 million people in the metro area.
Built on the ruins of Tenochtitlan, the ancient Aztec capital, it sits in a high-altitude valley.
Mexico City has one of the world's highest concentrations of museums.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Chichen Itza – A spectacular Mayan pyramid complex, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Teotihuacan – Ancient city near Mexico City with massive pyramids of the Sun and Moon.
Copper Canyon – A canyon system larger and deeper than the Grand Canyon.
Cancún & Tulum – Caribbean beaches with turquoise waters and ancient Mayan ruins.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Manufacturing – Mexico is a major producer of cars, electronics, and aerospace parts.
Agriculture – Mexico is the world's top producer of avocados, chillies, and limes.
Oil – PEMEX is Mexico's state oil company, one of the largest in the world.
Tourism – Mexico is the world's 7th most visited country for its beaches and ancient sites.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is the official language; Mexico has the world's largest Spanish-speaking population.
Over 68 indigenous languages are spoken, including Nahuatl (the Aztec language).
The Aztec, Maya, Olmec, and Zapotec civilisations built remarkable cities and calendars thousands of years ago.
Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) is a UNESCO-recognised tradition honouring ancestors.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Mexico covers 1.96 million sq km in North America, between the USA and Central America.
Has coastlines on both the Pacific Ocean and Gulf of Mexico / Caribbean Sea.
Geography includes deserts (Sonoran), tropical jungles, highlands, and volcanoes.
Popocatépetl is Mexico's most active volcano, visible from Mexico City.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Chocolate was invented by the ancient Aztecs and Mayans of Mexico!
Mexico City sinks about 10 cm per year because it was built on a lakebed.
Mexico is the 10th most biodiverse country on Earth.
The chihuahua (world's smallest dog breed) was named after a Mexican state.

Cuba.tagline: Isla Grande – Revolution, Rum, Salsa, and Classic Cars 🇨🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Havana (La Habana) is Cuba's capital, a UNESCO World Heritage city of colonial architecture and vintage cars.
Old Havana's pastel buildings, seafront Malecón, and jazz clubs make it one of the Americas' most atmospheric cities.
Cuba is the Caribbean's largest island, often called 'El Caiman' (the alligator) for its shape.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Old Havana (Habana Vieja) – A UNESCO World Heritage colonial city with fortresses, plazas, and baroque churches.
Viñales Valley – A UNESCO-listed valley with dramatic limestone mogotes (hills) and tobacco farms.
Trinidad – Another UNESCO colonial city, perfectly preserved, with cobblestone streets.
Varadero Beach – A 20-km stretch of white sand beach, one of the Caribbean's finest.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tobacco – Cuba is world-famous for its Havana cigars, hand-rolled and considered the world's finest.
Sugar & Rum – Cuba produces rum internationally known brands like Havana Club.
Tourism – A growing sector attracting visitors from around the world.
Healthcare – Cuba exports doctors and medical expertise to developing countries worldwide.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is Cuba's official language.
Cuban culture blends Spanish, African, and Caribbean influences in its music, dance, and food.
Salsa, son, and the cha-cha-chá all originated in Cuba – Cuba's gift to the world's dance floors!
Cuba has a 99.8% literacy rate – one of the highest in the Americas.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Cuba covers 109,884 sq km, the largest island in the Caribbean Sea.
Located 145 km south of Florida, USA, at the entrance to the Gulf of Mexico.
Mountainous in the east (Sierra Maestra), with fertile plains and tobacco valleys in the centre and west.
Tropical climate with hurricane season from June to November.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Havana is full of 1950s American cars kept running by Cuban ingenuity – you can take a taxi in a 70-year-old Chevrolet!
Cuba has more doctors per capita than almost any country in the world.
Ernest Hemingway lived in Cuba for 22 years and wrote The Old Man and the Sea there.
Cuba's classic car collection is one of the largest living museums of vintage automobiles anywhere on Earth.

National Animal 🐾.text: Cuban Trogon (Priotelus temnurus) – also the national bird

Costa Rica.tagline: Pura Vida! – Rainforests, No Army, and the Happiest People 🇨🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: San José is Costa Rica's capital, a modern city surrounded by volcanic mountains and coffee farms.
Costa Rica is known globally as a model for sustainability and peaceful coexistence with nature.
In 1948, Costa Rica abolished its army – one of the few nations in the world to have no military.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Arenal Volcano – A nearly perfect conical active volcano with hot springs at its base.
Manuel Antonio National Park – A tiny park where jungle meets the Pacific Ocean, teeming with wildlife.
Monteverde Cloud Forest Reserve – A magical misty forest where you walk above the clouds.
Tortuguero National Park – Accessible only by boat, a sea turtle nesting sanctuary.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Ecotourism – Costa Rica pioneered eco-tourism; 26% of its land is in protected national parks.
Coffee & Bananas – World-famous coffee and major banana exporter.
Medical Devices – Surprisingly, Costa Rica is a major exporter of medical devices to the USA.
Renewable Energy – Costa Rica regularly runs on 99% renewable electricity from hydro, wind, and solar.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is the official language.
'Pura Vida' (Pure Life) is the national motto and greeting, reflecting Costa Ricans' positive outlook on life.
Costa Rica has indigenous groups like the Bribri, Cabécar, and Ngäbe living in protected reserves.
Education and healthcare are free for all Costa Ricans, reflecting the country's social priorities.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Costa Rica covers 51,100 sq km in Central America, between Nicaragua and Panama.
Has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean.
Despite its small size, it contains 5% of the world's biodiversity.
Volcanoes, rainforests, cloud forests, mangroves, and coral reefs all exist in this tiny country.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Costa Rica has no army and abolished it in 1948 – the military budget is spent on education instead.
Costa Rica generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources.
Costa Rica has 5% of the world's biodiversity packed into 0.03% of the world's land area.
Costa Ricans (Ticos) consistently rank among the world's happiest people in global surveys.

Guatemala.tagline: Heart of the Maya – Tikal, Volcanoes, and Colourful Chichicastenango 🇬🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Guatemala City is the capital, the largest city in Central America.
Antigua Guatemala is the former colonial capital, a UNESCO World Heritage Baroque city surrounded by volcanoes.
Guatemala has the largest indigenous Maya population in Central America.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Tikal – UNESCO World Heritage ancient Maya city; temples rise above the jungle canopy.
Antigua – UNESCO colonial city of brightly painted buildings, cobblestone streets, and active volcanoes.
Lake Atitlán – A stunning volcanic caldera lake surrounded by indigenous Maya villages; Aldous Huxley called it the world's most beautiful lake.
Chichicastenango Market – One of the world's largest and most colourful indigenous markets.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Coffee – Guatemalan highland coffee (Antigua, Huehuetenango) is among the world's finest specialty coffees.
Agriculture – Bananas, sugar, palm oil, and cardamom (Guatemala is the world's largest cardamom producer).
Textiles – Hand-woven Maya textiles (huipiles) are world-renowned.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is official; 22 Mayan languages are also recognized.
Over 40% of Guatemala's population is indigenous Maya – the highest percentage in Central America.
Each Maya community has its own distinct traditional dress, woven with specific colours and patterns.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Guatemala covers 108,889 sq km in Central America.
Bordered by Mexico, Belize, Honduras, and El Salvador; coasts on both the Pacific and Caribbean.
Mountainous volcanic terrain; over 30 volcanoes including several active ones.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Guatemala is the world's largest cardamom producer – that spice in your chai latte likely comes from Guatemala!
Lake Atitlán sits in a volcanic caldera at 1,560m altitude and is so deep (340m) it has never been fully explored.
The Maya civilization invented the concept of zero independently!
Antigua's streets are lined with purple jacaranda trees that bloom spectacularly in spring.

Belize.tagline: Jewel of Central America – Blue Hole, Mayan Ruins, and Jungle Rivers 🇧🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Belmopan is Belize's capital, one of the world's newest capitals (moved from Belize City after a hurricane in 1961).
Belize City is the largest city on the Caribbean coast.
Belize is the only Central American country with English as its official language.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Great Blue Hole – A giant 300m wide, 125m deep marine sinkhole – one of the world's top diving sites.
Caracol Maya Ruins – Belize's largest Maya city, hidden in the jungle near Guatemala.
Belize Barrier Reef – UNESCO World Heritage; the second-largest barrier reef in the world.
Actun Tunichil Muknal Cave – A spectacular cave with Maya sacrificial remains and crystal-calcified skeletons.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Diving, jungles, and Maya ruins are major draws.
Sugar – A leading export crop.
Citrus & Bananas – Tropical agricultural exports.
Offshore Finance – Growing financial services.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is the official language; Creole, Spanish, and Maya languages are widely spoken.
Belize is uniquely diverse: Maya, Garifuna, Creole, Mestizo, Chinese, Mennonite, and Lebanese communities.
The Garifuna people of Belize have UNESCO-recognised music, dance, and cultural traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Belize covers 22,966 sq km – Central America's smallest country.
Bordered by Mexico and Guatemala, with a Caribbean coastline.
Belize Barrier Reef runs the length of the coastline.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Belize's Great Blue Hole is one of the world's most famous dive sites – a perfectly circular blue abyss visible from space.
Belize is the only country in Central America with English as its official language (it was British Honduras until 1981).
Belize's jaguar population is one of the largest and most protected in the world.
The Maya temples of Xunantunich are taller than any building in Belize City!

Honduras.tagline: Heart of the Americas – Copán Maya Ruins, Roatán Islands, and Cloud Forests 🇭🇳

Capital City 🏛️.text: Tegucigalpa is Honduras's capital and largest city.
San Pedro Sula is the industrial capital and a major Caribbean port.
Honduras hosts the UNESCO-listed Copán ruins – the 'Athens of the Maya world'.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Copán Maya Ruins – UNESCO World Heritage; famous for intricate stone stelae and the Hieroglyphic Stairway.
Bay Islands (Roatán, Utila) – Caribbean islands with world-class diving and whale shark encounters.
Pico Bonito National Park – Cloud forest with jaguars, ocelots, and hundreds of bird species.
Celaque National Park – Honduras's highest peak and most pristine cloud forest.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Textiles – Honduras is a major garment manufacturer for US brands.
Coffee – Highland coffee is a growing specialty export.
Agriculture – Bananas, palm oil, shrimp, and sugar.
Tourism – Diving and Maya ruins.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is the official language.
Honduras has Maya Ch'orti', Lenca, Miskito, and Garifuna indigenous communities.
The Garifuna of Honduras have UNESCO-recognised music and cultural traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Honduras covers 112,492 sq km in Central America.
Bordered by Guatemala, El Salvador, and Nicaragua; coasts on both Caribbean and Pacific.
Mostly mountainous with tropical coastal lowlands.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Copán's Hieroglyphic Stairway has the longest known Maya text – 2,200 glyphs carved on 72 steps!
Utila Island is one of the world's cheapest places to get PADI dive-certified, attracting backpackers from everywhere.
Honduras is home to the only baseball field in the world on a Bay Island in the middle of the Caribbean Sea.

El Salvador.tagline: Land of Volcanoes – Surfing Capital, Pupusas, and the Smallest Central American Nation 🇸🇻

Capital City 🏛️.text: San Salvador is El Salvador's capital, in a valley surrounded by volcanoes.
El Salvador is the smallest and most densely populated country in Central America.
El Salvador became the first country to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender in 2021.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Ruta de las Flores – A scenic road through colonial coffee-growing villages with flower festivals.
Joya de Cerén – UNESCO World Heritage; a Maya village preserved under volcanic ash like a Central American Pompeii.
El Boquerón – An active volcano with a perfect caldera you can walk around.
El Tunco Beach – A world-class surf break on the Pacific coast.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Remittances – Over 20% of GDP from Salvadorans living in the USA.
Coffee – High-altitude Salvadoran coffee is a specialty export.
Manufacturing – Textiles and electronics assembly.
Agriculture – Sugar, coffee, shrimp, and gold mining.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is the official language; El Salvador is the only Central American country with no significant indigenous language speakers.
Pupusas – thick corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, beans, or pork – are the national food and cultural icon.
El Salvador's 1980s civil war drove over 1 million Salvadorans to the USA.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: El Salvador covers 21,041 sq km – the smallest Central American country.
Bordered by Guatemala and Honduras; only Central American country with no Caribbean coast.
Chains of volcanoes run through the country; over 20 volcanic peaks.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: El Salvador is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coast.
Joya de Cerén was buried by volcanic ash in 600 AD – a complete Maya village preserved for 1,400 years!
El Salvador was the first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin as legal tender (2021).
Pupusas are El Salvador's national dish – there's even an annual National Pupusa Day!

Nicaragua.tagline: Land of Lakes and Volcanoes – Revolution, Corn Islands, and Colonial Granada 🇳🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: Managua is Nicaragua's capital on Lake Managua; the old city centre was destroyed by an earthquake in 1972.
Granada is Nicaragua's colonial gem, the oldest continuously inhabited Spanish-colonial city in the Americas.
Nicaragua was the site of a revolutionary war in the 1970s–80s between the Sandinistas and the Contras.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Ometepe Island – A stunning figure-8-shaped island in Lake Nicaragua, formed by two volcanoes.
Granada – A brightly coloured colonial city on Lake Nicaragua with baroque churches.
Masaya Volcano – The only volcano in the world you can drive to the rim and peer into an active lava lake.
Corn Islands – Remote Caribbean islands with white sand, crystal water, and lobster dinners.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Coffee, beef, sugar, and gold are the top exports.
Manufacturing – Textiles (free trade zones) for US brands.
Tourism – Colonial cities and unspoilt nature.
Remittances – A major economic support.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is official; Miskito and Creole English are spoken on the Caribbean coast.
Nicaragua has Miskito, Sumo, and Rama indigenous communities in the east.
Nicaraguan poetry is a national passion – Rubén Darío, one of the greatest Spanish-language poets, was Nicaraguan.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Nicaragua covers 130,374 sq km – Central America's largest country.
Bordered by Honduras and Costa Rica; coasts on both Pacific and Caribbean.
Lake Nicaragua is the largest lake in Central America.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Masaya Volcano allows you to drive to the crater's edge and look directly into an active lava lake – at night you can see the glow!
Lake Nicaragua has freshwater sharks – bull sharks swam upriver from the Caribbean and adapted to freshwater!
Nicaragua is Central America's largest country but one of its least populated.
Rubén Darío – Nicaragua's national poet – is considered the father of modernismo, influencing all of Spanish literature.

Panama.tagline: Crossroads of the World – Canal, Cloud Forests, and Two Oceans 🇵🇦

Capital City 🏛️.text: Panama City is the capital, a modern skyline rising from the Pacific alongside a 400-year-old colonial district.
Panama City is the only major city in the world with a rainforest within city limits.
The Panama Canal – one of the greatest engineering achievements in history – connects the Atlantic and Pacific.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Panama Canal – The 80km artificial waterway that allows 14,000 ships per year to cross between oceans.
Casco Viejo (Old Town) – UNESCO World Heritage colonial quarter with Spanish, French, and American heritage.
Bocas del Toro – Caribbean archipelago of idyllic beaches, coral reefs, and mangrove channels.
Cloud Forest of Chiriquí – Quetzals and endemic wildlife in the highlands above Boquete.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Panama Canal Tolls – The Canal generates $3+ billion per year in tolls.
Finance & Banking – Panama is a major international financial centre.
Shipping & Logistics – The world's second-largest free trade zone after Hong Kong.
Agriculture – Bananas, sugar, coffee (famous Geisha variety from Boquete), and shrimp.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is official; English is widely spoken.
Panama has indigenous Kuna (Guna), Ngäbe-Buglé, Emberá, and other communities.
The Kuna of the San Blas Islands are famous for their colourful mola textile art.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Panama covers 75,417 sq km in Central America.
The narrow land bridge connects North and South America; bordered by Costa Rica and Colombia.
The Continental Divide runs east-west; Pacific coast is drier, Caribbean is wet and lush.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Panama Canal shortens the journey between the Atlantic and Pacific by 12,000 km (no need to sail around South America)!
You can watch the sunrise on the Pacific and sunset on the Atlantic on the same day in Panama!
The Geisha coffee bean from Boquete, Panama, is the world's most expensive coffee – selling for $800+ per pound at auction.
Panama City is the only major city in the world with a tropical rainforest inside its city limits.

National Flower 🌸.text: Dove Orchid / Holy Ghost Orchid (Peristeria elata)

Dominican Republic.tagline: Caribbean Paradise – Merengue, Punta Cana Beaches, and Columbus Heritage 🇩🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Santo Domingo is the Dominican capital and the oldest continuously inhabited European settlement in the Americas, founded in 1496.
Punta Cana in the east is the main tourist resort area with some of the Caribbean's finest beaches.
The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Colonial Zone, Santo Domingo – UNESCO World Heritage; the first European city in the Americas with Christopher Columbus's remains.
Punta Cana – 48 km of white sand beaches and crystal-clear water on the Caribbean and Atlantic.
Samaná Peninsula – Humpback whales breed here January–March in the sheltered bay.
Pico Duarte – The highest peak in the Caribbean (3,098m), in the Cordillera Central.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – The Dominican Republic is the Caribbean's most visited destination.
Mining – Pueblo Viejo mine is one of the world's largest gold mines.
Sugar & Agriculture – Historically the leading sugar producer; now also cocoa and tobacco.
Manufacturing – Free trade zones produce medical devices and textiles.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is the official language.
Dominican culture is a vibrant blend of Spanish, African, and indigenous Taino heritage.
Merengue and Bachata – the national dances and music styles – are UNESCO-recognised and globally popular.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Dominican Republic covers 48,671 sq km on the eastern two-thirds of Hispaniola.
Bordered by Haiti to the west; surrounded by the Caribbean Sea and Atlantic Ocean.
The highest and lowest elevations in the Caribbean are both in the Dominican Republic.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Santo Domingo (1496) is the oldest continuously inhabited European city in the Americas!
The Dominican Republic has the Caribbean's highest peak (Pico Duarte, 3,098m) and the Caribbean's lowest point (Lake Enriquillo, 46m below sea level) – in the same country!
Bachata music originated in the Dominican Republic – now danced on every continent.

National Animal 🐾.text: Palm Chat (Dulus dominicus) – also the national bird

Haiti.tagline: Pearl of the Antilles – First Black Republic, Citadelle, and Haitian Art 🇭🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Port-au-Prince is Haiti's capital on the Caribbean coast.
Haiti was the first Black republic and first Caribbean nation to gain independence, in 1804.
Haiti's revolution was the only successful slave revolt in history, defeating Napoleon's army.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Citadelle Laferrière – UNESCO World Heritage; a massive mountain fortress built after independence to defend against French return.
Sans-Souci Palace – UNESCO World Heritage; ruins of King Henri Christophe's breathtaking Caribbean palace.
Labadee – A stunning coastal area on the northern coast.
Bassin Bleu – Gorgeous turquoise natural pools in the mountains near Jacmel.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Remittances – The Haitian diaspora (especially in the USA) sends over $3 billion annually.
Agriculture – Coffee, mangoes, and cocoa.
Textiles – A significant garment manufacturing sector in Port-au-Prince.
Arts – Haitian art and crafts are highly valued worldwide.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Haitian Creole and French are both official languages.
Haiti is one of the few countries where a creole language (Kreyòl ayisyen) is an official language.
Vodou (Voodoo) is an important Haitian religion – a blend of West African Vodun and Catholic traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Haiti covers 27,750 sq km on the western third of Hispaniola.
Bordered by the Dominican Republic; surrounded by the Caribbean Sea and Atlantic Ocean.
Mountainous (haiti means 'land of high mountains' in the Taino language).

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Haiti's revolution (1791–1804) is the ONLY successful slave revolt in human history – enslaved people defeated Napoleon's army!
Haiti was the first country in the Western Hemisphere to abolish slavery.
The Citadelle Laferrière is the largest fortress in the Western Hemisphere, built by freed slaves!
Haitian mango (Madame Francis) is considered one of the world's finest mango varieties.

Jamaica.tagline: One Love – Reggae, Bolt's Speed, Blue Mountains, and Jerk Everything 🇯🇲

Capital City 🏛️.text: Kingston is Jamaica's capital, birthplace of reggae and dancehall music.
Montego Bay in the north is Jamaica's main tourist resort area.
Jamaica was the first Caribbean country to gain independence from Britain (1962).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Blue Mountains – A UNESCO World Heritage coffee-growing mountain range; Blue Mountain Peak is 2,256m.
Dunn's River Falls – A famous tiered waterfall that visitors climb hand-in-hand.
Bob Marley Museum, Kingston – The legendary musician's former home.
Port Royal – Once the wickedest city in the world, the former pirate capital that sank into the sea in the 1692 earthquake.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Jamaica's beaches, music, and culture attract 4+ million visitors.
Blue Mountain Coffee – One of the world's most expensive and sought-after coffees.
Bauxite & Aluminium – Jamaica is a major bauxite producer.
Rum – Jamaica produces some of the world's finest aged rums.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; Jamaican Patois (Creole) is the everyday language.
Jamaica has given the world reggae, Bob Marley, Usain Bolt, and Blue Mountain coffee.
Jamaica has won more Olympic medals per capita than almost any country outside the US and UK.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Jamaica covers 10,990 sq km – the third-largest Caribbean island.
A Caribbean island south of Cuba and west of Haiti.
Mountainous interior with the Blue Mountains in the east.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Usain Bolt – the world's fastest human (9.58 seconds for 100m) – is Jamaican!
Jamaica has the world's most church buildings per square kilometre!
Bob Marley's Legend album has sold 28+ million copies – the best-selling reggae album ever.
Jamaica's Blue Mountain coffee is 100% shade-grown in the misty mountains and sells for $50+ per pound.

Trinidad and Tobago.tagline: Land of the Hummingbird – Carnival, Steel Pan, and Oil Wealth 🇹🇹

Capital City 🏛️.text: Port of Spain is Trinidad and Tobago's capital, the economic and cultural hub of the southern Caribbean.
Trinidad and Tobago is the southernmost country in the Caribbean, just 11 km from Venezuela.
T&T invented the steel pan – the only acoustic musical instrument invented in the 20th century!

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Carnival – One of the world's greatest festivals; four days of costumes, calypso, soca music, and dancing.
Caroni Bird Sanctuary – Thousands of scarlet ibis return to roost at sunset, an unforgettable spectacle.
Pitch Lake – The world's largest natural asphalt lake; tar naturally bubbles up in a 40-hectare deposit.
Tobago's Buccoo Reef – Coral reef snorkelling in crystal clear water with the Nylon Pool sandbank.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil & Gas – T&T has the Caribbean's largest hydrocarbon reserves.
Petrochemicals – A major global producer of methanol and ammonia.
Tourism – Carnival, diving, and ecotourism.
Rum – Angostura bitters (used in cocktails worldwide) is made in T&T.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; T&T is one of the Caribbean's most ethnically diverse societies.
Roughly 35% Indo-Trinidadian and 35% Afro-Trinidadian, plus Chinese, Syrian, European, and Amerindian communities.
Steel pan, calypso, and soca music all originated in Trinidad and have spread worldwide.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: T&T covers 5,128 sq km; two islands in the southern Caribbean.
Trinidad is just 11 km from Venezuela's coast.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The steel pan is the ONLY acoustic instrument invented in the 20th century – and it came from Trinidad!
Pitch Lake in Trinidad is the world's largest natural asphalt deposit – Sir Walter Raleigh caulked his ships here in 1595!
Trinidad and Tobago produces the world's hottest chili sauce – the Trinidadian Moruga Scorpion was the world's hottest pepper!
Angostura bitters – in almost every cocktail bar worldwide – is made in Trinidad.

Brazil.tagline: Land of Carnival – Amazon, Samba, and Endless Joy 🇧🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Brasília is Brazil's capital, a purpose-built city designed in the 1950s and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
São Paulo is Brazil's largest city and Latin America's financial powerhouse.
Rio de Janeiro is the most famous Brazilian city, known for Carnival, beaches, and Christ the Redeemer.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Christ the Redeemer – A giant statue of Jesus standing atop Corcovado Mountain in Rio, one of the New Seven Wonders.
Amazon Rainforest – The world's largest tropical rainforest, home to 10% of all species on Earth.
Iguaçu Falls – A spectacular set of 275 waterfalls wider than Niagara on the Argentina-Brazil border.
Rio Carnival – The world's biggest party, with samba parades, costumes, and millions of revellers.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Brazil is the world's largest producer of coffee, sugar, orange juice, and soybeans.
Mining – Brazil holds vast reserves of iron ore, gold, and bauxite.
Biofuels – Brazil is a global leader in sugarcane ethanol production.
Aviation – Embraer is one of the world's top commercial aircraft manufacturers.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Portuguese is Brazil's official language; Brazil is the world's largest Portuguese-speaking country.
Brazil has the largest Japanese population outside Japan and the largest Lebanese population outside Lebanon!
Over 300 indigenous tribes live in the Amazon, some with no contact with the outside world.
Capoeira (martial art dance), bossa nova, samba, and football are Brazil's cultural gifts to the world.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Brazil covers 8.5 million sq km, making it the world's 5th largest country.
The Amazon River flows through Brazil – the world's largest river by water volume.
Brazil shares borders with every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
Climate ranges from equatorial rainforest in the north to subtropical in the south.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Brazil has won the Football World Cup 5 times – more than any other country!
The Amazon River releases so much freshwater that it dilutes the Atlantic Ocean for 100 miles from shore.
Brazil is home to the world's largest carnival celebration in Rio de Janeiro.
Brazil is the only country in South America where Portuguese is spoken.

Argentina.tagline: Land of Silver – Tango, Steak, and Patagonian Wilds 🇦🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Buenos Aires is Argentina's capital, known as the 'Paris of South America' for its European architecture.
It is a city of passionate tango dancing, rich coffee culture, and late-night dining.
Buenos Aires has the widest avenue in the world – Avenida 9 de Julio with 16 lanes.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Iguaçu Falls (Argentine side) – The most dramatic viewpoint of the world's widest waterfall system.
Perito Moreno Glacier – A rare advancing glacier in Patagonia where you can hear ice cracking and calving.
Aconcagua – At 6,961m, the highest mountain in the Americas and the Southern Hemisphere.
Ushuaia – 'The End of the World', the southernmost city, gateway to Antarctica.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Argentina is the world's leading exporter of soy products and one of the top beef exporters.
Wine – Mendoza's Malbec wine is world-renowned.
Mining – Rich in lithium, copper, and gold deposits.
Automobile manufacturing and chemical industries are major sectors.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is the official language of Argentina.
Argentine Spanish has a distinctive Italian-influenced accent and its own slang (lunfardo).
Indigenous peoples like the Mapuche, Quechua, and Guaraní have rich cultural traditions.
Tango was born in Buenos Aires in the late 19th century and is now a UNESCO cultural heritage.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Argentina covers 2.78 million sq km, the 8th largest country in the world.
Stretches from the tropical north to the icy tip of South America near Antarctica.
Geography includes the Andes Mountains, Pampas grasslands, Patagonian steppe, and Tierra del Fuego.
The Paraná River is South America's second longest river, flowing through Argentina.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Argentina won the 2022 FIFA World Cup led by the legendary Lionel Messi!
Argentina produced 5 Nobel Peace Prize winners and 3 Nobel Science winners.
Buenos Aires has the highest number of therapists (psychologists) per capita in the world.
Argentina is shaped almost like an inverted triangle, pointing towards Antarctica.

Colombia.tagline: Where Flowers, Coffee, and Colour Bloom 🇨🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bogotá is Colombia's capital, sitting at 2,625m above sea level in the Andes, making it one of the world's highest capitals.
Medellín, once notorious, has transformed into one of the world's most innovative cities.
Cartagena is a beautifully preserved colonial walled city on the Caribbean coast.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Salt Cathedral of Zipaquirá – An underground Catholic cathedral built inside a salt mine.
Los Nevados National Park – Stunning highland volcanoes with year-round snow near the equator.
Tayrona National Park – Where the Andes meet the Caribbean Sea with pristine beaches.
Coffee Cultural Landscape – UNESCO-listed coffee farms on Andean slopes.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Coffee – Colombian coffee is world-famous for its smooth flavour and quality.
Flowers – Colombia is the world's 2nd largest flower exporter, supplying 80% of US flower imports.
Emeralds – Colombia produces 70–90% of the world's emeralds.
Oil & Mining – Major oil and coal exporter in South America.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is Colombia's official language.
Colombia has 65 officially recognised indigenous languages and groups, including Wayuu and Kogui.
Vallenato music and cumbia dance are UNESCO-recognised cultural traditions.
Colombia is the most biodiverse country per square kilometre on Earth.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Colombia covers 1.14 million sq km in northwestern South America.
The only country in South America with both Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea coastlines.
The Andes Mountains run through western Colombia; Amazon jungle covers the east.
Colombia sits on the equator and has no seasons – just rainy and dry periods.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Colombia has more species of birds than any other country in the world – over 1,900 species!
Gabriel García Márquez, author of 'One Hundred Years of Solitude', was Colombian and won the Nobel Prize.
Colombia's City of Gold (El Dorado) legend inspired European explorers for centuries.
Medellín was named the world's most innovative city in 2013 for its transformation from strife to prosperity.

Peru.tagline: Land of the Incas – Machu Picchu, Amazon, and Ancient Gold 🇵🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Lima is Peru's capital, a coastal megacity of over 10 million people and South America's culinary capital.
Cusco, high in the Andes at 3,399m, was the capital of the Inca Empire and is a UNESCO World Heritage city.
Peru was the centre of the great Inca Empire, the largest empire in pre-Columbian America.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Machu Picchu – The iconic 15th-century Inca citadel on a mountain top, one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
Nazca Lines – Giant geoglyphs of animals and shapes carved into the desert, visible only from the air.
Amazon River Source – The mighty Amazon begins in the Peruvian Andes.
Lake Titicaca – The world's highest navigable lake, shared with Bolivia at 3,812m above sea level.
Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca) – A naturally multi-coloured mountain in the Andes, striped in vivid colours.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Mining – Peru is the world's 2nd largest silver and copper producer.
Food Exports – Peru exports asparagus, avocados, blueberries, and quinoa globally.
Fishing – Peru is one of the world's top fishing nations (anchovies, sardines).
Tourism – Machu Picchu and the Inca Trail attract over 1 million visitors annually.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish, Quechua (Inca language), and Aymara are all official languages.
Peru has over 70 indigenous ethnic groups, many living in the Amazon rainforest.
Quechua was the language of the Inca Empire and is still spoken by over 8 million people today.
Lima is considered the gastronomic capital of South America – ceviche, lomo saltado, and causa are globally celebrated.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Peru covers 1.28 million sq km in South America.
Has three distinct zones: desert coast, Andean highlands, and Amazon jungle.
The Amazon rainforest covers 60% of Peru's territory.
Shares the Andes with Ecuador, Colombia, Bolivia, Chile, and Argentina.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Machu Picchu was built without mortar or wheels – the stones fit so perfectly that not even a knife blade can slide between them!
The Nazca Lines are so large and precise that many wonder how the ancient people made them without flying.
Peru has over 3,000 varieties of potato – potato was first cultivated in Peru over 7,000 years ago!
Lima has the world's second-tallest sand dune (Cerro Blanco) just outside the city.

Chile.tagline: Land of Extremes – Atacama to Patagonia, Desert to Ice 🇨🇱

Capital City 🏛️.text: Santiago is Chile's capital, a modern city nestled between the Andes and the Pacific coast.
Valparaíso is Chile's UNESCO World Heritage port city, famous for colourful hillside houses and street art.
Chile stretches 4,300 km north to south – one of the world's longest countries.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Atacama Desert – The world's driest non-polar desert, with alien-like landscapes and the best stargazing on Earth.
Torres del Paine National Park – Dramatic granite towers, glaciers, and condors in Chilean Patagonia.
Easter Island (Rapa Nui) – A remote Pacific island with nearly 1,000 mysterious moai stone statues.
Marble Caves (Cuevas de Mármol) – Stunning turquoise caves carved into marble islands in Patagonia.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Copper – Chile is the world's largest copper producer, holding 28% of global reserves.
Lithium – Chile has the world's largest lithium reserves, crucial for electric batteries.
Wine – Chilean wine from the Maipo and Colchagua valleys is exported worldwide.
Salmon – Chile is the world's 2nd largest salmon producer after Norway.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is Chile's official language.
Mapuche are Chile's largest indigenous group, with a proud history of resisting both Inca and Spanish conquest.
Chilean Spanish has a distinctive, rapid accent and unique slang ('chilenismos').
Cueca (dance), empanadas, and cazuela stew are beloved cultural traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Chile covers 756,102 sq km but is only 177 km wide on average – the world's most elongated country.
Runs along the entire western coast of South America from Peru to Tierra del Fuego.
Extreme geography: Atacama Desert in the north, fertile heartland in the centre, glaciers and fjords in the south.
The Andes form Chile's entire eastern border with Argentina.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Atacama Desert is so dry that some areas have never recorded rainfall in human history!
Chile's Atacama has the world's clearest skies – 300+ nights of perfect stargazing per year.
Chile's Easter Island is one of the most remote inhabited places on Earth, 3,700 km from mainland Chile.
In 2010, 33 Chilean miners were rescued alive after 69 days trapped underground – the world watched in joy!

Venezuela.tagline: Land of Grace – Angel Falls, Oil Wealth, and Colourful Coasts 🇻🇪

Capital City 🏛️.text: Caracas is Venezuela's capital, surrounded by the dramatic Avila Mountain.
Venezuela was the first South American country to be settled by Europeans (1498).
Simón Bolívar, liberator of six South American nations, was born in Caracas in 1783.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Angel Falls (Salto Ángel) – The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall at 979 metres, in Canaima National Park.
Canaima National Park – A UNESCO World Heritage site of ancient flat-topped tepuis (table mountains).
Los Roques Archipelago – A stunning Caribbean coral atoll with crystal blue waters.
Mount Roraima – The inspiration for Arthur Conan Doyle's 'The Lost World', rising from the jungle in a cloud.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves, even more than Saudi Arabia.
Agriculture – Coffee, cocoa, and tropical fruits are traditional exports.
Mining – Rich in gold, diamonds, bauxite, and iron ore.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is Venezuela's official language.
Over 30 indigenous groups including the Yanomami, Warao, and Pemón live in Venezuela's interior.
Venezuelan culture is warm and festive, known for joropo music, dancing, and llanero (cowboy) traditions.
Venezuelan food includes arepas (corn cakes), pabellón criollo, and hallacas.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Venezuela covers 916,445 sq km in northern South America.
Bordered by Colombia, Brazil, and Guyana, with a long Caribbean coast.
Geography spans Caribbean beaches, Andes mountains, Orinoco River basin, and Guiana Highlands.
The Orinoco River is one of South America's longest rivers, flowing through Venezuela.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Angel Falls is 15 times higher than Niagara Falls – the water atomises into mist before reaching the bottom!
Venezuela has won more Miss World and Miss Universe titles than any other country.
Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves yet struggles to produce enough.
The tepuis of Venezuela are so old and isolated that many species found there exist nowhere else on Earth.

National Animal 🐾.text: Troupial (Icterus icterus) – also the national bird

Ecuador.tagline: Middle of the World – Galápagos, Amazon, Andes, and Quito's Eternal Spring 🇪🇨

Capital City 🏛️.text: Quito is Ecuador's capital, the world's highest official capital city at 2,850m, known as 'the City of Eternal Spring'.
Quito's Old Town was the first city declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1978).
Ecuador is named after the Equator (Ecuadorial) that crosses through it.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Galápagos Islands – UNESCO World Heritage; the archipelago that inspired Darwin's theory of evolution.
Quito Old Town – UNESCO World Heritage; the best-preserved colonial city in Latin America.
Cotopaxi Volcano – One of the world's highest active volcanoes (5,897m).
Amazon Rainforest – Ecuador's Yasuní National Park is one of the world's most biodiverse spots.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Ecuador is South America's 5th largest oil producer.
Bananas – Ecuador is the world's largest banana exporter; the Cavendish banana was developed here.
Flowers – Ecuador is the world's 3rd largest cut flower exporter; roses grow year-round in the Andes.
Cocoa – Ecuadorian fine-flavour cocoa is the world's most prized chocolate ingredient.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is official; Kichwa (Quechua) and Shuar are also official indigenous languages.
Ecuador has over 13 indigenous nationalities including Quechua, Shuar, Huaorani (Waorani), and Afro-Ecuadorian communities.
The Panama hat was actually invented in Ecuador! It gets its name from being shipped through Panama.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Ecuador covers 283,561 sq km in northwestern South America.
Bordered by Colombia and Peru; has Pacific and Amazon coastlines.
Four distinct regions: Galápagos Islands, Pacific coast, Andean highlands, and Amazon jungle.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Panama hat was actually invented in Ecuador! Ecuadorian weavers made them – they got the name because they were shipped via Panama.
Darwin's visit to the Galápagos in 1835 directly inspired On the Origin of Species – the book that changed biology.
Galápagos tortoises can live over 150 years – the oldest confirmed tortoise (Jonathan) is alive today at 191!
Ecuador's Yasuní National Park has more tree species per hectare than all of North America combined.

Bolivia.tagline: Roof of the World – Uyuni Salt Flats, Lake Titicaca, and Highest Capital 🇧🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Sucre is Bolivia's constitutional capital; La Paz is the seat of government and highest administrative capital in the world (3,640m).
Bolivia has two capitals – the only country in the world to do so officially.
Bolivia is one of South America's two landlocked countries (with Paraguay).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Salar de Uyuni – The world's largest salt flat (10,582 sq km); creates perfect mirror reflections after rain.
Lake Titicaca – The world's highest navigable lake (3,812m), shared with Peru; home to the floating Uros islands.
Tiwanaku – UNESCO World Heritage ruins of a pre-Inca civilisation, 3,500 years old.
Death Road (Yungas Road) – A terrifying mountain road popular with thrill-seeking mountain bikers.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Lithium – Bolivia has the world's largest lithium reserves (the 'Saudi Arabia of lithium').
Natural Gas – Bolivia is South America's 2nd largest gas producer.
Mining – Tin, silver, zinc, and gold from the Andes.
Agriculture – Quinoa (Bolivia produces much of the world's quinoa), soybeans, and coca.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is official along with 36 indigenous languages including Quechua and Aymara.
Bolivia has the highest proportion of indigenous population in South America – about 40%.
Cholitas – indigenous Aymara women in colourful skirts and bowler hats – are an iconic Bolivian cultural image.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Bolivia covers 1.098 million sq km in central South America.
A landlocked country bordered by Peru, Chile, Argentina, Paraguay, and Brazil.
Three zones: Altiplano (high plateau), Yungas (valleys), and Llanos (lowland plains).

Unique Facts 🌟.text: The Salar de Uyuni is so flat and clear that NASA uses it to calibrate altitude sensors on satellites!
Bolivia has the world's largest lithium reserves – crucial for electric vehicle batteries.
La Paz has the world's longest cable car network (urban teleférico system) – used by locals for daily commuting!
Death Road was nicknamed the world's most dangerous road – cyclists now bike down it as a thrill-seeking adventure.

Paraguay.tagline: Heart of South America – Jesuit Ruins, Yachting Capital, and Guaraní Pride 🇵🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Asunción is Paraguay's capital and South America's oldest city continuously governed by Europeans (1537).
Paraguay is one of South America's two landlocked countries.
Paraguay is the world's largest exporter of electricity and runs almost entirely on hydropower.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Jesuit Missions of La Santísima Trinidad – UNESCO World Heritage; spectacular ruins of Jesuit indigenous communities.
Pantanal (Paraguay section) – Part of the world's largest tropical wetland, with jaguars and giant river otters.
Itaipú Dam – One of the world's largest hydroelectric dams, shared with Brazil; produces 15% of Brazil's electricity.
Chaco – A vast, largely unexplored subtropical wilderness.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Hydropower – Paraguay exports the vast majority of Itaipú Dam's power to Brazil and Argentina.
Agriculture – Paraguay is among the world's top soybean and beef exporters.
Tobacco & Cotton – Traditional exports.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish and Guaraní are both official languages – Paraguay is the only country where an indigenous language is spoken by the majority.
Guaraní is spoken by 90% of Paraguayans – the most successful indigenous language survival in the Americas.
The Chaco War (1932–35) against Bolivia was one of South America's bloodiest 20th-century conflicts.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Paraguay covers 406,752 sq km in central South America.
Landlocked, bordered by Argentina, Bolivia, and Brazil.
The Paraguay River divides the country into the fertile Eastern region and the wild Chaco in the west.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where an indigenous language (Guaraní) is used by the majority of the population in daily life!
Itaipú Dam is one of the world's largest power stations – generating enough electricity to power all of Argentina.
Paraguay's Triple Alliance War (1864–1870) killed 60-70% of Paraguay's entire male population!

Uruguay.tagline: Quiet Jewel – Uruguay's Social Democracy, Carneval, and Mate Culture 🇺🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Montevideo is Uruguay's capital and largest city; it is consistently ranked South America's most liveable city.
Uruguay is South America's smallest Spanish-speaking country.
Uruguay was the first country in the world to legalise cannabis (2013) and same-sex marriage (2013).

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Colonia del Sacramento – UNESCO World Heritage; a Portuguese colonial town on the Río de la Plata, accessible by ferry from Buenos Aires.
Punta del Este – South America's most glamorous beach resort and art scene.
Montevideo's Old Town (Ciudad Vieja) – A walkable historic centre of cafes, tango milongas, and art deco buildings.
Salto Grande Dam – Uruguay's largest dam on the Uruguay River.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – Uruguay is one of the world's top beef and wool exporters per capita.
Software – Uruguay's 'Uruware' tech sector is a growing export.
Tourism – Buenos Aires day-trippers and South American beach tourism.
Renewable Energy – Uruguay generates 98% of its electricity from renewables (mostly wind).

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Spanish is Uruguay's official language.
Uruguay has no significant indigenous population today.
Uruguay's political culture is very progressive – it was one of the first countries with free public education and state secularism.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Uruguay covers 176,215 sq km in southeastern South America.
Bordered by Argentina and Brazil; coastlines on the Río de la Plata and Atlantic Ocean.
Mostly flat rolling plains (pampas) with the Cuchilla Grande hills in the north.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Uruguay generates 98% of its electricity from renewable sources – among the world's highest!
Uruguay was the first country to legalise and regulate marijuana, same-sex marriage, and abortion all in one year (2013).
Uruguay's former president José Mujica lived in a farmhouse, donated 90% of his salary to charity, and drove a 1987 VW Beetle!
Uruguay has more cattle than people – about 11.5 million cattle for 3.5 million people.

Guyana.tagline: Land of Many Waters – Kaieteur Falls, Rupununi, and Caribbean Coast 🇬🇾

Capital City 🏛️.text: Georgetown is Guyana's capital, a city of wooden colonial buildings and Dutch-laid canals.
Guyana is South America's only English-speaking country.
Guyana recently became one of the world's top oil producers after massive offshore discoveries in 2015.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Kaieteur Falls – One of the world's most powerful waterfalls; 5x wider than Niagara and 4x taller, hidden in pristine jungle.
Rupununi Savannah – A vast untouched savannah with giant anteaters, giant river otters, and jaguars.
Iwokrama Rainforest – One of the world's last untouched primary rainforests.
Mount Roraima – A flat-topped tepui that inspired Arthur Conan Doyle's 'The Lost World'.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Oil – Major offshore ExxonMobil discovery; Guyana is now one of the world's fastest-growing oil producers.
Gold & Bauxite – Long-established mining sector.
Sugar & Rice – Traditional agricultural exports.
Timber – Rich tropical hardwood forests.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is official; Guyanese Creole is the everyday tongue.
Guyana is the most ethnically diverse South American country: Indo-Guyanese, Afro-Guyanese, and indigenous Amerindian groups.
Guyana's 'El Dorado' legend inspired Spanish conquistadors – the mythical city of gold was supposedly in the Guyanese interior.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Guyana covers 214,969 sq km in northeastern South America.
Bordered by Venezuela, Brazil, and Suriname; Atlantic coast in the north.
80% covered by Amazon rainforest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Kaieteur Falls has 4x the height of Niagara and 5x the width – yet is so remote it's barely visited.
Guyana is the ONLY English-speaking country in South America.
One of the world's largest oil discoveries of the 21st century was made offshore Guyana in 2015 – transforming a tiny poor nation.

Suriname.tagline: Amazon's Caribbean Jewel – Rainforest Republic, Dutch Heritage, and Maroon Culture 🇸🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Paramaribo is Suriname's capital, a UNESCO World Heritage city of Dutch colonial wooden buildings.
Suriname is South America's smallest sovereign country.
Suriname is the only Dutch-speaking country in South America.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Paramaribo Historic Centre – UNESCO World Heritage; unique Dutch colonial wooden architecture in the tropics.
Central Suriname Nature Reserve – UNESCO World Heritage; one of the world's largest protected primary tropical rainforests.
Brownsberg Nature Park – Rainforest plateau above Brokopondo Lake.
Galibi Nature Reserve – Leatherback sea turtle nesting beaches.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Gold & Bauxite – Mining accounts for most of Suriname's export earnings.
Oil – Offshore exploration is developing.
Timber – Controlled timber extraction from vast forests.
Agriculture – Rice and bananas from the coastal plain.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Dutch is the official language – the only Dutch-speaking country in South America.
Suriname is extraordinarily diverse: Hindu Indians, Javanese, Afro-Surinamese (Creole), Maroons, indigenous Amerindians, Chinese, and Dutch.
Maroons – descendants of escaped slaves who created free communities in the jungle – maintain a unique African-derived culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Suriname covers 163,820 sq km in northeastern South America.
Bordered by Guyana, Brazil, and French Guiana; Atlantic coast in the north.
80% covered by pristine Amazon rainforest.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Suriname is the ONLY Dutch-speaking country in South America.
The Maroons of Suriname – descendants of escaped slaves – have preserved 17th-18th century West African culture in the jungle for 300 years.
Suriname's Central Nature Reserve covers 10% of the country and is virtually untouched.
Paramaribo has a mosque and a synagogue next to each other, with their congregations sharing Ramadan and Passover celebrations!

Australia.tagline: Land Down Under – Kangaroos, Coral, and Outback Adventure 🇦🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Canberra is Australia's capital, chosen as a compromise between rival cities Sydney and Melbourne.
Sydney is the most famous Australian city with its iconic Opera House and Harbour Bridge.
Australia is both a country and a continent – the only nation to occupy an entire continent.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Sydney Opera House – One of the 20th century's most iconic buildings, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Great Barrier Reef – The world's largest coral reef system, visible from space, home to 9,000 species.
Uluru (Ayers Rock) – A massive red sandstone monolith sacred to the Aboriginal Anangu people.
Great Ocean Road – A stunning coastal drive with the Twelve Apostles limestone stacks.
Kakadu National Park – Ancient Aboriginal rock art site and wildlife haven in the Northern Territory.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Mining – Australia is a top exporter of iron ore, coal, gold, and lithium.
Agriculture – Wool, beef, wheat, and wine are major exports.
Tourism – The Great Barrier Reef, Uluru, and Sydney draw millions of visitors.
Education & Research – Australia has world-class universities attracting international students.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English is the primary language; there is no official language but English is used in government.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have lived in Australia for over 65,000 years – the world's oldest living culture.
Over 250 Aboriginal languages existed before European settlement; about 120 are still spoken.
Australian slang (g'day, arvo, brekky) is a unique and beloved part of the culture.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Australia covers 7.7 million sq km, making it the world's 6th largest country.
Surrounded by the Indian Ocean to the west and the Pacific Ocean to the east.
The vast interior – the Outback – is one of the hottest, driest places on Earth.
Australia drifts northward at 7 cm per year due to tectonic plate movement.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Australia has more unique species than any other continent – kangaroos, koalas, platypuses, and wombats are found nowhere else!
The platypus is one of the world's strangest animals: a mammal that lays eggs and has a duck's bill!
Australia is the driest inhabited continent on Earth.
Over 80% of Australians live in cities within 50 km of the coast, leaving the vast interior almost empty.

New Zealand.tagline: Aotearoa – Land of the Long White Cloud and Middle-Earth 🇳🇿

Capital City 🏛️.text: Wellington is New Zealand's capital, a compact, windy, and vibrant city at the southern tip of the North Island.
Auckland is the largest city, home to one-third of New Zealand's population.
New Zealand's indigenous name 'Aotearoa' means 'Land of the Long White Cloud' in Māori.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Fiordland National Park – Dramatic fjords including Milford Sound, one of the world's most photographed places.
Tongariro Alpine Crossing – An active volcanic landscape that doubled as Mordor in The Lord of the Rings films.
Bay of Islands – Beautiful subtropical bay with Māori cultural heritage.
Hobbiton – The real film set in Matamata, where The Hobbit and Lord of the Rings were filmed.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Agriculture – New Zealand is famous for dairy, lamb, kiwifruit, and wine.
Film Industry – Weta Workshop (Lord of the Rings, Avatar) is world-class.
Tourism – Stunning landscapes attract adventure and eco-tourism.
Wool & Timber – New Zealand merino wool is among the world's finest.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English and Māori are both official languages; Māori was the language of New Zealand's first people.
The Māori arrived in New Zealand about 700 years ago from Polynesia in canoes.
The haka (war dance) is a powerful Māori tradition performed by the All Blacks rugby team before matches.
New Zealand was the first country in the world to give women the right to vote (1893).

Area & Geography 🌍.text: New Zealand covers 268,021 sq km, made up of two main islands (North and South) and many smaller ones.
Located in the southwestern Pacific Ocean, about 1,500 km southeast of Australia.
The Southern Alps run along the South Island with peaks over 3,700m.
Sits on the 'Ring of Fire' with active volcanoes and frequent earthquakes.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: New Zealand has more sheep than people – about 5 sheep per person!
The kiwi bird is nocturnal, flightless, and lays the largest egg relative to its body of any bird.
New Zealand was the last major landmass to be settled by humans (only 700 years ago).
The All Blacks rugby team has the highest win rate of any sports team in history.

Fiji.tagline: Bula! – Island Paradise of Smiles and Blue Lagoons 🇫🇯

Capital City 🏛️.text: Suva is Fiji's capital, located on the island of Viti Levu.
Nadi is the tourist gateway city, home to the international airport and resort areas.
Fiji is a Pacific island nation comprising 333 islands.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mamanuca Islands – A chain of stunning small islands with white sand beaches and coral reefs.
Garden of the Sleeping Giant – A beautiful orchid garden near Nadi.
Sigatoka Sand Dunes – Fiji's first national park with ancient archaeological sites.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Fiji's beaches and resorts are the backbone of its economy.
Sugar – Sugarcane is Fiji's main agricultural product and export.
Fiji Water – Fiji's natural artesian water is exported globally and is a premium brand.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Fijian and English are official languages; Hindi is also widely spoken due to Indian-Fijian communities.
'Bula!' is the Fijian greeting meaning hello and good health – you'll hear it everywhere!
Fijians are known as some of the world's friendliest people.
Traditional meke (dance) and kava ceremony are important cultural practices.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Fiji covers 18,274 sq km across 333 islands in the South Pacific Ocean.
About 110 islands are inhabited; the two largest are Viti Levu and Vanua Levu.
Tropical climate with warm temperatures year-round and a wet season November–April.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Fiji sits right on the International Date Line – one of the first countries to start each new day!
The Fijian rugby sevens team is world-famous for its athleticism and flair.
Fiji has some of the world's most pristine coral reefs and is a top scuba diving destination.

Papua New Guinea.tagline: Land of the Unexpected – Birds of Paradise, Tribal Culture, and Wild Rivers 🇵🇬

Capital City 🏛️.text: Port Moresby is Papua New Guinea's capital on the Coral Sea coast.
PNG is the world's most linguistically diverse country with over 800 languages spoken.
PNG is the 3rd largest island country in the world and has some of the world's most isolated communities.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Kokoda Track – A 96km jungle trail that was the scene of fierce WWII battles; now a historic trekking route.
Sepik River – One of the great wild rivers of the world, with extraordinary tribal art and culture.
Mt Wilhelm – The country's highest peak (4,509m).
Raja Ampat (nearby) – Some of the world's most biodiverse coral reefs in western PNG.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Minerals – PNG is a major producer of gold, copper, silver, nickel, and cobalt.
Oil & Gas – LNG exports are a major and growing revenue source.
Agriculture – Coffee, cocoa, and palm oil.
Timber – Tropical hardwood logging.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: PNG has over 800 languages – more than any other country on Earth!
Tok Pisin (a creole English-based language) serves as the lingua franca.
PNG has over 1,000 tribal groups; many communities in the highlands had never contacted the outside world until the 20th century.
Elaborate tribal body painting, feather headdresses, and Sing-Sing festivals are extraordinary cultural traditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: PNG covers 462,840 sq km in Oceania.
Occupies the eastern half of New Guinea island; western half is Indonesian Papua.
Bordered by Indonesia to the west; surrounded by Coral Sea, Bismarck Sea, and Solomon Sea.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Papua New Guinea has more languages than any country in the world – over 800!
PNG's Highlands was one of the world's last regions of contact – some communities first met outsiders in the 1930s.
PNG's birds of paradise – with extraordinary plumage – inspired national costumes and are icons of evolutionary spectacle.
The penis gourd (koteka) is still worn as traditional dress by some Highland men.

Solomon Islands.tagline: WWII Battleground and Pacific Paradise – Coral Reefs and Kastom Culture 🇸🇧

Capital City 🏛️.text: Honiara is the capital on Guadalcanal, the island that was the site of one of WWII's most brutal battles.
The Solomon Islands is an archipelago of 992 islands in the Pacific Ocean.
The Battle of Guadalcanal (1942–43) was one of the turning points of WWII in the Pacific.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Guadalcanal WWII Sites – Iron Bottom Sound is littered with sunken ships and planes.
Marovo Lagoon – The world's largest saltwater lagoon, UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
Skull Island – A traditional skull shrine from headhunting days in the Malaita lagoon.
Mount Popomanaseu – The highest peak in the Solomons (2,335m).

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Timber – Tropical hardwood logging is a major but unsustainable industry.
Fisheries – Tuna fishing in Pacific waters.
Agriculture – Palm oil and cocoa.
Tourism – Diving among WWII wrecks and pristine coral reefs.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Solomon Islands Pijin (Creole) is the lingua franca; over 70 indigenous languages are spoken.
95+ ethnic groups; Melanesian islanders are the majority.
Traditional 'Kastom' (custom) practices including shell money, chiefs' governance, and traditional dances are central to life.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Solomon Islands covers 28,896 sq km of land across 992 islands in the Pacific.
Located northeast of Australia; neighboured by PNG and Vanuatu.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Iron Bottom Sound near Guadalcanal has over 50 sunken WWII ships and planes – a world-class wreck diving site.
John F. Kennedy's PT-109 torpedo boat was sunk in the Solomon Islands; he swam to shore carrying an injured crewman.
Marovo Lagoon is the world's largest saltwater lagoon, covering over 700 sq km of clear water.

Vanuatu.tagline: Happy Island – Kastom, Active Volcanoes, and Bungee Jumping Origins 🇻🇺

Capital City 🏛️.text: Port Vila on Efate Island is Vanuatu's capital.
Vanuatu consistently ranks as one of the world's happiest countries.
The bungee jump is thought to originate from Vanuatu's Pentecost Island 'land diving' ritual.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mount Yasur – One of the world's most accessible active volcanoes; you can walk to the crater rim.
Pentecost Island Land Diving – Men dive from 30m towers with only a vine on their ankles – the origin of bungee jumping.
Blue Holes, Espiritu Santo – Crystal-clear freshwater sinkholes for swimming and diving.
Million Dollar Point – Where the US Army dumped WWII equipment into the sea; now a dive site.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Volcano tourism, diving, and cultural experiences.
Offshore Finance – A major Pacific offshore financial centre.
Agriculture – Copra, cocoa, coffee, and beef.
Kava – Vanuatu's traditional kava drink culture is central to society and an export.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Bislama (Creole), English, and French are all official languages.
Vanuatu has 110+ languages for a population of 330,000 – one of the world's highest language density.
Kastom (custom) practices are legally protected and honoured alongside modern governance.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Vanuatu covers 12,189 sq km across 80+ islands in the Pacific.
Located in the Pacific Ocean east of Australia and northeast of New Caledonia.
Sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire with active volcanoes.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Bungee jumping was inspired by Vanuatu's Pentecost Island 'land diving' – where boys jump from 30m towers with vines on their ankles as a rite of passage!
Vanuatu has one of the world's highest language densities – 110 languages for 330,000 people!
Vanuatu consistently ranks as the 'Happiest Country on Earth' in international surveys.
Mount Yasur has been erupting continuously for 800 years – one of the world's most reliable volcanoes.

Samoa.tagline: Treasure Islands of the Pacific – Faasamoa Culture, Pristine Beaches, and Polynesian Roots 🇼🇸

Capital City 🏛️.text: Apia is Samoa's capital on the main island of Upolu.
Samoa (formerly Western Samoa) was the first Pacific nation to gain independence (1962).
Samoa is in Polynesia and considered one of the spiritual homelands of Polynesian culture.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: To Sua Ocean Trench – A dramatic swimming hole connected to the sea by an underwater tunnel.
Robert Louis Stevenson Museum (Vailima) – The home and tomb of the Scottish author of Treasure Island.
Palolo Deep Marine Reserve – Samoa's only marine reserve; spectacular coral and fish.
Papase'ea Sliding Rocks – Natural rock slides into a freshwater pool.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Remittances – Samoans working abroad (especially in New Zealand and USA) send vital funds.
Agriculture – Cocoa, coconuts, and taro.
Tourism – Beaches and Polynesian culture.
Fishing – Pacific tuna fishing.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Samoan and English are official languages.
Fa'a Samoa (the Samoan way) – a system of community, tradition, and respect for elders – governs daily life.
Traditional Samoan tattoo (pe'a) is one of the most significant traditional tattoo cultures in the world.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Samoa covers 2,842 sq km of two main islands (Upolu and Savai'i) and eight smaller islands.
Located in the central South Pacific Ocean.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Robert Louis Stevenson (Treasure Island, Kidnapped) spent his last years in Samoa and is buried there.
Samoa switched sides of the International Date Line in 2011 to align with Australia and New Zealand, skipping an entire day!
Traditional Samoan pe'a tattoo (covering the body from waist to knee) takes weeks of painful sessions to complete.

Tonga.tagline: Friendly Islands – Pacific Kingdom, Flying Foxes, and the First to Greet the New Year 🇹🇴

Capital City 🏛️.text: Nuku'alofa on Tongatapu is Tonga's capital.
Tonga is the only monarchy in the Pacific and was never formally colonised.
Tonga is the world's first country to see the New Year each January 1st.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Ha'amonga 'a Maui Trilithon – A massive stone arch gateway from the 13th century, Tonga's Stonehenge.
'Eua Island – Tonga's oldest island with dramatic cliffs, caves, and rare birds.
Anahulu Cave – A network of limestone caves with eels and bats.
Humpback Whale Breeding Grounds – Tonga's Ha'apai Group is one of the world's best places to swim with humpbacks.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Remittances – Tongans abroad (especially in NZ, Australia, USA) send over 30% of GDP.
Agriculture – Squash, vanilla, coconuts, and root crops.
Fisheries – Tuna fishing in the Pacific.
Tourism – Whale swimming and beach tourism.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Tongan and English are official languages.
Tongan culture values hierarchy, ceremony, and community; the monarchy is deeply respected.
Tonga has the world's highest obesity rate – a social and health challenge.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Tonga covers 748 sq km across 170 islands in the Pacific.
Located south of Samoa in the South Pacific.
Sits on the Tonga Trench, one of the world's deepest ocean trenches.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Tonga is the world's first country to welcome the New Year every January 1st!
Tonga is the only Pacific island nation never to have been colonised.
The Hunga Tonga volcanic eruption in 2022 was the most powerful explosion on Earth in a century – heard 10,000 km away!
Tonga's humpback whale watching is considered some of the best in the world – you can swim alongside them!

Nauru.tagline: World's Smallest Island Nation – Phosphate Boom, Bust, and Pacific Solitude 🇳🇷

Capital City 🏛️.text: Yaren is Nauru's de facto capital; Nauru technically has no official capital.
Nauru is the world's smallest island nation and the third smallest country overall.
Nauru was once one of the world's wealthiest countries per capita thanks to phosphate mining.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Buada Lagoon – A freshwater lake in the island's centre, home to fish and birds.
Command Ridge – The highest point on Nauru (71m) with WWII Japanese fortifications.
Phosphate Mines – The moonscape of exhausted phosphate mines covers 80% of the island.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Phosphate – Nearly exhausted but historically the entire economy.
Offshore Finance – A Pacific banking centre.
Fishing Rights – License fees from foreign fishing fleets.
Regional Processing Centre (Australia) – Nauru receives Australian aid in exchange for hosting asylum seekers.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Nauruan and English are official languages.
Nauruans are a Micronesian people with a strong communal culture.
Nauru's phosphate wealth (1970s) made it briefly the richest per capita country on Earth – then the money ran out.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Nauru covers just 21 sq km – the world's smallest island nation.
A raised coral atoll in the central Pacific Ocean.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Nauru was briefly (1970s) the richest country per capita in the world due to phosphate – then the mines ran out.
Nauru is the world's smallest republic, the smallest island country, and the smallest country with no official capital.
Nauru has one of the world's highest obesity rates – a result of post-mining reliance on processed imported food.

Kiribati.tagline: Straddling the Equator – The First to See Tomorrow and Sinking into the Sea 🇰🇮

Capital City 🏛️.text: South Tarawa (capital region of Tarawa Atoll) is Kiribati's capital.
Kiribati (pronounced 'Kiribas') is the only country in the world that falls in all four hemispheres.
Kiribati is the first country expected to become uninhabitable due to rising sea levels.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Tarawa Atoll – Site of one of WWII's bloodiest battles; US Marines fought Japanese forces in 1943.
Phoenix Islands Protected Area – UNESCO World Heritage; one of the world's largest marine protected areas.
Christmas Island (Kiritimati) – The world's largest coral atoll by land area.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Fishing Rights – The main income; foreign fishing fleets pay for access to the vast Pacific EEZ.
Copra – Dried coconut production.
Remittances – I-Kiribati workers abroad.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: English and Gilbertese (I-Kiribati) are official languages.
Kiribati people face an existential crisis as their islands sink below the rising Pacific.
Kiribati has purchased land in Fiji as a potential future home for climate refugees.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Kiribati covers 811 sq km across 33 atolls scattered over 3.5 million sq km of Pacific Ocean.
Straddles the equator and the International Date Line.
The highest point is just 3 metres above sea level.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Kiribati is pronounced 'Kiribas' – the 'ti' sounds like 's' in the Gilbertese language!
Kiribati is the only country in all four hemispheres simultaneously – north, south, east, and west!
Kiribati may be the first country to disappear due to climate change – its highest point is only 3m above sea level.
Kiribati purchased land in Fiji as a possible future refuge for its 120,000 citizens if the islands flood.

Tuvalu.tagline: Nine Atolls – The World's Most Vulnerable Nation Against Rising Seas 🇹🇻

Capital City 🏛️.text: Funafuti is Tuvalu's capital and main atoll.
Tuvalu is the world's fourth smallest country by area.
Tuvalu may become uninhabitable in 50-100 years due to sea level rise from climate change.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Funafuti Marine Conservation Area – A pristine lagoon ecosystem with sea turtles and reef fish.
WWII Relics, Funafuti – Rusting WWII American equipment left on the islands.
Funafuti Atoll – A series of tiny islands surrounding a stunning lagoon.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: '.tv' Domain – Tuvalu licenses its '.tv' internet domain for $5 million+ per year – a major income source!
Fishing Licenses – Foreign fishing fleets pay to access the Pacific EEZ.
Remittances – Tuvaluans working in New Zealand and Australia.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Tuvaluan and English are official languages.
Tuvaluans are Polynesian; a deeply community-oriented island culture.
Tuvalu has signed a unique 'Falepili Union' with Australia guaranteeing Tuvaluans the right to live in Australia.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Tuvalu covers just 26 sq km across 9 atolls in the central Pacific.
The highest point is only 4.6 metres above sea level.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Tuvalu earns millions by licensing its '.tv' internet domain – used by television companies worldwide!
Tuvalu is the world's least visited country by tourists – only a few hundred per year.
Tuvalu is making a digital 'Digital Nation' backup in the metaverse to preserve its culture even if the islands flood.
Australia has agreed to give Tuvaluans the right to move to Australia as climate change raises seas.

Palau.tagline: Pristine Pacific – Jellyfish Lake, WWII Wrecks, and Conservation Paradise 🇵🇼

Capital City 🏛️.text: Ngerulmud is Palau's capital, one of the world's least known capital cities.
Koror is the largest city and main commercial centre.
Palau became the world's first country to ban reef-toxic sunscreen in 2020 to protect its reefs.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Jellyfish Lake – A lake containing millions of golden jellyfish that have lost their sting; swimming among them is surreal.
Rock Islands Southern Lagoon – UNESCO World Heritage; dramatic limestone islands with pristine coral reefs.
Blue Corner Wall – Considered one of the world's top 5 dive sites.
WWII Wreck Diving – Dozens of Japanese ships and planes sunk in Palau's lagoon.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Tourism – Scuba diving, Jellyfish Lake, and Rock Islands.
Fishing – Pacific tuna access fees.
US Compact – Palau receives US defence and financial support.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Palauan and English are official languages.
