Palauans are Micronesian-Malay; traditional matrilineal clans govern community life.
Palau created the world's first 'shark sanctuary' in 2009 – all fishing of sharks is banned.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Palau covers 459 sq km across 340 islands in the western Pacific.
Located north of Indonesia and east of the Philippines.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Jellyfish Lake has over 8 million golden jellyfish with no sting – you can swim through them!
Palau was the world's first shark sanctuary (2009) and first to ban reef-toxic sunscreen (2020).
Palau's Rock Islands are some of the world's most beautiful – uninhabited limestone mushroom islands in turquoise water.
Palau's reefs are considered the most pristine in the western Pacific.

McMurdo Station.tagline: Gateway to the Ice – America's Largest Antarctic Research Hub 🧊

Capital City 🏛️.text: McMurdo Station is the United States' main Antarctic research base, operated by the National Science Foundation.
Located on the southern tip of Ross Island, near the active Mount Erebus volcano.
It can house up to 1,200 people in summer and is the largest community in Antarctica.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Mount Erebus – The southernmost active volcano on Earth, with a lava lake inside its crater.
Observation Hill – Where Scott's expedition cross stands in memorial to the ill-fated Terra Nova expedition.
Discovery Hut – Built by Robert Falcon Scott's 1901 expedition, still preserved on the ice.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: Scientific Research – Climate change, glaciology, marine biology, and astronomy are major research areas.
Ice Core Drilling – Scientists drill deep into the ice to read 800,000 years of Earth's climate history.
Astronomy – Antarctica's dry, cold, high-altitude atmosphere makes it one of the best places on Earth for telescopes.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Antarctica has no native human population – only rotating scientific crews from dozens of countries.
English is the most common working language but scientists from over 50 nations work here.
The Antarctic Treaty (1959) dedicates the continent to peaceful science, signed by 54 countries.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Antarctica is the 5th largest continent, covering 14 million sq km – bigger than Europe.
It holds 90% of the world's ice and 70% of the world's fresh water in frozen form.
The coldest recorded temperature on Earth was -89.2°C at Vostok Station, Antarctica.
Winds can reach 320 km/h – the strongest winds on the planet.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: Antarctica has no time zone – scientists use the time zone of their home country or the nearest supply base.
The ice sheet covering Antarctica is up to 4.8 km thick in places.
Antarctica is technically a desert – it receives less precipitation than the Sahara!
Penguins and seals are the most common wildlife; no land predators exist here.

Bharati Station.tagline: India's Eye on the Ice – Science at the Bottom of the World 🇮🇳🧊

Capital City 🏛️.text: Bharati is India's third Antarctic research station, inaugurated in 2012 on the Larsemann Hills, East Antarctica.
India also operates Maitri Station (1989) and the historical Dakshin Gangotri (1983).
Bharati can house up to 47 scientists and support staff year-round.

National Importance & Famous Landmarks 🏔.text: Larsemann Hills – Ice-free rocky hills on Prydz Bay where Bharati is located.
Prydz Bay – Rich marine ecosystem studied by Indian oceanographers.
Polar Plateau access – Used for deep ice core drilling and climate science.

Core Production & Economic Focus 🏭.text: India's Antarctic Programme – Run by the National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR).
Climate Science – Studying how the Southern Ocean affects monsoon patterns in India.
Geological Studies – Researching ancient rocks that connect Antarctica to the Indian subcontinent.

Native People & Languages 🗣️.text: Scientists and support staff are from India, speaking Hindi and English.
India has been sending annual expeditions to Antarctica since 1981.
Station life involves strict routines, teamwork, and surviving extreme polar conditions.

Area & Geography 🌍.text: Located at 69.4°S latitude on the Princess Astrid Coast of East Antarctica.
Nearby Prydz Bay is one of the most biologically productive seas in Antarctica.
Extreme cold, blizzards, and 24-hour darkness in winter test the resilience of researchers.

Unique Facts 🌟.text: India is one of only a few developing nations to maintain a year-round Antarctic presence.
Scientists at Bharati study connections between Antarctic ice melt and Indian monsoon rainfall.
The station was built using a modular design – all parts were pre-assembled in Germany and shipped to Antarctica.
Living in Antarctica means no weekends, no shops, and no escaping your colleagues for months!

National Animal 🐾.text: Emperor Penguin (Aptenodytes forsteri) – most commonly sighted wildlife
